Fact.Name: Has a casualty or theft event to report on Form 4684 (a loss, or a reimbursement that exceeds basis)
Fact.Description:
Whether the return reports one or more casualty or theft losses on Form 4684. Gate for the casualty intake; when true the /casualtyEvents collection carries one item per casualty or theft event. This covers BOTH sections: Section A (personal-use property) and Section B column (b)(i) (trade, business, rental or royalty property), which each event picks between via /casualtyEvents/*/writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing.
THE QUESTION IS WIDENED AND THE PATH IS NOT: this is the INTAKE half of the arm named on the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain, and the RETIREMENT half is still owed there. Form 4684 is the form for BOTH a loss and a GAIN (line 4 "Gain from casualty or theft. If line 3 is more than line 2, enter the difference here", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 1, on the same page as the loss lines; IRC 165(h)(3)(A) defines the personal casualty gain on the same property class as the loss, 26 U.S.C. 165, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section165&num=0&edition=2024), so the question the application asks on this writable reads as "a casualty or theft event" - property damaged, destroyed or stolen, whether the insurance or other reimbursement was less than the loss (a loss) OR more than the property's basis (a gain). A filer with a gain and no loss who answers yes has the event enter the collection, ../hasCasualtyGain resolves true, and /knockoutCasualtyGain REFUSES the return - the safe direction, and strictly better than the silent omission a NO answer produces. Nothing in this dictionary COMPELS the widening: it is a Name and Description change with no asked-when in the tree; the widening lands when the application lands the row. NO WRITABLE IS ADDED AND NO VALUE MOVES: every committed fixture answered this question yes for a loss and still does.
THE PATH KEEPS ITS NAME: /hasCasualtyLoss is read by /claimsCasualtyLoss alone, and through that gate by the guard's own When, by 26 other facts of this module and by the flow (which carries the guard, flow.xml); renaming it would be a churn with no tax effect. Widening this intake while the guard's own When keys on it is NOT the same as retiring the guard: the RETIREMENT cannot happen without the widening (else the gain-only filer is omitted the moment the guard stops refusing), but the widening CAN happen without the retirement, and it turns an omission into a refusal. The retirement itself is still owed on the contract.

Fact.Name: Claims a casualty or theft loss (Form 4684 Section A or Section B)
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe gate: true only when /hasCasualtyLoss is answered and true (the IsComplete pattern, as /claimsItemizedDeductions). Unanswered resolves Complete false so every return without a casualty loss still resolves and keeps the aggregates Complete-0 - the ~all existing scenarios that never populate /casualtyEvents stay byte-identical.
THE NAME IS NARROWER THAN THE QUESTION IT READS: /hasCasualtyLoss covers a casualty or theft EVENT whether it produced a loss or a gain (the intake half of an arm of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain), so "claims a casualty loss" here means "reports a Form 4684 event". Nothing in this fact's body changes and no value moves; the path is kept because the guard's own When, the flow and every Section A and Section B total read it.

Fact.Name: Casualty and theft events
Fact.Description: The collection of casualty or theft events reported on Form 4684 - one item per event (one Form 4684, lines 1-12 for a Section A event or lines 19-28 for a Section B one, per casualty or theft). Each item holds the per-event inputs (basis, FMV before/after, reimbursement, the federally-declared- disaster attestation, and the Section A / Section B fork ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing) and the per-event loss chain for whichever section the fork selects. An item may instead be a SECTION C event (../writableIsPonziSafeHarborTheft): a Ponzi-type theft loss figured under the Rev. Proc. 2009-20 safe harbor, whose lines 40-51 replace the lines 19-27 chain and whose output re-enters at line 28. Section C is per-ARRANGEMENT rather than per-property, so the one-property-per-event simplification below does not bite it at all. SIMPLIFICATION: the form's four per-event property columns (A-D) are collapsed to a single property per event; a multi-item event is entered as separate events (each keeps its own 100-dollar floor, a conservative difference only when one physical event damages several properties - and no difference at all for a Section B event, which has no per-event floor to duplicate). Section B lays out the same four columns under the same one-part-per-event rule ("Use a separate Part l for each casualty or theft", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2), so the collapse and its consequence are identical on both arms.

Fact.Name: Casualty event description (stable identity)
Fact.Description: A human-referenceable label for this casualty or theft event (Form 4684 line 1 "Description of properties"). Plays no part in any computation; a faithful-record field. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered leaves the event unlabeled and changes no tax value.

Fact.Name: Loss attributable to a federally declared disaster (eligibility attestation)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section A eligibility gate: whether this event's loss is attributable to a FEDERALLY DECLARED DISASTER (a Presidential major-disaster or emergency declaration under the Stafford Act, identified by a FEMA DR- or EM- number). For tax years beginning after 2017, a personal-use casualty or theft loss is deductible ONLY if this is true (IRC 165(h); 2025 i4684 "Limitation on personal casualty and theft losses"). The taxpayer attests the FEMA declaration; the engine gates on the attestation, it does not validate the declaration number. An event answered FALSE (or left unanswered) is NOT deducted here - its loss can only offset casualty gains (not modelled), so it contributes 0.

Fact.Name: Loss is a qualified disaster loss (increased-standard-deduction attestation)
Fact.Description: Whether this event's loss is a QUALIFIED DISASTER LOSS - a casualty or theft loss of personal-use property attributable to a qualified disaster (a specific federally-declared major-disaster category with a defined incident-period window; 2025 i4684 "Qualified disaster loss" enumerates the covered disasters and incident-period bounds through July 4, 2025). A qualified disaster loss follows the OBBBA / section 165(h)(5) special rules: the per-event floor is 500 dollars (not 100), the 10%-of-AGI reduction does NOT apply, and the net loss INCREASES the standard deduction (so it is deductible WITHOUT itemizing - 2025 i4684 "You can deduct qualified disaster losses without itemizing"). The taxpayer ATTESTS the qualified- disaster status; the engine gates on the attestation, it does not validate the FEMA declaration or the incident-period window. A qualified disaster loss is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with the ordinary Schedule A casualty path (U-066a): an event attested TRUE here is EXCLUDED from ../deductibleLossAfterFloor (the Schedule A line-15 aggregate) so the same loss is never deducted twice. Left unanswered (or FALSE) means not a qualified disaster loss - no increased standard deduction (the conservative, higher-tax direction).

Fact.Name: Adjusted basis of the property (Form 4684 line 2)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 2: the cost or other adjusted basis of the property for this event. Bounds the loss (line 8 takes the smaller of basis or the FMV decline).

Fact.Name: Fair market value before the casualty or theft (Form 4684 line 5)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 5: the fair market value of the property immediately BEFORE the casualty or theft.

Fact.Name: Fair market value after the casualty or theft (Form 4684 line 6)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 6: the fair market value of the property immediately AFTER the casualty or theft (0 for property stolen or totally destroyed). HELP TEXT, A HOME TORN DOWN OR MOVED BY ORDER (IRC 165(k)): if the home was in a disaster area and a state or local government ordered it torn down or moved because the disaster made it unsafe to use as a home, enter here the home's value BEFORE it was torn down or moved, not the value after (which may be zero). Entering the post-demolition value overstates the loss. The order must have been issued within 120 days after the area was declared a disaster area; the graph holds no date to test that, so the filer attests it.

Fact.Name: Did you determine your decrease in fair market value using an IRS safe harbor method under Revenue Procedure 2018-08?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Did you determine your decrease in fair market value using an IRS safe harbor method under Revenue Procedure 2018-08?" Shown once per Section A event, before the fair-market-value lines.
HELP TEXT: Rev. Proc. 2018-08 (2018-2 I.R.B. 286) provides safe harbor methods for determining the amount of a casualty or theft loss to a home and personal belongings; the 2025 Instructions for Form 4684 point filers to it by name: "Safe harbor methods for determining casualty and theft losses. See Revenue Procedure 2018-08 ... for safe harbor methods that you may use in determining the amount of your casualty and theft losses for your home and personal belongings" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 8). The reporting instruction that makes this a DIRECT-ENTRY line rather than a computed one: "When completing Form 4684, do not enter an amount on line 5 or line 6 for each property. Instead, enter the decrease in the FMV determined in the relevant safe harbor method on line 7" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 8). A filer using one of these methods must also attach a statement naming the specific method used - a print-only obligation this dictionary does not model (no such statement fact exists anywhere in this module).
ASKED-WHEN: every Section A event, ahead of ../fmvBefore and ../fmvAfter.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: FALSE (no safe harbor method used) - lines 5/6 remain the computation path, which is today's exact behavior on every existing return, since this writable is new.
VALIDATION: Boolean, no further constraint.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../usedFmvSafeHarborMethod (the complete-safe restatement) gates ../fmvDecrease's direct-entry Case, ahead of the ordinary line-5-minus-line-6 arithmetic. When TRUE, ../fmvBefore and ../fmvAfter are not read for this event's line 7 - matching the instruction's "do not enter an amount on line 5 or line 6" - though this dictionary does not suppress those two writables' own screens; the print-line correctness is what this fact governs.

Fact.Name: Event used a Rev. Proc. 2018-08 FMV safe harbor method (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableUsedFmvSafeHarborMethod when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Read only by ../fmvDecrease, ahead of its ordinary line-5-minus-line-6 arm.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Enter the decrease in fair market value determined under the Revenue Procedure 2018-08 safe harbor method
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Enter the decrease in fair market value determined under the safe harbor method (Form 4684 line 7)." Shown only when ../writableUsedFmvSafeHarborMethod is TRUE, replacing the ../fmvBefore / ../fmvAfter pair for this event.
HELP TEXT: same Rev. Proc. 2018-08 reporting instruction as the attestation above - "enter the decrease in the FMV determined in the relevant safe harbor method on line 7" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 8). The filer supplies the FIGURE the safe harbor method (not modeled here - the method's own worksheets and tables live entirely inside Rev. Proc. 2018-08) produces; this dictionary does not recompute it.
ASKED-WHEN: ../writableUsedFmvSafeHarborMethod is TRUE.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: 0 - the conservative, HIGHER-tax direction (an attested-but-unentered safe harbor amount yields no loss rather than an invented one).
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../fmvDecreaseFromSafeHarborMethod (the complete-safe restatement) is ../fmvDecrease's direct-entry value when the attestation is true.

Fact.Name: The Rev. Proc. 2018-08 safe harbor FMV decrease amount, if used (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableFmvDecreaseFromSafeHarborMethod when ../usedFmvSafeHarborMethod is true AND the writable is answered; else $0 (the IsComplete pattern plus the same coherence gate ../fmvDecreaseFromSafeHarborMethod's sibling writables use elsewhere in this module - an orphan amount with no attested safe harbor use cannot move a dollar). Read only by ../fmvDecrease.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Are you using the Revenue Procedure 2010-36 special procedure for corrosive drywall damage?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Are you using the Revenue Procedure 2010-36 special procedure for corrosive drywall damage?" Shown once per Section A event.
HELP TEXT: Pub. 547's special procedure for imported corrosive drywall installed between 2001 and 2009: "you can deduct the amounts you paid to repair damage to your home and household appliances due to corrosive drywall. Under this procedure, you treat the amounts paid for repairs as a casualty loss in the year of payment" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 5). The special reporting instructions replace the ordinary basis/FMV computation ENTIRELY, not just line 7: "Line 2. Skip this line. ... Lines 4-7. Skip these lines. Line 8. Enter the amount you paid to repair the damage to your home and household appliances due to corrosive drywall" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 6) - the figure lands on FORM 4684 LINE 8 (../lossBeforeReimbursement), not line 7 (../fmvDecrease), which is why this procedure is a SEPARATE intake from the Rev. Proc. 2018-08 safe harbor above rather than sharing its shape: the two procedures replace different lines. CAUTION, carried here for the filer's benefit though not separately gated: "Because the personal casualty losses claimed under this special procedure aren't attributable to a federally declared disaster, they're only deductible to the extent such losses don't exceed your personal casualty gains" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 5) - already enforced by this module's existing ../isEligible / ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor machinery PROVIDED the filer answers ../federallyDeclaredDisaster consistently (false, for a drywall-only event); this fact does not force that consistency, the same reliance-on-consistent-attestation posture every other attestation pair in this module carries.
ASKED-WHEN: every Section A event, alongside the other loss-measurement questions.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: FALSE - the ordinary basis/FMV computation stays the path, which is today's exact behavior on every existing return, since this writable is new.
VALIDATION: Boolean, no further constraint.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../usedCorrosiveDrywallProcedure (the complete-safe restatement) gates ../lossBeforeReimbursement's direct-entry Case, ahead of the ordinary LesserOf(../adjustedBasis, ../fmvDecrease) arithmetic. When TRUE, ../adjustedBasis, ../fmvBefore and ../fmvAfter are not read for this event's line 8.

Fact.Name: Event used the Rev. Proc. 2010-36 corrosive drywall special procedure (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableUsedCorrosiveDrywallProcedure when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Read only by ../lossBeforeReimbursement, ahead of its ordinary LesserOf(basis, FMV decrease) arm.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Enter the amount you paid to repair the damage to your home and household appliances due to corrosive drywall
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Enter the amount you paid to repair the damage to your home and household appliances due to corrosive drywall (Form 4684 line 8)." Shown only when ../writableUsedCorrosiveDrywallProcedure is TRUE.
HELP TEXT: Pub. 547's special instruction: "Enter the amount you paid to repair the damage to your home and household appliances due to corrosive drywall. Enter only the amounts you paid to restore your home to the condition existing immediately before the damage. Don't enter any amounts you paid for improvements or additions that increased the value of your home above its pre-loss value" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 6).
ASKED-WHEN: ../writableUsedCorrosiveDrywallProcedure is TRUE.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: 0 - the conservative, HIGHER-tax direction.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../corrosiveDrywallRepairCost (the complete-safe restatement) is ../lossBeforeReimbursement's direct-entry value when the attestation is true.

Fact.Name: The Rev. Proc. 2010-36 corrosive drywall repair-cost amount, if used (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableCorrosiveDrywallRepairCost when ../usedCorrosiveDrywallProcedure is true AND the writable is answered; else $0 (the IsComplete pattern plus the coherence gate - an orphan amount with no attested drywall-procedure use cannot move a dollar). Read only by ../lossBeforeReimbursement.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Insurance or other reimbursement (Form 4684 line 3)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 3: insurance or other reimbursement received or reasonably expected for this event (whether or not a claim was filed). Reduces the loss (line 9). OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means no reimbursement, resolved to 0 by ../reimbursementAmount so an event with no insurance need not answer it. THE PARENTHESIS "(whether or not a claim was filed)" ABOVE IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE STATUTE. IRC 165(h)(4)(E): "Any loss of an individual described in subsection (c)(3) to the extent covered by insurance shall be taken into account under this section only if the individual files a timely insurance claim with respect to such loss" (26 U.S.C. 165, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section165&num=0&edition=2024). The printed line 3 is captioned "Insurance or other reimbursement (whether or not you filed a claim)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 1), and the instructions spell the consequence out: "If you don't file a timely insurance claim, you can't deduct the full unrecovered amount as a casualty or theft loss and only the part of the loss that isn't covered by your insurance policy is deductible" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 3, LEFT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction). The line 3 instruction itself says it in as many words: "Include your insurance coverage whether or not you are filing a claim for reimbursement. For example, your car worth $2,000 is totally destroyed in a flood in an area designated as a federal disaster. You are insured with a $500 deductible, but decide not to report it to your insurance company because you are afraid the insurance company will cancel your policy. In this case, enter $1,500 on this line." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 7, RIGHT column of the same TWO-COLUMN extraction). On that printed example line 3 is the 1,500 COVERAGE with 0 received, and line 9 is 500. So this writable is the amount the policy COVERS, and ../lossAfterReimbursement subtracting it from line 8 is exactly "taken into account only to the extent not covered". This writable is REQUIRED whenever ../writableDeclinedToFileReimbursementClaim is true. HELP TEXT, INSURANCE FOR LIVING EXPENSES: do not include insurance paid to cover your living expenses when you lost the use of your main home, or were denied access to it by government authorities, because of the casualty or a threat of one. Those payments do not reduce the casualty loss (Pub. 547, Insurance payments for living expenses). If they exceed the temporary increase in your living expenses and the casualty was NOT in a federally declared disaster area, the excess is other income on Schedule 1 line 8z, which this graph does not compute (finding FED-4684-LIVING-EXPENSE-PAYMENTS-052, open).

Fact.Name: Property was used in a trade, business, rental or royalty activity (Form 4684 Section B, column (b)(i))
Fact.Description: THE SECTION A / SECTION B FORK. TRUE when this event's property was TRADE, BUSINESS, RENTAL OR ROYALTY property - Form 4684 Section B Part II column (b)(i), "Trade, business, rental, or royalty property" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2). The whole computation forks here: a true event skips Section A entirely (no federally- declared-disaster gate, no $100 per-event floor, no 10%-of-AGI floor - "Losses on business property and income-producing property aren't subject to these rules", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 15) and its loss leaves on Form 4684 lines 31 and 38a to Form 4797 line 14, not on Schedule A line 15. NOT COVERED BY THIS ATTESTATION, stated here because the path name is broader than the column: Section B's OTHER loss column, (b)(ii) "Income-producing property" (investment property held for the production of income), leaves the form by a DIFFERENT door - lines 32 and 38b, "Individuals, enter the amount from income-producing property on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2). That column is ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty; answer THAT one, not this one, for income-producing property. Routing a (b)(ii) loss down this arm instead would put it on Schedule 1 line 4 (above the line, no itemizing needed), which is the taxpayer- FAVOURABLE error - so the two attestations are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE and, if both are answered true, the (b)(ii) one wins (see ../sectionBLossColumnBi). OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means personal-use property, which is today's behaviour for every existing return exactly - see ../isBusinessOrIncomeProducing.

Fact.Name: This Section B loss is from a fraudulent investment arrangement reported without Section C
Fact.Description: QUESTION: "Is this business or income-producing loss a theft loss from a fraudulent investment arrangement (for example a Ponzi-type scheme) that you are reporting on Section B rather than through the Section C safe harbor?" This attestation identifies the Form 4684 line 19 population whose instructions require the name of the individual or entity that conducted the arrangement: "If you are claiming a loss from a fraudulent investment arrangement and you are not filling out Section C". A financial scam that was not an investment arrangement (i4684 Losses From Financial Scams) is answered FALSE: the line 19 identity rule does not reach it. Asked only after the event is classified as Section B; unanswered means no identity requirement and changes no dollar computation. The name, and the identification number and address the instruction asks for if known, are line 19 entries: ../writableSectionBFinancialScamPerpetratorName, ../writableSectionBFinancialScamPerpetratorTin and ../writableSectionBFinancialScamPerpetratorAddress.

Fact.Name: Name of the financial-scam perpetrator (Form 4684 Section B line 19)
Fact.Description: The name the filer enters for the individual or entity that conducted the fraudulent investment arrangement reported in this Section B event. Form 4684 line 19 identity is required for such a theft loss reported without Section C. The taxpayer identification number and address the same sentence asks for carry "if known" and are collected optionally at ../writableSectionBFinancialScamPerpetratorTin and ../writableSectionBFinancialScamPerpetratorAddress. Required when ../writableSectionBFinancialScam is true; otherwise optional and blank.

Fact.Name: Taxpayer identification number of the financial-scam perpetrator, if known (Form 4684 Section B line 19)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer identification number of the individual or entity that conducted the fraudulent investment arrangement reported in this Section B event, entered on line 19 when the filer knows it. A String rather than a TIN or EIN because the conductor may be an individual (SSN or ITIN) or an entity (EIN), and a blank is allowed. A record field that no computation reads. OPTIONAL: asked when ../writableSectionBFinancialScam is true; unanswered leaves it blank, changes no tax value and never refuses the return.

Fact.Name: Address of the financial-scam perpetrator, if known (Form 4684 Section B line 19)
Fact.Description: The address of the individual or entity that conducted the fraudulent investment arrangement reported in this Section B event, entered on line 19 when the filer knows it. A record field that no computation reads. OPTIONAL: asked when ../writableSectionBFinancialScam is true; unanswered leaves it blank, changes no tax value and never refuses the return.

Fact.Name: Property was held for the production of income, and was not property used as an employee (Form 4684 Section B, column (b)(ii))
Fact.Description: THE SECOND SECTION B COLUMN. TRUE when this event's property was INCOME-PRODUCING property - Form 4684 Section B Part II column (b)(ii), "Income-producing property" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2): investment property held for the production of income rather than used in a trade, business, rental or royalty activity. Like ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing this skips Section A entirely - no federally- declared-disaster gate, no $100 per-event floor, no 10%-of-AGI floor, because "Losses on business property and income-producing property aren't subject to these rules" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 15) names BOTH kinds of property. THE COLUMNS DIFFER ONLY IN WHERE THE LOSS LEAVES THE FORM. Column (b)(i) goes to lines 31 and 38a, "enter this amount on Form 4797, line 14"; column (b)(ii) goes to lines 32 and 38b, "Individuals, enter the amount from income-producing property on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2). So a TRUE answer here routes the loss to Schedule A line 16 - an ITEMIZED deduction that is lost entirely if the filer does not itemize - and never to Form 4797 line 14 / Schedule 1 line 4, which would be above the line and taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. THE EMPLOYEE CARVE-OUT IS FOLDED INTO THIS ATTESTATION rather than modeled separately, and the Name says so. Lines 32 and 38b both end "(Do not include any loss on property used as an employee.)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2), and the 2025 Schedule A instructions' line-16 list - the closed list, "Only the expenses listed next can be deducted on line 16" - names "Casualty and theft losses of income-producing property ... from Form 4684, lines 32 and 38b, or Form 4797, line 18a" and nothing about employee property (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sca.pdf, page 11). A separate writable for the carve-out would have no consumer of its own; the honest alternative is to define this attestation as excluding employee-used property, which is what the Name and this paragraph do. A filer whose property WAS used as an employee therefore answers FALSE and keeps today's Section A treatment - deduction denied absent a federal disaster - which UNDER-states nothing they were entitled to on line 16 anyway. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing: one property sits in one column. If both are answered true THIS ONE WINS - see ../sectionBLossColumnBi. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means not income-producing property, which is today's behaviour for every existing return exactly - see ../isIncomeProducingProperty.

Fact.Name: Was this property used in performing services as an employee?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Was this property used in performing services as an employee (rather than in a trade or business you operate)?" Shown once per event that answered ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing TRUE - a follow-up refinement of that column (b)(i) attestation, not a stand-alone gate.
HELP TEXT: the 2025 Instructions for Form 4684, under "Section B-Business and Income- Producing Property": "Caution: You can no longer claim any miscellaneous itemized deductions. As a result, business casualty and theft losses of property used in performing services as an employee cannot be deducted or applied in the netting process to offset gains" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 10 and lines 723-725). IRC 67(g) is the statutory root: the TCJA suspension of miscellaneous itemized deductions subject to the 2%-of-AGI floor through 2025 reaches unreimbursed employee business expenses, and an employee-use casualty loss was one of those. Column (b)(i) ("Trade, business, rental, or royalty property") carries NO employee test of its own - only column (b)(ii) ("Income-producing property") folds an employee carve-out into its own attestation (../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty). Without this question, property that was actually used in performing services as an employee could be attested TRUE on (b)(i) instead and deducted in full on Form 4797 line 14, an ordinary above-the-line loss the Caution flatly bars.
ASKED-WHEN: every event where ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing is TRUE. Not asked on a (b)(ii) event - that column's own attestation already excludes employee-use property (see ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty's Description).
UNANSWERED POSTURE: FALSE (not employee-use property) - the SAME conservative default every sibling Section B attestation in this module uses (unanswered means today's pre-fill behaviour is unchanged); this is the direction that keeps the loss on the taxpayer-favourable Form 4797 path rather than silently barring it, so an unanswered event is a NAMED completeness gap, not a defect: the correct fix is asking the question, which the application is obliged to do whenever ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing is answered TRUE.
VALIDATION: Boolean, no further constraint.
[APPENDED 2026-09-12, S333: when ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing is answered TRUE, an unanswered employee-use answer no longer silently qualifies the loss. The derived ../sectionBEmployeeUseUnanswered flag makes both Section B loss columns Incomplete until this condition-of-allowance is answered; non-claiming events retain the prior FALSE alias.]
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../usedInPerformingServicesAsEmployee (the complete-safe restatement) is read as a negated conjunct on BOTH ../sectionBLossColumnBi and ../sectionBLossColumnBii, so a TRUE answer here removes the loss from column (b)(i) entirely - Form 4684 lines 29/30/34/35 column (b)(i) and, downstream, /sectionBNetGainOrLoss (Form 4797 line 14) - rather than merely capping it, matching the Caution's "cannot be deducted or applied in the netting process to offset gains": the loss does not move to column (b)(ii) either, even on the contradictory event that also answers ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty TRUE, it is simply barred, the same non-deductible outcome ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty's own employee carve-out already gives a (b)(ii)-only-attested employee-use property.

Fact.Name: This event's property was used in performing services as an employee (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableUsedInPerformingServicesAsEmployee when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern) - the same conservative default the writable's own Description explains. Read as a negated conjunct by both ../sectionBLossColumnBi and ../sectionBLossColumnBii - the employee-use bar excludes the loss from BOTH Section B Part II columns, not only the one the writable is asked on.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: This Section B business-property event has an unanswered employee-use posture
Fact.Description: Complete-safe flag for the posture doctrine: an unanswered condition of allowance is never silently defaulted in the favourable direction. It is true only when the event is claimed as Section B business/trade/rental/royalty property and the required employee-use question is unanswered. Section B column (b)(i) and the column (b)(ii) tie-break must not silently treat an unanswered condition of allowance as FALSE; the loss therefore remains Incomplete until the filer answers the question. Non-claiming and Section-A-only events remain false and retain their existing complete-safe behavior.

Fact.Name: Every claimed Section B business-property event has answered the employee-use question
Fact.Description:
THE RETURN-LEVEL COMPLETENESS MEMBER FOR THE SECTION B EMPLOYEE-USE QUESTION. FALSE when this return claims a casualty loss and at least one event is attested as Section B column (b)(i) trade, business, rental or royalty property while its required employee-use question (../writableUsedInPerformingServicesAsEmployee) is unanswered; TRUE otherwise, including on a return with no casualty collection at all.
WHY THIS AND NOT AN INCOMPLETE DOLLAR. The posture doctrine says an unanswered condition of allowance must not be silently defaulted in the favourable direction. External block 1 first expressed that by making ../sectionBLossColumnBi and ../sectionBLossColumnBii Incomplete on such an event. That is a defensible reading of the doctrine, but the employee-use question's own ASKED-WHEN is "every event where ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing is TRUE", so the fence fired on EVERY Section B business witness in the corpus - 39 committed form4684 cases, 8 form4797 and 2 scheduleD by cascade - and no input distinguishes those witnesses from the case the fence was written for. The dollar columns therefore keep the complete-safe FALSE alias, and the unanswered condition of allowance is enforced where it bites without falsifying an arithmetic line: this fact joins flow:/flowIncomplete's All, so the return cannot be completed - and therefore cannot be filed - until the question is answered. The taxpayer-favourable silent deduction the row was opened against can no longer reach a SUBMITTED return.
Nothing further is owed in the dictionary.

Fact.Name: Was this a home you used for business or rented out (and are NOT filing Schedule C for)?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Was this property a home you used for business or rented out?" Shown once per Section B event (../isBusinessOrIncomeProducing).
HELP TEXT: the 2025 i4684 "Home Used for Business or Rented Out" section: "If you had a casualty or theft loss involving a home you used for business or rented out, your deductible loss may be limited... For a home you rented out or used for a business for which you aren't filing Schedule C (Form 1040), see section 280A(c)(5) to figure your deductible loss. Attach a statement showing your computation of the deductible loss, enter that amount on line 27" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 10). IRC 280A(c)(5): the deduction for business/rental use of a dwelling unit "shall not exceed the excess of (A) the gross income derived from such use for the taxable year, over (B)" other allocable deductions (26 U.S.C. 280A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section280A&num=0&edition=2024).
THE FORM 8829 HALF IS ITS OWN QUESTION. The SAME i4684 paragraph forks on whether the filer files Schedule C: "If the loss involved a home used for a business for which you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040)... figure your deductible casualty or theft loss on Form 8829... Enter on Form 4684, line 27, the deductible loss from Form 8829, line 35" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 10). That half is ../writableHomeUsedForScheduleCBusiness with the join ../writableHomeScheduleC, and when it is YES it governs ../sectionBCasualtyLoss ahead of this attestation. This attestation and its ceiling apply to the other half only (a home rented out, or used for a business the filer does not file Schedule C for).
A SIMPLIFICATION IS MADE, NAMED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT: 280A(c)(5)'s ceiling is gross income LESS subparagraph (B)'s other allocable deductions (mortgage interest, taxes, depreciation etc. already claimed against the same use) - this module asks only for the GROSS INCOME half (../writableGrossIncomeFromBusinessOrRentalUse) and caps against that alone, which is a taxpayer-FAVOURABLE approximation (the true ceiling is never larger than gross income, since subparagraph (B) only subtracts further) rather than a conservative one. This is the DIRECT INTAKE the lead ruled for this unit, in place of a full Form 8829 worksheet.
ASKED-WHEN: every Section B event.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: FALSE - the ordinary Section B loss computation stays uncapped, which is today's exact behavior on every existing return, since this writable is new.
VALIDATION: Boolean, no further constraint.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../homeUsedForBusinessOrRentedOut (the complete-safe restatement) gates a cap on ../sectionBCasualtyLoss's ordinary arm at ../grossIncomeFromBusinessOrRentalUse.

Fact.Name: Event is a home used for business or rented out, subject to the 280A(c)(5) ceiling (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableHomeUsedForBusinessOrRentedOut when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Read only by ../sectionBCasualtyLoss, as the gate on its 280A(c)(5)-ceiling cap.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Enter the gross income derived from the business or rental use of this home for the year
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Enter the gross income derived from the business or rental use of this home for the year (IRC 280A(c)(5))." Shown only when ../writableHomeUsedForBusinessOrRentedOut is TRUE.
HELP TEXT: IRC 280A(c)(5)(A): the deduction ceiling is "the gross income derived from such use for the taxable year" (26 U.S.C. 280A, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section280A&num=0&edition=2024). This module asks for that gross income figure directly and caps the deductible casualty loss at it - the simplification named on the attestation above (this module does not additionally subtract 280A(c)(5)(B)'s other allocable deductions, so the cap is taxpayer-favourable, never smaller than the true statutory ceiling).
ASKED-WHEN: ../writableHomeUsedForBusinessOrRentedOut is TRUE.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: 0 - the conservative, HIGHER-tax direction (an attested-but-unentered ceiling caps the loss at $0 rather than leaving it uncapped).
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../grossIncomeFromBusinessOrRentalUse (the complete-safe restatement) is the ceiling ../sectionBCasualtyLoss's ordinary arm is capped at, LesserOf-style, when the attestation is true.

Fact.Name: The 280A(c)(5) gross-income ceiling amount, if attested (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableGrossIncomeFromBusinessOrRentalUse when ../homeUsedForBusinessOrRentedOut is true AND the writable is answered; else $0 (the IsComplete pattern plus the coherence gate - an orphan amount with no attested home-use cannot cap a dollar it was never meant to reach). Read only by ../sectionBCasualtyLoss.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Was this a home you used for a business you report on Schedule C?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Was this property a home you used for a business you report on Schedule C (Form 1040)?" Asked on every Section B event (../isSectionB), beside ../writableHomeUsedForBusinessOrRentedOut, which asks the other half of the same i4684 fork (a home rented out, or used for a business the filer does not file Schedule C for).
HELP TEXT: the 2025 i4684 "Home Used for Business or Rented Out": "If the loss involved a home used for a business for which you are filing Schedule C (Form 1040), Profit or Loss From Business, figure your deductible casualty or theft loss on Form 8829, Expenses for Business Use of Your Home (if you are using Form 8829). Enter on Form 4684, line 27, the deductible loss from Form 8829, line 35".
WHAT IT FEEDS: a YES makes ../writableHomeScheduleC REQUIRED, and ../sectionBCasualtyLoss (line 27 and line 28) becomes that Schedule C's Form 8829 line 35 (form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line35CasualtyPortion). Until the Schedule C is named, line 28 is Incomplete; the loss never falls through to the uncapped Section B arithmetic. If both this and ../writableHomeUsedForBusinessOrRentedOut are YES, this one governs: its instruction names the specific form that figures the loss.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: no, the ordinary Section B computation, which is the posture every return had before this question existed.

Fact.Name: Event is a home used for a Schedule C business, its loss figured on Form 8829 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableHomeUsedForScheduleCBusiness AND ../isSectionB when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). The Section B conjunct keeps a personal use event, whose loss Section A already takes, out of Form 8829 even if the question was answered on it. Gates the Form 8829 line 35 arm of ../sectionBCasualtyLoss, and is the head of the reverse join form8829:/scheduleCs/*/hasLinkedHomeCasualty evaluates, where its being complete safe keeps the comparison against an unanswered ../writableHomeScheduleC unforced on every event that is not such a home. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT.

Fact.Name: Which Schedule C business used this home?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Which of your businesses used this home?", a choice among the return's Schedule C businesses (/scheduleCs). Asked when ../writableHomeUsedForScheduleCBusiness is YES, and REQUIRED then.
WHAT IT FEEDS: it names the Schedule C whose Form 8829 figures this casualty. ../sectionBCasualtyLoss reads that Schedule C's Form 8829 line 35 through it, and form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line29ExcessCasualtyLosses reads this event's loss back (../homeCasualtyLossForForm8829) on the Schedule C it names. One event names one Schedule C; a home used by two businesses is outside this intake.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: on an event attested YES, line 27 and line 28 are Incomplete; on any other event it is never read.

Fact.Name: This home casualty's loss for Form 8829 line 29 (Form 4684 lines 19 to 26, less the reimbursement)
Fact.Description: The loss Form 8829 takes up for a home used for a Schedule C business: 0 when ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear is true (the loss belongs to another tax year), else ../sectionBLineTwentyEightMeasure, the Section B line 26 loss less the line 21 reimbursement, summed over the property columns when they are answered. i4684 says to "complete Form 4684, Section B, lines 19 through 26" and then figure the deductible loss on Form 8829; i8829 Line 29 multiplies "the casualty losses attributable to the home" by the business percentage. This fact is that loss, before the business percentage, which form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line29ExcessCasualtyLosses applies. It never reads line 27, so the Form 8829 line 35 that line 27 then reads cannot loop back into it.

Fact.Name: Property was totally destroyed by casualty or lost from theft (Form 4684 line 26 Note, Section B only)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 26 carries a Note that Section A line 8 does not: "If the property was totally destroyed by casualty or lost from theft, enter on line 26 the amount from line 20" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2) - i.e. the loss is the FULL adjusted basis, not the smaller of basis and the decline in fair market value. Compare Section A line 8, "Enter the smaller of line 2 or line 7" (line 43), which has no such Note. The two answers differ only when the property's fair market value before the casualty was already BELOW its adjusted basis; otherwise the smaller-of rule already returns the basis. READ ONLY ON THE SECTION B ARM (../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement); it changes no Section A event. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means NOT totally destroyed, which takes the smaller-of rule and so UNDER-states the loss for a filer who was entitled to the Note - the conservative direction, and the same posture every other unanswered intake here takes.

Fact.Name: Had you owned this property for more than one year when the casualty or theft happened?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Had you owned this property for more than one year when the casualty or theft happened?" The per-event HOLDING-PERIOD attestation. The filer reads it off their own records; it is not a computation, and it is deliberately NOT a DATE (a date would let the engine derive the period and would be the better intake if the acquisition date were on any document the filer transcribes, and it is not).
ASKED-WHEN: on a SECTION A event - gain events AND loss events alike - whenever the return has a Form 4684 line-15 net gain, because line 15 says to "Combine your short-term gains with your short-term losses" and to combine long with long, so a net-gain return needs a holding period on every Section A event that carries a loss as well; and on EVERY SECTION B event, because Section B Part II sorts every item, gain or loss, under one of its two printed headings ("Casualty or Theft of Property Held One Year or Less" and "Casualty or Theft of Property Held More Than One Year").
WHAT MAKES IT REQUIRED IS NARROWER THAN WHAT MAKES IT USEFUL, and ../heldMoreThanOneYear holds that distinction rather than this writable. It reads this answer BARE - so an unanswered one refuses - on a Section A event when /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD is more than zero, and on a Section B event when /anySectionBCasualtyGain is true. On a Section B event with neither, it reads the answer behind IsComplete: supplied, it sorts the row into the line 29 half or the line 34 half; unanswered, it resolves a complete FALSE and nothing is refused. The sort changes which Part II half PRINTS the row and no dollar at either exit, which ../heldMoreThanOneYear proves.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: no answer is ever silently taken as short-term where the answer changes a number - the bare arms refuse instead - and everywhere else it resolves a complete FALSE. VALIDATION: Boolean, no further constraint.

Fact.Name: Were you entitled to an insurance payment or other reimbursement for this loss that you chose not to claim?
Fact.Description:
THE DECLINED-CLAIM ATTESTATION, and it is a question about a CHOICE, not about an outcome: the filer was entitled to a reimbursement and elected not to file a claim for it. 2025 i4684 Line 4 makes that choice change the MEASURE of the gain and nothing else: "If you are entitled to an insurance payment or other reimbursement for any part of a casualty or theft loss but you choose not to file a claim for the loss, you can't realize a gain from that payment or reimbursement. Therefore, figure the gain on line 4 by subtracting your cost or other basis in the property (line 2) only from the amount of reimbursement you actually received. Enter the result on line 4, but don't enter less than zero."
WHAT IT CHANGES AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. It changes the MINUEND of line 4 only - ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure reads ../writableReimbursementActuallyReceived instead of line 3. It does NOT change line 3 itself and therefore does not change the LOSS side: line 10 keeps subtracting the full reimbursement the filer was entitled to, which is what the instructions require of a filer who did not claim ("If you don't file a timely insurance claim, you can't deduct the full unrecovered amount as a casualty or theft loss and only the part of the loss that isn't covered by your insurance policy is deductible", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 3, LEFT column). The statutory loss-side mirror, IRC 165(h)(4)(E), is arm (10) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain and is NOT built here; this attestation makes it DETECTABLE for the first time, which is recorded there rather than acted on.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means the filer either claimed, or was entitled to nothing - today's behaviour for every existing return exactly, because ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure then falls through to line 3. TRUE-BUT-UNANSWERED-AMOUNT IS REFUSED IN THE SAFE DIRECTION rather than defaulted: with no amount the measure ALSO falls through to line 3, so the gain is the larger one and /knockoutCasualtyGain keeps refusing the return exactly as it did before this intake existed. A default of zero would silently DELETE a real gain, which this fact's REFUSED-in-the-safe-direction design exists to prevent.

Fact.Name: In what year did you receive the reimbursement for this loss? (Form 4684 line 4 timing)
Fact.Description:
THE TIMING TERM. 2025 i4684 Line 4 puts the gain in the year the money arrives, not the year the casualty happened: "If you filed a claim for reimbursement but didn't receive it until after the year of the casualty or theft, include the gain in your income in the year you received the reimbursement."
WHAT THIS RETURN DOES WITH A LATER-YEAR REIMBURSEMENT: NOTHING, and that is the rule rather than an omission. A year after /taxYear makes ../reimbursementReceivedInLaterYear true, which drives ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure to 0 for this event - so there is no line-4 gain on THIS return and /knockoutCasualtyGain does not refuse the return for one. The gain belongs to the LATER year's return, where the filer reports it; nothing in a TY2025 dictionary can carry it forward, and nothing here pretends to.
THE LOSS SIDE IS NOT TOUCHED, deliberately, and the reason is that the loss has its own timing rule which is NOT this one: "If in the year of the casualty there is a claim for reimbursement with a reasonable prospect of recovery, the loss isn't sustained until you know with reasonable certainty whether such reimbursement will be received" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 23, LEFT column). That is a rule about WHETHER THERE IS A LOSS TO REPORT AT ALL, it is not stated on any Form 4684 line, and this dictionary models it nowhere. It is named here so it is not silence.
THE YEAR IS ASKED, NOT A YES/NO, because the year is what the filer reads off their own records and because a Boolean would collapse two different answers ("2026" and "I don't know yet") into one. The Limit floor is /taxYear itself: this collection carries no casualty DATE, so every event in it is a THIS-YEAR casualty by construction. A reimbursement for a PRIOR-year casualty arriving in 2025 is expressible: the prior-year-casualty intake is ../writableCasualtyOccurredInPriorTaxYear, and this fact's Limit floor at /taxYear is unchanged and still correct because it bounds the year the MONEY arrived, not the year the casualty happened - a prior-year casualty reimbursed in 2025 already produces the printed line-4 gain through this fact's own default arm, since lines 2 and 3 are both this return's figures. What remains owed for that population is only the IRC 111 ordinary-income recharacterization, set out on ../writableCasualtyOccurredInPriorTaxYear.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means the reimbursement arrived in the tax year, which is today's behaviour for every existing return exactly - ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure takes its default arm and the gain is this year's. That default is the LARGER measure for this return and never deletes income.

Fact.Name: How much of that reimbursement did you actually receive? (Form 4684 line 4 measure)
Fact.Description:
THE AMOUNT ACTUALLY RECEIVED, read only when ../writableDeclinedToFileReimbursementClaim is true. It is the minuend of Form 4684 line 4 for a filer who declined to claim: "figure the gain on line 4 by subtracting your cost or other basis in the property (line 2) only from the amount of reimbursement you actually received" (2025 i4684 Line 4).
IT IS NOT LINE 3 AND MUST NOT BE ENTERED AS LINE 3. ../reimbursement stays the full amount the filer was entitled to, because that is what reduces the loss on line 10; this fact is the smaller figure that measures the GAIN. On a filer who claimed everything they were entitled to the two are equal and this fact is never read.
IT MAY BE ZERO, and zero is the ordinary case: a filer who declined the claim outright received nothing, so line 4's minuend is 0 and there is no gain. Zero is therefore an ANSWER here and not an absence, which is why the sibling Boolean carries the requiredness rather than this Dollar carrying it alone.
UNANSWERED IS THE SAFE FALL-THROUGH, NOT A ZERO. If the Boolean is true and this is unanswered, ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure takes line 3 - the LARGER measure - so the return keeps its gain and /knockoutCasualtyGain keeps refusing it. Defaulting to zero here would delete a real gain from a real return.

Fact.Name: Did this casualty or theft happen in a tax year BEFORE 2025?
Fact.Description:
ITEM (14) OF THE /knockoutCasualtyGain CONTRACT - THE HALF OF ARM (8) THAT RUNS THE OTHER WAY. Arm (8) discharged the case where THIS year's casualty is reimbursed LATER; this is the case where a PRIOR year's casualty is reimbursed NOW. 2025 i4684 Line 4 puts the gain in the RECEIPT year whichever side of the line the casualty falls on: "If you filed a claim for reimbursement but didn't receive it until after the year of the casualty or theft, include the gain in your income in the year you received the reimbursement" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 8, LEFT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction), and the When To Deduct a Loss Caution says it once more from the gain's own side: "If you realize a gain from the reimbursement on your casualty loss, do not report the gain until the year in which that amount is received" (same file, lines 203-205, RIGHT column).
WHAT THIS ANSWER DOES NOT DO, said first so it is not read as more than it is. It does NOT change the MEASURE of the gain, and no new arm was needed for that: Form 4684 line 2 (adjusted basis) and line 3 (the reimbursement) are both THIS return's figures whether the casualty happened this year or four years ago, so ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure and ../casualtyGainAmount already produce the printed line-4 number for this population. Nor does it suppress a loss by itself: a prior-year casualty CAN still be deducted on this return, because "if in the year of the casualty there is a claim for reimbursement with a reasonable prospect of recovery, the loss is not sustained until you know with reasonable certainty whether such reimbursement will be received" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 4, LEFT column) - the sustained-later rule, which this module models nowhere and which is exactly why a blanket "prior year means no loss" arm would be WRONG. What this answer does is make the population EXPRESSIBLE, and it is the coherence gate on ../writableLossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn, which is the question that does move a dollar.
THE NAMED GAP THIS ANSWER MAKES VISIBLE RATHER THAN CLOSES: the recovery-of-a-deducted-loss RECHARACTERIZATION. Pub. 547 - "If you have already taken a deduction for a loss and you receive the reimbursement in a later year, you may have to include the gain in your income for the later year. Include the gain as ordinary income up to the amount of your deduction that reduced your tax for the earlier year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 14, RIGHT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction) - and 2025 i4684 with the limit attached: "If you are reimbursed for a loss you deducted in an earlier year, include the reimbursement in your income in the year you received it, but only to the extent the deduction reduced your tax in an earlier year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 4, LEFT column). THAT RULE IS NOT BUILT, for two reasons that are both structural rather than budgetary. (a) Its measure needs TWO PRIOR-YEAR FIGURES - the deduction taken AND how much of it reduced tax - and this dictionary carries no figure across tax years anywhere. (b) Its destination is not a Form 4684 line at all: an ordinary recovery under IRC 111 belongs on the Schedule 1 other-income line, which this unit holds no grant over, and collecting the two figures to feed nothing would be the wired-into-nothing anti-pattern. THE DIRECTION OF THE OMISSION is a mis-CHARACTERIZATION and not a shortfall: the whole line-4 gain is still reported and still reaches Schedule D, so no income disappears; what may be wrong is the RATE GROUP, when a slice of it should have been ordinary. Recorded as item (14) on the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain, which refuses every return carrying a casualty gain today anyway.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means the casualty is this year's, which is exactly today's behaviour for every existing return - the same posture ../writableYearReimbursementReceived takes for its own year question.

Fact.Name: Did you deduct a casualty or theft loss for this same event on a return for an EARLIER tax year?
Fact.Description:
THE ONE VALUE-MOVING HALF OF ITEM (14). A loss already deducted on an earlier year's return is not deducted a second time here: 2025 i4684 puts the deduction in the year the casualty happened - "Generally, you can deduct the part of your casualty or theft loss that isn't reimbursable in the tax year the casualty occurred or the theft was discovered" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction) - and Pub. 547 treats what arrives afterwards as an INCOME adjustment in the receipt year, not as a fresh deduction: "If you figured your casualty or theft loss using the amount of your expected reimbursement, you may have to adjust your tax return for the tax year in which you get your actual reimbursement" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 14, LEFT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction).
WHAT IT DOES: through ../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn and the shared gate ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear it drives ../lossAfterReimbursement - Form 4684 lines 9 and 10 - to 0 for this event, which empties all three Section A loss legs at once (../deductibleLossAfterFloor, ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor and ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor all read line 10) and therefore Schedule A line 15, /netQualifiedDisasterLoss and the increased standard deduction with them. THE LOSS SIDE IS THE ONE THIS ATTESTATION ITSELF DRIVES; the line-4 measure never reads this fact directly, because the whole point of the population is that the reimbursement IS this year's gain - see ../writablePriorYearDeductionNoTaxBenefitPortion for the separate, narrower intake that caps HOW MUCH of that gain is includible under the IRC 111 tax-benefit rule. IT DOES THE SAME FOR SECTION B, through the same shared gate: ../sectionBCasualtyLoss (Form 4684 lines 27-28) reads ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear as a leading Case, so this answer empties both Section B destinations - Form 4797 line 14 via ../sectionBLossColumnBi and Schedule A line 16 via ../sectionBLossColumnBii - and, because the Case leads, the Rev. Proc. 2009-20 safe-harbor theft loss of Section C with it. THIS IS THE HALF OF THE GATE THAT REACHES A PONZI EVENT; the 165(i) election beside it cannot, being gated on ../isEligible. The coherence gate below is inherited unchanged rather than duplicated: a Section B filer who answers this one alone still moves no dollar.
IT IS GATED ON ../casualtyOccurredInPriorTaxYear and answering it alone does nothing. The two questions are one story and the coherence is enforced rather than assumed: a loss deducted on an earlier year's return presupposes a casualty in an earlier year, and a filer who answers only this one has not told this return which year it was. THE AMOUNT of that earlier deduction and how much of it reduced tax - the two figures IRC 111's recovery rule needs - are SEPARATE, NARROWER intakes from this one, asked only on an event that answers THIS writable TRUE: ../writablePriorYearDeductionNoTaxBenefitPortion (the part that did not reduce tax, feeding ../casualtyGainAmount and ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome), and, on an event with no line 4 gain, ../writablePriorYearAllowedCasualtyDeduction and ../writablePriorYearExpectedReimbursementNotYetReceived (feeding ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome).
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means no earlier deduction, which is today's behaviour for every existing return exactly, and it is the LARGER-deduction default only for a filer who would be double-deducting.

Fact.Name: How much of the deduction you claimed for this loss on an earlier year's return did NOT reduce your tax for that year?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "How much of the casualty or theft loss deduction you claimed on your return for the earlier year did NOT reduce your tax for that year?" Shown once per event that answered ../writableLossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn TRUE - a follow-up to that attestation, not a stand-alone gate.
HELP TEXT: IRC 111(a), the tax-benefit rule: "Gross income does not include income attributable to the recovery during the taxable year of any amount deducted in any prior taxable year to the extent such amount did not reduce the amount of tax imposed by this chapter" (26 U.S.C. 111, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section111&num=0&edition=2024, SINGLE column). The 2025 Instructions for Form 4684 state the casualty-specific application in as many words: "If you are reimbursed for a loss you deducted in an earlier year, include the reimbursement in your income in the year you received it, but only to the extent the deduction reduced your tax in an earlier year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 4, LEFT column). Pub. 547 states the same rule under "Reimbursement Received After Deducting Loss": "if any part of the original deduction didn't reduce your tax for the earlier year, don't include that part of the reimbursement amount in your income" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 14, RIGHT column). This dictionary has no cross-year register - it does not know the amount of the earlier deduction or how much of it reduced tax - so the filer supplies the one figure that actually caps the includible amount directly, rather than this module attempting to re-derive a prior year's tax computation it never modeled.
ASKED-WHEN: every event where ../writableLossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn is TRUE (this is exactly the population the rule describes - a reimbursement for "a loss you deducted in an earlier year"). Not asked otherwise: an event with no attested earlier-year deduction has no recovery for section 111 to limit.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: 0 (the full computed gain is includible, i.e. NO reduction) - the conservative, HIGHER-tax default, and it is ALSO today's exact behaviour on every existing return: this writable is new, so an unanswered event resolves byte-identical to its pre-fill value. This is the opposite conservative direction from the sibling Boolean attestations in this module (which default to the taxpayer-favourable "no" answer), because here the taxpayer-favourable direction is a NONZERO answer the filer must affirmatively supply.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0. No natural Max is enforceable - this module tracks no prior-year deduction amount to cap it against.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../priorYearDeductionNoTaxBenefitPortion (the complete-safe restatement, additionally gated on ../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn so an orphan answer with no attested prior-year deduction cannot move a dollar - the same coherence idiom ../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn itself uses for ../casualtyOccurredInPriorTaxYear) is subtracted from ../casualtyGainAmount before the floor at 0, capping the recognized gain that flows to Schedule D via /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD, and to /knockoutCasualtyGain's refusal; on an event with no line 4 gain it instead reduces the earlier allowed deduction that caps ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome.

Fact.Name: The portion of an earlier year's deduction for this event that produced no tax benefit (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writablePriorYearDeductionNoTaxBenefitPortion when answered AND ../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn is true; else $0 (the IsComplete pattern plus the same coherence gate the writable's own Description explains - an orphan amount with no attested earlier-year deduction cannot move a dollar). Read by ../casualtyGainAmount, as a direct subtraction before the floor at 0, and by ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome, as a reduction of the earlier allowed deduction that caps the recovery; an event reaches at most one of the two, because the second is measured only on an event with no line 4 gain.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Was this loss already claimed as a deduction on an estate tax return (Form 706)?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "Was this casualty or theft loss already claimed as a deduction on an estate tax return (Form 706)?" Shown once per Section A (personal-use property) event, asked alongside ../writableLossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn.
HELP TEXT: IRC 165(h)(4)(D) flatly bars the deduction: "No loss described in subsection (c)(3) shall be allowed if, at the time of filing the return, such loss has been claimed for estate tax purposes in the estate tax return" (26 U.S.C. 165, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section165&num=0&edition=2024, SINGLE column). The 2025 Instructions for Form 4684, Section A, state the same rule before line 1: "Don't include any loss previously deducted on an estate tax return" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 7, Section A preamble). This is the situation where a decedent's property was damaged or stolen and the loss was already deducted against the DECEDENT'S ESTATE on its Form 706 - claiming the same loss again on an income tax return would be a double deduction, which the statute disallows outright rather than netting or capping.
ASKED-WHEN: every Section A event (personal-use property; the (c)(3) statutory description this bar names is the personal-use casualty/theft category defined at IRC 165(c)(3), which excludes property "connected with a trade or business" - so a Section B business or income-producing event does not carry this question).
UNANSWERED POSTURE: FALSE (not claimed on an estate tax return) - the same conservative default ../writableLossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn uses for the sibling suspension question, so an event that leaves this unanswered deducts normally rather than being silently barred.
VALIDATION: Boolean, no further constraint.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../lossClaimedOnEstateTaxReturn (the complete-safe, Section-A-scoped restatement) is a disjunct of ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear, the single choke point that drives ../lossAfterReimbursement (Form 4684 line 10) to 0 for this event when true - emptying ../deductibleLossAfterFloor (Schedule A line 15), ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor (/netQualifiedDisasterLoss, the increased standard deduction) and ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor (the Worksheet 1-1 gain-offset lift) together, exactly as the sibling prior-year-deduction and 165(i)-election attestations already do.

Fact.Name: This event's loss was already claimed on an estate tax return (complete-safe, Section A only)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when ../writableLossClaimedOnEstateTaxReturn is answered TRUE AND the event is NOT a Section B event (../isSectionB); FALSE otherwise, including when the writable is unanswered. THE Not(../isSectionB) CONJUNCT IS DELIBERATE AND NARROWER THAN ITS TWO SIBLINGS: IRC 165(h)(4)(D) bars only "a loss described in subsection (c)(3)" - the personal-use casualty/theft category IRC 165(c)(3) defines by excluding property "connected with a trade or business" - so unlike ../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn (IRC 165(a), no such restriction) this leg must not reach a Section B event through ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear's widened Section B consumer (../sectionBCasualtyLoss). Scoping it here, on this alias, keeps ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear itself unchanged in shape (an Any of complete-safe aliases) rather than adding an isSectionB test to that shared fact for one leg only.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT: the writable's IsComplete/Switch idiom plus the complete-safe ../isSectionB gate make this complete-safe by construction.

Fact.Name: Are you electing to deduct this federally declared disaster loss on your 2024 return instead of this one?
Fact.Description:
ITEM (15) OF THE /knockoutCasualtyGain CONTRACT: THE IRC 165(i) ELECTION, built in the one direction a TY2025 return can carry. The statute: "Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (a), any loss occurring in a disaster area and attributable to a federally declared disaster may, at the election of the taxpayer, be taken into account for the taxable year immediately preceding the taxable year in which the disaster occurred" (IRC 165(i)(1), 26 U.S.C. 165, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section165&num=0&edition=2024, SINGLE column). The instruction states the fork as an either/or: "You can either deduct the unreimbursed loss on your tax return for the disaster year (2025) or make an election to deduct the unreimbursed loss on your tax return for the preceding year (2024)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 4, RIGHT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction).
WHY IT ZEROES THIS RETURN'S LOSS RATHER THAN MOVING IT, and the statute says it in as many words rather than by implication: "If an election is made under this subsection, the casualty resulting in the loss shall be treated for purposes of this title as having occurred in the taxable year for which the deduction is claimed" (IRC 165(i)(2), 26 U.S.C. 165, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section165&num=0&edition=2024, SINGLE column). The casualty is DEEMED to have happened in 2024, so on this 2025 return there is no loss to report at all - which is what ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear delivers by driving ../lossAfterReimbursement to 0.
NOTHING OF SECTION D PRINTS ON THIS RETURN, and the brief that commissioned this fill had it the other way, so it is stated plainly. Section D is Form 4684 lines 52 through 57 (Part I election statement 52-54, Part II revocation 55-57; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 4), not lines 40-49, and it carries NO dollar amount - a disaster name, the loss dates and the property address. It rides the OTHER return: "To make this election for a loss in disaster year 2025, complete Part I of Section D on your 2024 Form 4684 and attach it to your 2024 original or amended return that claims the disaster loss" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 4, RIGHT column). So this answer's ONLY effect on the TY2025 return is the loss dropping out of it, and the Section D statement itself is a rendering obligation on the 2024 filing that this dictionary does not produce - named, not silent.
THE THREE THINGS THIS DOES NOT REACH, each a named gap with its own reason. (a) THE REVERSE DIRECTION. What would put an amount ONTO this return is a 2026-sustained disaster loss elected back into 2025 - the 2025 Form 4684's own Section D. That needs the 2026 event's basis, FMV and reimbursement, and /casualtyEvents is a TY2025 collection; no intake here can hold a future year's casualty. Item (15) on the contract named this and it is unchanged. (b) THE PART II REVOCATION (lines 55-57) attaches to an AMENDED preceding-year return ("Attach this Section D to your amended return for the tax year immediately preceding the tax year the loss was sustained to remove the previous disaster loss deduction", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 4), so no TY2025 original return carries it. (c) THE SECTION B HALF IS DISCHARGED. IRC 165(i) is not limited to personal-use property, and this election's gate now reaches Section B too: ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear is read by ../sectionBCasualtyLoss (Form 4684 lines 27-28) as a leading Case, and by ../properties/*/sectionBLineTwentySevenCasualtyLoss on the print side, so a Section B event that answers THIS election - reaching ../isEligible exactly as a Section A event does, since neither ../isEligible nor ../electsSection165iPrecedingYearDeduction carries a section conjunct - drops out of Form 4797 line 14 and Schedule A line 16 alike. WHAT 165(i) STILL DOES NOT REACH: the Section C safe-harbor theft loss. The election is gated on ../isEligible, and a Ponzi-type theft need not be a federally declared disaster; the leading Case does catch that population, but through ../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn, the other half of the shared gate, not through this election. Residuals (a) and (b) above are unchanged and still open.
IT IS GATED ON ../isEligible, the federally-declared-disaster attestation, because 165(i)(1) reaches only a loss "occurring in a disaster area and attributable to a federally declared disaster"; an election answered on a non-disaster event resolves FALSE and moves nothing. THE 6-MONTH DEADLINE IS FOLDED INTO THE ATTESTATION rather than derived: "the deadline for electing to take a 2025 disaster loss on your 2024 tax return is October 15, 2026" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 4, RIGHT column). This dictionary holds no filing date, so the filer attests that the election was validly made; that is stated here rather than hidden.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means no election, which is today's behaviour for every existing return exactly, and it is the arm that keeps the deduction on THIS return.

Fact.Name: Was the property destroyed in this casualty your MAIN HOME?
Fact.Description:
THE SECTION 121 GATE, and it comes FIRST for a destroyed main home: the gain is excludable as if the home had been sold, and only what is left is a candidate for the section 1033 postponement. IRC 121(d)(5)(A) is what makes a casualty a "sale" at all: "For purposes of this section, the destruction, theft, seizure, requisition, or condemnation of property shall be treated as the sale of such property" (26 U.S.C. 121, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section121&num=0&edition=2024). 2025 i4684 states the consequence: "If you have a gain because your main home was destroyed, you can generally exclude the gain from your income as if you had sold or exchanged your home."
THIS IS THE FIRST OF THREE, and the other two are ../writableOwnedAndUsedAsMainHomeTwoOfFiveYears and ../writableSection121ExclusionClaimed. All three must be answered before ../section121ExclusionAmount is anything but zero - it reads this one through the complete-safe ../mainHomeDestroyed - so a filer who answers this alone changes nothing.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means not the main home, which is today's behaviour for every existing return exactly.

Fact.Name: Did you own and live in that home as your main home for at least 2 of the 5 years ending on the day it was destroyed?
Fact.Description:
THE SECTION 121 OWNERSHIP-AND-USE TEST, asked as the single question the statute and the instruction both state as one: IRC 121(a) excludes the gain only "if, during the 5-year period ending on the date of the sale or exchange, such property has been owned and used by the taxpayer as the taxpayer's principal residence for periods aggregating 2 years or more", and 2025 i4684 restates it with the casualty date substituted for the sale date - "To exclude a gain, you must generally have owned and lived in the property as your main home for at least 2 years during the 5-year period ending on the date it was destroyed."
WHAT THIS ONE ANSWER FOLDS IN, said plainly because the fold is this fill's choice and not the statute's. IRC 121 carries a large body of qualification the taxpayer alone can apply - 121(b)(3) one sale every two years, 121(b)(5) the nonqualified-use allocation, 121(c) the reduced exclusion for a filer who fails the test for a qualifying reason, 121(d)(9) the suspension for qualified official extended duty, 121(d)(10) the section-1031 five-year bar. NONE of them is modelled. A filer to whom any of them applies must reflect it in ../writableSection121ExclusionClaimed, which is an AMOUNT rather than a computation precisely so that the reduced and the disallowed cases can both be expressed. The engine enforces only the two things it can: this test, and the statutory dollar ceiling.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means the test is not met, which denies the exclusion. That is the CONSERVATIVE direction - the gain stays on the return - and it is today's behaviour for every existing return exactly.

Fact.Name: How much of the gain on your main home are you excluding under section 121?
Fact.Description:
THE EXCLUSION AMOUNT the filer claims, capped by the engine at the statutory ceiling in ../section121ExclusionCap ($250,000, or $500,000 on a joint return) and read only when ../writableMainHomeDestroyed and ../writableOwnedAndUsedAsMainHomeTwoOfFiveYears are both true.
IT IS AN AMOUNT AND NOT A COMPUTATION, deliberately. Section 121 carries qualifications no return-preparation graph can apply from the facts this module collects - the once-every-two- years rule, the nonqualified-use allocation, the reduced exclusion under 121(c) - and an engine that computed the maximum would OVERSTATE the exclusion for every filer any of them touches, which is the taxpayer-adverse-to-the-IRS direction. Asking the amount lets the reduced case and the full case use the same field.
HOW IT ENTERS THE FORM IS THE IRS'S OWN MECHANISM, not this fill's invention: "If the gain is more than you can exclude, reduce the insurance or other reimbursement by the amount of the exclusion and enter the result on line 3" (2025 i4684). So the exclusion is subtracted from the line-4 MEASURE - ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure - and not from the gain after the fact. The instruction's other half, "If you exclude the gain and the entire gain is excludable, don't report the casualty on Form 4684", falls out of the same arithmetic: a measure reduced below ../adjustedBasis leaves no gain at all.
THE STATUTORY ORDER IS 121 BEFORE 1033 AND IT IS THE STATUTE'S OWN, not a convenience: IRC 121(d)(5)(B) says that "In applying section 1033 (relating to involuntary conversions), the amount realized from the sale or exchange of property shall be treated as being the amount determined without regard to this section, reduced by the amount of gain not included in gross income pursuant to this section" (26 U.S.C. 121, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section121&num=0&edition=2024). This fact reduces the measure; ../recognizedCasualtyGainAmount then applies section 1033 to what is left.
UNANSWERED IS ZERO EXCLUSION, the conservative direction: the whole gain stays on the return.

Fact.Name: Were these insurance proceeds for UNSCHEDULED personal property that was part of the contents of your main home in a disaster area?
Fact.Description:
IRC 1033(h)(1)(A)(i), AND IT IS NOT AN ELECTION. Where a main home in a federally declared disaster area is damaged or destroyed, "No gain is recognized on any insurance proceeds received for unscheduled personal property that was part of the contents of the home" (2025 i4684, Gains Realized on Homes in Disaster Areas). The filer does not choose this and cannot decline it; it is non-recognition as a matter of law, and under the 165(h)(5) regime that governs TY2025 it covers a large share of the very population /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses.
UNSCHEDULED IS THE LOAD-BEARING WORD. Scheduled property - the items separately listed and separately valued on the policy - is NOT covered by this rule and takes item 2 of the same instruction, which is the ordinary 1033 election at ../writableElectsToPostponeGainUnderSection1033. A screen that drops "unscheduled" collects the wrong fact.
