WHAT IT DOES: drives ../recognizedCasualtyGainAmount to zero for this event. The REALIZED gain on line 4 is unchanged, and so is ../hasCasualtyGain, so this answer does not remove the return from /knockoutCasualtyGain's population - the guard's own When is untouched by this fill.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means no, which recognizes the gain - the conservative direction and today's behaviour for every existing return exactly.

Fact.Name: Are you electing to postpone this gain by buying replacement property within the replacement period?
Fact.Description:
THE IRC 1033(a)(2)(A) ELECTION, which is never automatic. 2025 i4684: "Generally, you must recognize the gain if you receive unlike property or money as reimbursement. But you can generally choose to postpone all or part of the gain if, within 2 years of the end of the first tax year in which any part of the gain is realized, you purchase: Property similar or related in service or use to the damaged, destroyed, or stolen property; or A controlling interest (at least 80%) in a corporation owning such property."
THE REPLACEMENT PERIOD IS FOLDED INTO THIS ONE ANSWER rather than computed, and the Name says so - this is the same house convention ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty uses for the employee carve-out. The period is 2 years from the end of the first tax year in which any part of the gain is realized, extended to 4 years for a main home or its contents in a disaster area under IRC 1033(h)(1)(B) ("the period in which you must purchase replacement property is extended until 4 years after the end of the first tax year in which any part of the gain is realized"). Deriving it would need an acquisition DATE this module does not collect, and asking for the date would be the better intake only if a filer transcribed it from a document; they do not.
WHAT IS NOT FOLDED IN, and is a named gap rather than a silence: the RELATED-PERSON bar of IRC 1033(i), which denies the postponement to certain acquisitions from related persons. A filer it touches must answer NO here; nothing in this graph detects it.
WHAT IT DOES: with ../writableCostOfReplacementProperty it drives ../recognizedCasualtyGainAmount down to the excess of the reimbursement over the replacement cost, capped at the realized gain. The REALIZED gain on line 4 is unchanged.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means no election, which recognizes the whole gain - the conservative direction and today's behaviour for every existing return exactly.

Fact.Name: What did the replacement property cost?
Fact.Description:
THE REPLACEMENT COST, read only when ../writableElectsToPostponeGainUnderSection1033 is true. It is the whole arithmetic of the section 1033 postponement: "To postpone all of the gain, the cost of the replacement property must be equal to or more than the reimbursement you received for your property. If the cost of the replacement property is less than the reimbursement received, you must recognize the gain to the extent the reimbursement exceeds the cost of the replacement property" (2025 i4684).
SO THE RECOGNIZED GAIN IS THE EXCESS OF THE REIMBURSEMENT OVER THIS COST, floored at zero and capped at the realized gain - see ../recognizedCasualtyGainAmount, which is where the cap lives. A cost at or above the reimbursement postpones the gain entirely.
THE REIMBURSEMENT IT IS COMPARED AGAINST is ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure, i.e. the line-4 figure AFTER the declined-claim, timing and section 121 qualifications - which is what IRC 121(d)(5)(B) requires when both sections apply ("the amount realized ... reduced by the amount of gain not included in gross income pursuant to this section").
UNANSWERED IS NO POSTPONEMENT, not a zero cost. A zero cost would postpone nothing and recognize everything, which is the same OUTCOME here, but the two are recorded distinctly: ../section1033ElectedPostponement requires the amount to be answered, so an election with no cost behind it simply does not fire and the return keeps its whole gain.

Fact.Name: Was the property that was damaged, destroyed or stolen depreciable section 1245 property?
Fact.Description: THE PROPERTY-CLASS ATTESTATION arm (12) of /knockoutCasualtyGain needs, and the first half of the Form 4797 Part III route into Form 4684 line 33. 2025 i4684 Line 33: "If you had a casualty or theft gain from certain trade, business, or income-producing property held more than 1 year, you may have to recapture part or all of the gain as ordinary income. See the instructions for Form 4797, Part III, for more information on the types of property subject to recapture. If recapture applies, complete Form 4797, Part III, and this line, instead of Form 4684, line 34." SECTION 1245 PROPERTY IS THE ONE CLASS THIS BUILD MODELS on a casualty event, deliberately and with the rest NAMED. Form 4797 Part III covers sections 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 and 1255; the section 1245 block is lines 25a and 25b, "Depreciation allowed or allowable from line 22" and "Enter the smaller of line 24 or 25a", which is arithmetic this event already has both operands for. The section 1250 block (lines 26a through 26g) needs an additional-depreciation-after-1975 intake and an applicable percentage, and the 1252, 1254 and 1255 blocks need their own expenditure intakes; NONE of them is collected here, so a casualty gain on property of those classes still routes wholly to line 34 and its ordinary part is still understated. That residual is named on /sectionBLongTermGain and in the rebody contract, and it is one reason the guard is not narrowed. THE CLASSES ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ON THE PRINTED FORM and this build ORDERS a contradictory pair (1245 > 1250 > 1254) where form4797 refuses one; see ../sectionBSection1254OrdinaryRecapture. UNANSWERED IS "NOT SECTION 1245 PROPERTY", through ../isSection1245CasualtyProperty, and that default is TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE - it leaves the whole gain on line 34 as section 1231 gain rather than recapturing part of it as ordinary income. It is chosen anyway, because the alternative (refusing an event whose class question is unanswered) would refuse every Section B gain fixture committed before this fill on a question none of them was asked, and because NO RETURN CARRYING A SECTION B CASUALTY GAIN CAN BE FILED AT ALL: /knockoutCasualtyGain blocks the whole population. The favourable default is therefore unreachable in production and is a shape for the intake, not a live posture. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this event exactly where it was before this fill.

Fact.Name: How much depreciation was allowed or allowable on that property?
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 22, "Depreciation (or depletion) allowed or allowable", for a CASUALTY or theft disposition rather than a sale. Asked when the event attests section 1245 property (../writableIsSection1245CasualtyProperty) OR section 1250 property; it is the section 1245 block's line 25a ("Depreciation allowed or allowable from line 22") and therefore the cap on the ordinary recapture, which is line 25b, "Enter the smaller of line 24 or 25a" - and it also feeds the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 1 for the section 1250 attestation. WHY NO SEPARATE COST-BASIS AND ADJUSTED-BASIS INTAKE IS NEEDED, which is the whole reason this arm costs two questions and not five. Part III line 20 is the gross sales price, line 21 the cost or other basis, line 23 their difference and line 24 the total gain - and for a CASUALTY those are the same three figures Form 4684 Section B already collects: the amount realized is the line-21 insurance or other reimbursement, and line 23 is the same adjusted basis Form 4684 line 20 asks for. So Part III line 24 for a casualty event IS this event's ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount, and only the DEPRECIATION is new. ../casualtyDepreciationAllowed reads this writable BARE, and is therefore REQUIRED, on an event whose gain routes through Form 4797 Part III and which attests section 1245 or section 1250 property - an unanswered line 22 there REFUSES the return instead of quietly recapturing nothing and quietly emptying the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 1. It defaults to $0 everywhere else - every Section A event, every Section B loss event, every section-1254-only event - which is what keeps the Placeholder off /casualtyLossDeduction.

Fact.Name: Of the replacement property you bought, what was the fair market value of the part that is NOT depreciable section 1245 property?
Fact.Description:
ITEM (19) OF THE REBODY CONTRACT AT /knockoutCasualtyGain, section 1245 leg: the IRC 1245(b)(4)(B) term, which is the ONE operand of the involuntary-conversion recapture cap this build has never collected.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION (the application builds this screen from here and does not open an IRS document). QUESTION, as it must be asked: "Of the replacement property you bought for [event description], what was the fair market value of the part that is NOT depreciable section 1245 property?" Section 1245 property is depreciable personal property and certain depreciable non-residential real property; a building, land or a non-depreciable asset bought as the replacement is NOT section 1245 property and its fair market value belongs here. HELP TEXT, paraphrasing the governing statute with its cite: when a casualty gain is postponed under section 1033, the law still makes some of the depreciation you took come back as ordinary income now. The amount that comes back is limited to the gain you are already reporting PLUS the fair market value of any replacement property that is not section 1245 property. IRC 1245(b)(4): "If property is disposed of and gain (determined without regard to this section) is not recognized in whole or in part under section 1031 or 1033, then the amount of gain taken into account by the transferor under subsection (a)(1) shall not exceed the sum of - (A) the amount of gain recognized on such disposition (determined without regard to this section), plus (B) the fair market value of property acquired which is not section 1245 property and which is not taken into account under subparagraph (A)." (26 U.S.C. 1245, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1245&num=0&edition=2024, LEFT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction. THE SPELLING DIFFERS FROM THIS FACT'S OWN authority: COMMENT ON PURPOSE and both name the same file: XML forbids a double hyphen inside a comment, so the comment carries the single-hyphen form skeleton.py rule (9) collapses, and this Description carries the exact on-disk name .) ASKED-WHEN: the event attests depreciable section 1245 property (../writableIsSection1245CasualtyProperty) AND the filer elected to postpone gain under section 1033 (../writableElectsToPostponeGainUnderSection1033). Ask it on the SAME screen as the replacement-property cost (row 74) and about the SAME replacement property, worded "of the replacement property whose cost you just entered" - that wording is what honours 1245(b)(4)(B)'s own closing clause "and which is not taken into account under subparagraph (A)", because the (A) figure on a section 1033 election is the reimbursement LESS that cost. Ask it on no other event: with no postponement the cap's (A) term already equals the whole realized gain, so (B) can never bind and the question would be noise. It is NOT gated on the mandatory 1033(h)(1)(A)(i) regime (row 72) - that regime is written for unscheduled personal property that was part of the contents of a principal residence, which is never a Section B trade-or-business event. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED on the events this question is ASKED on, and DEFAULTED TO $0 everywhere else - both through ../fmvOfNonSection1245ReplacementProperty, which reads this writable BARE under All(../isSection1245CasualtyProperty, ../section1033ElectedPostponement) and resolves a Complete $0 outside it. So a filer who attests section 1245 property and elects section 1033 and leaves this blank gets Result.Incomplete and the return STOPS; every other event keeps exactly the arithmetic this module shipped before the fill, and no committed return moves. THE SCREEN OBLIGATION THAT COMES WITH THE REFUSAL: the screen that asks row 76 and row 73 is the screen that must ask this. A filer who reaches those two questions and is not asked this one cannot file. VALIDATION: Dollar, minimum $0, no maximum. It is a FAIR MARKET VALUE, not a cost: ../writableCostOfReplacementProperty (row 74) is a different figure asked for a different purpose (the section 1033 postponement measure) and asks nothing about the replacement's CLASS, which is why this question exists beside it rather than reusing it. $0 IS A REAL ANSWER AND THE COMMON ONE - a filer who replaced equipment with equipment enters zero - so the screen must let them say zero rather than skip. ONE MORE NAMED GAP, BESIDE THE ANTI-DOUBLE-COUNT CLAUSE ABOVE: SECTION 121 IS UPSTREAM OF THE (a)(1) MEASURE AND NOTHING CORRECTS FOR IT. ../casualtyGainAmount is built on ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure, which is the POST-section-121 figure, so a section 121 exclusion shrinks the (a)(1) amount this arm caps - while IRC 1245(a)(1)'s flush text recognizes the recapture "notwithstanding any other provision of this subtitle", which cuts the other way. THE INTERSECTION IS EMPTY IN PRACTICE - a principal residence is not section 1245 property and a Section B event is not a principal residence - and the direction is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, so this is a NAME rather than a build. It is stated so a reader does not take the silence for a finding.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: ../fmvOfNonSection1245ReplacementProperty, thence the (b)(4) cap inside ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture (Form 4797 Part III line 25b), thence /casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture, form4797:/section1245OrdinaryRecapture, Form 4797 line 31 and Part II line 13 as ORDINARY income; and by complement ../sectionBPartIIILine32Remainder, Form 4684 line 33.
OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this event exactly where it was before this fill.

Fact.Name: Was the property that was damaged, destroyed or stolen depreciable section 1250 property?
Fact.Description: THE SECOND PROPERTY-CLASS ATTESTATION, item (18) of /knockoutCasualtyGain, and the section 1250 twin of ../writableIsSection1245CasualtyProperty. Form 4797 Part III line 26 is the section 1250 block ("If section 1250 property: If straight line depreciation was used, enter -0- on line 26g, except for a corporation subject to section 291"), and a CASUALTY disposition is a Part III property column like any other - the instructions say so on line 20 itself: "For casualty or theft gains, include insurance or other reimbursement you received or expect to receive for each item." SECTION 1250 PROPERTY IS DEPRECIABLE REALTY - the instructions define it as "depreciable real property (other than section 1245 property)" - so this is the question a filer whose destroyed rental building was depreciated answers yes to, while row 76 asks the same question about equipment and other depreciable personal property. UNANSWERED IS "NOT SECTION 1250 PROPERTY", through ../isSection1250CasualtyProperty, and that default is TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE for exactly the reason row 76's is: it leaves the whole gain on line 34 as section 1231 gain. It is chosen anyway, and it is unreachable in production, because /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain of any class. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this event exactly where it was before this fill.

Fact.Name: How much additional depreciation after 1975 was on that property?
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 26a, "Additional depreciation after 1975", for a CASUALTY or theft disposition rather than a sale. Read only where ../writableIsSection1250CasualtyProperty is answered true. The instructions define the figure as "the excess of actual depreciation (including any special depreciation allowance, or commercial revitalization deduction) over depreciation figured using the straight line method" for the period after 1975. IT IS AN EXCESS, NOT THE WHOLE DEPRECIATION, and that is the entire difference between the section 1250 block and the section 1245 one. Row 77 asks for ALL the depreciation allowed or allowable (line 22, carried to line 25a); this asks only for the part above straight line. A filer who answered row 77's figure here would over-recapture. A CARRY-IN ATTESTATION, NOT A COMPUTATION, for the same structural reason the sale-side twin gives: the excess needs a per-year depreciation history and a straight-line recomputation of the same property over the same recovery period, and this graph holds neither. THE ZERO ANSWER IS THE COMMON ONE AND IS STILL AN ANSWER. The form's own line-26 header says "If straight line depreciation was used, enter -0- on line 26g, except for a corporation subject to section 291", and the instructions carve out post-1986 MACRS realty - 27.5-year residential rental and 22-, 31.5- and 39-year nonresidential real property - which is the bulk of the TY2025 population. NOT CAPPED HERE. ../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture applies line 26b's own minimum against the gain, so this input is free to exceed it; the cap belongs on the recapture. UNANSWERED IS ZERO through ../casualtyAdditionalDepreciationAfter1975, which recaptures nothing - the same taxpayer-favourable direction as the class attestation, and unreachable for the same reason: /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return that could carry this amount. THE SALE SIDE REFUSES THIS CASE AND THIS SIDE DEFAULTS IT, deliberately: form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/hasUnansweredAdditionalDepreciationGain knocks out an attested section 1250 GAIN whose line 26a is unanswered, and no equivalent refusal is written here because the whole population is already refused by the Section B casualty-gain guard, and because a refusal fact on this collection would have to be Complete on every Section A event to avoid the completeness contagion the (12) fill measured. NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit): an excess is never negative.

Fact.Name: Was the property that was damaged, destroyed or stolen section 1254 oil, gas, geothermal or other mineral property?
Fact.Description: THE THIRD PROPERTY-CLASS ATTESTATION, item (18) of /knockoutCasualtyGain. Form 4797 Part III line 28 is the section 1254 block ("If section 1254 property:"), and a CASUALTY disposition is a Part III property column like any other - the instructions say so on line 20 itself: "For casualty or theft gains, include insurance or other reimbursement you received or expect to receive for each item." SECTION 1254 PROPERTY IS AN OIL, GAS, GEOTHERMAL OR OTHER MINERAL PROPERTY whose adjusted basis was reduced by deducted section 263/616/617 expenditures or by section 611 depletion - IRC 1254(a)(3). It is neither of the other two classes: section 1245 gives back depreciation, section 1250 gives back the excess over straight line, and section 1254 gives back deductions that never entered basis at all. UNANSWERED IS "NOT SECTION 1254 PROPERTY", through ../isSection1254CasualtyProperty - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE in the same direction as rows 76 and 81, and unreachable for the same reason: /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain of any class. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this event exactly where it was before this fill.

Fact.Name: How much in intangible drilling, development, mining exploration costs and depletion was deducted on that property?
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 28a, "Intangible drilling and development costs, expenditures for development of mines and other natural deposits, mining exploration costs, and depletion", for a CASUALTY or theft disposition rather than a sale. Read only where ../writableIsSection1254CasualtyProperty is answered true. IT IS THE STATUTE'S LEG (A): IRC 1254(a)(1)(A) is "the aggregate amount of- (i) expenditures which have been deducted by the taxpayer or any person under section 263, 616, or 617 with respect to such property and which, but for such deduction, would have been included in the adjusted basis of such property, and (ii) the deductions for depletion under section 611 which reduced the adjusted basis of such property". It is what the filer DEDUCTED rather than capitalized - not depreciation, which is what rows 77 and 82 ask about for the other two classes. NOT CAPPED HERE. ../sectionBSection1254OrdinaryRecapture applies line 28b's own minimum against the gain, so this input is free to exceed it; the cap belongs on the recapture. UNANSWERED IS ZERO through ../casualtySection1254Expenses, which recaptures nothing - the same taxpayer-favourable direction as the class attestation, and unreachable for the same reason. THE SALE SIDE REFUSES THIS CASE AND THIS SIDE DEFAULTS IT, deliberately, exactly as for line 26a: form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/hasUnansweredSection1254ExpensesGain knocks out an attested section 1254 GAIN whose line 28a is unanswered, and no equivalent refusal is written here because a refusal fact on this collection would have to be Complete on every Section A event. THE PLACED-IN-THE APPLICATION FORK IS NOT COLLECTED, AND IT IS THE ONE TAXPAYER-ADVERSE GAP IN THIS UNIT. The instructions define line 28a in TWO ways by placed-in-service date: property placed in service BEFORE 1987 enters "the total expenses after 1975 that ... were deducted ... as intangible drilling and development costs under section 263(c)" and nothing else, while property placed in service AFTER 1986 enters the section 263, 616 or 617 deductions PLUS "the deduction under section 611 that reduced the adjusted basis of such property". THIS INTAKE ASKS THE POST-1986 QUESTION, and only that: an event attesting the pre-1987 date (../writableCasualtyPropertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987) reads the pre-1987 figure instead, ../writableCasualtySection1254ExpensesPre1987 (row 101), and ../casualtySection1254Expenses forks between them. THE RESIDUAL IS THE FILER WHO NEVER ANSWERS ROW 100: the default is still the post-1986 question, so an event whose destroyed mineral property was placed in service before 1987 and whose filer leaves row 100 unanswered OVER-states line 28a with depletion and mining-exploration costs the earlier definition excludes - and because line 28b is a minimum against line 24, an over-stated 28a can only raise the recapture, never lower it. THE DIRECTION IS TAXPAYER-ADVERSE for that unanswered population, which is the opposite of every other residual this unit carries, and it is why it is named rather than left to the screen: the screen wording must state it, and it is unreachable in production for the reason everything else here is - /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain. THE SALE SIDE HAS THE SAME GAP: form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/writableSection1254Expenses collects no placed-in-service date and no fork, so that side's over-statement is unconditional rather than confined to an unanswered row - inherited, not introduced. NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit).

Fact.Name: Was that property placed in service before 1987?
Fact.Description: THE FORK THE 2025 INSTRUCTIONS FOR FORM 4797 PUT ON LINE 28a, and item (21) of the kind="rebody" contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain - the ONE TAXPAYER-ADVERSE residual that contract carried. Line 28a is not one question but two, chosen by the property's placed-in-service date. Property placed in service BEFORE 1987 enters "the total expenses after 1975 that: - Were deducted by the taxpayer or any other person as intangible drilling and development costs under section 263(c) (except previously expensed mining costs that were included in income upon reaching the producing state), and - Would have been reflected in the adjusted basis of the property if they had not been deducted." Property placed in service AFTER 1986 enters the section 263, 616 or 617 deductions PLUS "The deduction under section 611 that reduced the adjusted basis of such property." WHY IT IS A QUESTION RATHER THAN A SCREEN NOTE: the earlier definition EXCLUDES depletion and mining-exploration costs, and line 28b is a MINIMUM against line 24, so an over-stated 28a can only RAISE the ordinary recapture. Every other default on this collection is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE; this one was not, which is why it costs an intake. THE PRINTED DEEMING RULE IS PART OF THIS QUESTION, not a second intake: "Property placed in service after 1986 and acquired under a written contract entered into before September 26, 1985, and binding at all times thereafter is treated as placed in service before 1987." A filer in that position answers YES here, and the screen wording must carry the sentence. WHAT THE SAME INSTRUCTION SAYS AND THIS BUILD DOES NOT DO, named rather than left silent: i4797 "Line 28" also tells a pre-1987 filer to "Include on Form 4797, line 22, any depletion allowed (or allowable) in determining the adjusted basis of the property". Line 22 on this collection is ../writableCasualtyDepreciationAllowed, which feeds only the section 1245 block (line 25a) and the unrecaptured section 1250 worksheet, and a section-1254-only event reaches neither, so that sentence moves no dollar here. The i4797 "Note" on integrated oil companies is CORPORATIONS ONLY and cannot arise on a Form 1040 return. UNANSWERED IS "PLACED IN THE APPLICATION AFTER 1986" through ../casualtyPropertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987, which is byte-for-byte the behaviour this module had before this fill. THE ADVERSE DIRECTION IS REVERSED FOR THE POPULATION THAT ANSWERS AND UNCHANGED FOR THE POPULATION THAT DOES NOT, which is why item (21) is re-stated as a narrower residual on the contract rather than struck. Unreachable in production for the reason everything else in this block is: /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this event exactly where it was before this fill.

Fact.Name: How much was deducted on that property as intangible drilling and development costs under section 263(c) after 1975?
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 28a, THE PRE-1987 LEG, for a CASUALTY or theft disposition rather than a sale. Read only where BOTH ../writableIsSection1254CasualtyProperty and ../writableCasualtyPropertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987 are answered true. IT IS A NARROWER FIGURE THAN ITS POST-1986 SIBLING, and that difference is the whole reason this intake exists: it is section 263(c) intangible drilling and development costs ALONE, excluding previously expensed mining costs that were included in income on reaching the producing state, and excluding BOTH the section 616/617 mining deductions AND the section 611 depletion that ../writableCasualtySection1254Expenses asks for. A filer who answered the post-1986 question for pre-1987 property therefore over-stated line 28a, and because line 28b is a minimum against line 24 that could only raise the recapture - the taxpayer-adverse direction item (21) of the rebody contract named. NOT CAPPED HERE, exactly as its sibling is not: ../sectionBSection1254OrdinaryRecapture applies line 28b's own minimum against the gain, so this input is free to exceed it. UNANSWERED IS ZERO through ../casualtySection1254ExpensesPre1987. On an event that attests the pre-1987 date and leaves this blank, line 28a is 0 and nothing recaptures - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the same posture rows 76, 77, 81-84 take, and unreachable for the same reason: /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this event exactly where it was before this fill.

Fact.Name: Was the property that was damaged, destroyed or stolen section 1252 farm land?
Fact.Description: THE FOURTH PROPERTY-CLASS ATTESTATION, item (18)'s residual on /knockoutCasualtyGain. Form 4797 Part III line 27 is the section 1252 block ("If section 1252 property: Skip this section if you didn't dispose of farmland or if this form is being completed for a partnership"), and a CASUALTY disposition is a Part III property column like any other - the instructions say so on line 20 itself: "For casualty or theft gains, include insurance or other reimbursement you received or expect to receive for each item." SECTION 1252 PROPERTY IS FARM LAND for which soil and water conservation expenditures were deducted under section 175 - IRC 1252(a)(2), "the term 'farm land' means any land with respect to which deductions have been allowed under section 175". It is none of the other classes: section 1245 gives back depreciation, section 1250 the excess over straight line, section 1254 the drilling and mining deductions that never entered basis, and section 1252 an AGE-DISCOUNTED share of the section 175 deductions. A CASUALTY REACHES THIS SECTION BY THE STATUTE'S OWN WORDS: IRC 1252(a)(1)(B)(i) measures leg (B) from "the amount realized (in the case of a sale, exchange, or involuntary conversion)". A casualty or theft is an involuntary conversion, so the section applies to it and nothing about this build extends the statute to reach it. THE 10-YEAR LIMIT IS NOT A GATE ON THIS ATTESTATION, deliberately, and the sale-side twin made the same choice for the same printed reason: IRC 1252(a)(1) applies to farm land "held for less than 10 years", but the way the form expresses that is the 0 percent band of the (a)(3) table and "Skip line 27 if you dispose of such farmland during the 10th or later year after you acquired it". Gating admission on a held-under-10-years test would refuse the very item the 0 percent band exists to compute; ../casualtySection1252Line27b delivers the zero instead. UNANSWERED IS "NOT SECTION 1252 PROPERTY", through ../isSection1252CasualtyProperty - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE in the same direction as rows 76, 81 and 83, and unreachable for the same reason: /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain of any class. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this event exactly where it was before this fill.

Fact.Name: How much in soil, water and land clearing expenses was deducted on that farm land?
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 27a, "Soil, water, and land clearing expenses", for a CASUALTY or theft disposition rather than a sale. Read only where ../writableIsSection1252CasualtyProperty is answered true. IT IS THE STATUTE'S LEG (A) BEFORE THE PERCENTAGE: IRC 1252(a)(1)(A) is "the applicable percentage of the aggregate of the deductions allowed under section 175 (relating to soil and water conservation expenditures) for expenditures made by the taxpayer with respect to the farm land". This intake carries the AGGREGATE; the applicable percentage is applied by ../casualtySection1252Line27b, exactly as the printed line 27b does it. THE CAPTION AND THE STATUTE HAVE DRIFTED APART and the caption wins on the screen, which is the sale-side twin's own choice restated: the 2018 amendment (Pub. L. 115-141 section 401(b)(32)(B)) struck the section 182 land-clearing half of (a)(1)(A), so the statute now names section 175 alone while the printed line 27a still says "land clearing". The filer is copying a figure off a line captioned "Soil, water, and land clearing expenses", so that is what this question asks for. A FILER CARRY-IN, like every other Part III history figure on this collection: it is a cumulative record of deductions taken in earlier years and the graph holds no prior-year state. NOT CAPPED HERE: ../sectionBSection1252OrdinaryRecapture applies line 27c's own minimum against the gain, so this input is free to exceed it. UNANSWERED IS REFUSED WHERE IT MOVES A NUMBER, through ../casualtySection1252Expenses: an event whose gain actually routes through Part III, attesting section 1252, inside the percentage bands (fewer than 9 full years held) reads this writable BARE. Everywhere else it reads $0. That is the ../casualtyDepreciationAllowed requiredness idiom, taken here for the reason the sale side gives its refusal fact: unanswered-is-zero would recapture nothing and send the whole gain to Part I, which is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE and cannot be a silent default. REQUIRED on an attested section 1252 casualty gain inside the bands; optional everywhere else.

Fact.Name: How many full years did you hold that farm land before the casualty or theft?
Fact.Description: THE IRC 1252(a)(3) APPLICABLE-PERCENTAGE DRIVER for a CASUALTY or theft disposition: the number of WHOLE years between the day the farm land was acquired and the day of the casualty. Read only where ../writableIsSection1252CasualtyProperty is answered true. IT IS NOT ../writablePropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear, and the two are not substitutes. That Boolean sorts a gain or loss between Schedule D Part I and Part II and between the Form 4684 Section B Part II halves; this Int indexes the 5-to-10-year bands of the section 1252 table. One quantity, one fact: a Boolean cannot carry a band index and this count cannot carry a holding-period sort, because a filer answering "more than one year" has said nothing about which band applies. A WHOLE-YEAR COUNT IS EXACT HERE, not an approximation, and the reason is printed: every band of IRC 1252(a)(3) breaks on an ANNIVERSARY ("Within the sixth year after it was acquired", and so on), so the whole years elapsed decide the band with nothing left over. Its section 1255 sibling would NOT be exact - IRC 1255(a)(3) counts "each year or part thereof" - which is why the section 1255 block on this collection asks for the product instead and why no years intake exists for it. UNANSWERED IS ZERO FULL YEARS through ../casualtyFarmlandFullYearsHeld, which is the 100 percent band - the LARGEST recapture and therefore the taxpayer-ADVERSE default, which is why it is a default rather than a refusal. It also keeps an unanswered count inside the requiredness gate on ../casualtySection1252Expenses: 0 is under 9, so an event that answers neither intake still refuses on the expenses rather than computing a silent zero. OPTIONAL: unanswered takes the 100 percent band.

Fact.Name: Was the property that was damaged, destroyed or stolen section 1255 cost-sharing property?
Fact.Description: THE FIFTH AND LAST PROPERTY-CLASS ATTESTATION, and with it item (18)'s class complement on /knockoutCasualtyGain is closed. Form 4797 Part III line 29 is the section 1255 block ("If section 1255 property:"), the last of the printed line 19(a) classes ("Description of section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254, or 1255 property"). SECTION 1255 PROPERTY IS SECTION 126 PROPERTY - IRC 1255(a)(2), "any property acquired, improved, or otherwise modified by the application of payments excluded from gross income under section 126", the federal cost-sharing conservation payments a farmer or landowner elected not to include in income. A CASUALTY REACHES THIS SECTION BY THE STATUTE'S OWN WORDS, as it does section 1252: IRC 1255(a)(1)(B)(i) measures leg (B) from "the amount realized (in the case of a sale, exchange, or involuntary conversion)". UNANSWERED IS "NOT SECTION 1255 PROPERTY", through ../isSection1255CasualtyProperty - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE in the same direction as rows 76, 81, 83 and 102, and unreachable for the same reason: /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain of any class. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this event exactly where it was before this fill.

Fact.Name: What is the applicable percentage of the section 126 payments excluded on that property?
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 29a, "Applicable percentage of payments excluded from income under section 126", for a CASUALTY or theft disposition rather than a sale. Read only where ../writableIsSection1255CasualtyProperty is answered true. THE PRINTED LINE ASKS FOR THE PRODUCT, NOT THE PAYMENTS, and this intake matches the form rather than the statute's two factors. That is why this class needs ONE intake where section 1252 needs two: line 27a asks for the raw expenses and line 27b multiplies, but line 29a is already "Applicable percentage of payments". THE PERCENTAGE THE FILER APPLIES is IRC 1255(a)(3): 100 percent for a disposition less than 10 years after the section 126 payments were received, then 100 percent reduced by 10 percentage points "for each year or part thereof in excess of 10 years", not below zero - which the instructions restate as "Use zero if 20 years or more". WHY THE GRAPH DOES NOT COMPUTE IT, stated rather than left to a reader, and it is the sale-side twin's reasoning re-derived on this collection: the count is from the DATE OF RECEIPT OF THE PAYMENTS, not from acquisition, and it counts "each year or PART thereof", so a whole-year intake of the kind ../writableCasualtyFarmlandFullYearsHeld carries would be an approximation rather than the rule. /casualtyEvents holds no receipt date to count from and no month count, and asking for two figures the printed line does not ask for would still not settle the part-year rounding. Every band of IRC 1252(a)(3) breaks on an exact anniversary, which is why THAT percentage is computed on ../casualtySection1252Line27b and this one is not. NOT CAPPED HERE: ../sectionBSection1255OrdinaryRecapture applies line 29b's own minimum against the gain, so this input is free to exceed it. UNANSWERED IS REFUSED WHERE IT MOVES A NUMBER, through ../casualtySection1255ApplicablePercentageOfPayments: an event whose gain actually routes through Part III and attests section 1255 reads this writable BARE; everywhere else it reads $0. UNLIKE THE SECTION 1252 TWIN THERE IS NO BAND IN WHICH THE ANSWER STOPS MATTERING - the section 1255 phase-down is not knowable to this graph - so the gate carries no stand-down conjunct. REQUIRED on an attested section 1255 casualty gain that routes through Part III; optional everywhere else.

Fact.Name: Reimbursement (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../reimbursement when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern) - an event with no insurance leaves line 3 blank and this resolves 0.

Fact.Name: Declined-claim attestation (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableDeclinedToFileReimbursementClaim when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Complete on EVERY event, including an event that answers nothing at all, because ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure reads it and that measure feeds ../hasCasualtyGain, which /knockoutCasualtyGain reads collection-wide - an Incomplete here would make the knockout and therefore /flowIsKnockedOut Incomplete on every return with a casualty event.

Fact.Name: Reimbursement arrived after the tax year (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when ../writableYearReimbursementReceived is answered AND is strictly later than /taxYear; FALSE otherwise, including when it is unanswered. Complete on EVERY event, including an event that answers nothing at all, because ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure reads it and that measure feeds ../hasCasualtyGain, which /knockoutCasualtyGain reads collection-wide.
STRICTLY LATER, not later-or-equal, and the comparison is against /taxYear rather than a literal 2025 so the fact reads correctly if this module is ever carried to another year.

Fact.Name: The casualty happened before this tax year (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableCasualtyOccurredInPriorTaxYear when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means the casualty is this year's, which is what every existing return already assumes.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including an event that answers nothing at all, because ../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn reads it inside an <All> and that chain reaches ../lossAfterReimbursement, which the whole Section A loss side and the i4684 Line 11 floor flip depend on. Reading the writable BARE would make those Switches Placeholder on every event that leaves it blank - the trap this module measured once already and records at ../ownedAndUsedAsMainHomeTwoOfFiveYears.

Fact.Name: This loss was already deducted on an earlier year's return (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when ../writableLossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn is answered TRUE AND ../casualtyOccurredInPriorTaxYear is true; FALSE otherwise, including when either is unanswered. The second conjunct is the coherence gate described on the writable: a deduction taken on an earlier year's return presupposes an earlier year's casualty, and answering the deduction question alone leaves this return without the year it belongs to.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT. Both operands are complete-safe by construction, so this fact is too, which is what lets ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear be read BARE inside ../lossAfterReimbursement's first <When>.

Fact.Name: IRC 165(i) preceding-year election is in force for this event (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when ../writableElectsSection165iPrecedingYearDeduction is answered TRUE AND ../isEligible is true; FALSE otherwise, including when either is unanswered. The eligibility conjunct is IRC 165(i)(1)'s own condition - the loss must be one "occurring in a disaster area and attributable to a federally declared disaster" - and ../isEligible is this module's complete-safe reading of that attestation.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, for the same reason its sibling above is: both operands are complete-safe, so ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear can be read bare.

Fact.Name: This event's Section A loss belongs to another tax year, or is barred entirely (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
THE SINGLE CHOKE POINT FOR ITEMS (14) AND (15) AND THE ESTATE-TAX COORDINATION BAR, and it is one fact rather than three arms because all three rules have the same effect on this return by different routes. TRUE when the loss was already deducted on an earlier year's return (../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn - the deduction has been taken, in the year the casualty occurred), OR when the IRC 165(i) election puts it on the preceding year's return (../electsSection165iPrecedingYearDeduction - the casualty is DEEMED to have occurred there, 165(i)(2)), OR when the loss was already claimed on a decedent's estate tax return (../lossClaimedOnEstateTaxReturn - IRC 165(h)(4)(D)'s flat Section-A-only bar). Either way Form 4684 lines 9 and 10 are empty for this event on THIS return.
WHY IT IS WIRED AT LINE 10 AND NOWHERE ELSE. ../lossAfterReimbursement is the single upstream of all three Section A loss legs - ../deductibleLossAfterFloor (Schedule A line 15), ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor (/netQualifiedDisasterLoss and the increased standard deduction) and ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor (the Worksheet 1-1 line 1 lift) - and it is also the left-hand side of the i4684 Line 11 floor-flip comparison. Zeroing it once therefore empties every Section A destination coherently, and no leg needs its own copy of the gate.
WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REACH: the GAIN side (../lineFourReimbursementMeasure and everything downstream of it), because a prior-year casualty's reimbursement IS this year's gain and an elected disaster loss is a loss, not a gain. THE SECTION B LOSS CHAIN IS REACHED TOO, at the matching post-reimbursement choke point: ../sectionBCasualtyLoss (Form 4684 lines 27-28) reads this fact as a leading Case, ahead of its Section C/Ponzi arm, so both the ordinary Section B loss and the Rev. Proc. 2009-20 safe-harbor theft loss are suspended there - the Section B mirror of the "WIRED AT LINE 10 AND NOWHERE ELSE" paragraph above. ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement (line 26) is UNTOUCHED, for the same reason ../lossBeforeReimbursement (line 8) is untouched on this side. The printed property columns follow the same rule they follow in Section A: ../properties/*/sectionBLineTwentySevenCasualtyLoss carries the suspension exactly as ../properties/*/lossAfterReimbursement already does, so no column can print a loss on line 27 while the event's line 28 is a Complete 0. THE NAME IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: renaming would move the records contract and eleven committed assert files for no change in value.
THE THIRD LEG (../lossClaimedOnEstateTaxReturn) DOES NOT FOLLOW THE OTHER TWO INTO SECTION B, and that is a deliberate difference from the "widen the consumer, not the fact" precedent just above. IRC 165(h)(4)(D) bars only "a loss described in subsection (c)(3)" - the personal-use casualty/theft category - so unlike the prior-year-deduction leg (IRC 165(a), no property-type restriction) this leg must not reach a Section B event through ../sectionBCasualtyLoss's widened consumer. Rather than adding an isSectionB test to this shared fact (which would also have narrowed the other two legs), the scoping lives on ../lossClaimedOnEstateTaxReturn itself - that alias resolves FALSE for any Section B event regardless of the writable's answer, so this Any() stays a flat union of three complete-safe aliases and only one of them carries the extra gate.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Property destroyed was the main home (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableMainHomeDestroyed when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means not the main home, so no section 121 exclusion is available - the conservative direction.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, and it is not decoration. Reading the writable BARE inside a <When> makes the whole Switch Placeholder on every event that leaves it unanswered - MEASURED on this fill's first node-test run, where it reached /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized, /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain, /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD and /casualtyLossDeduction on eleven committed fixtures. This alias is what keeps /knockoutCasualtyGain, and therefore /flowIsKnockedOut, Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: IRC 121(a) ownership-and-use test met (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableOwnedAndUsedAsMainHomeTwoOfFiveYears when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means the test is not met, which DENIES the exclusion and keeps the whole gain on the return.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, and it is not decoration. Reading the writable BARE inside a <When> makes the whole Switch Placeholder on every event that leaves it unanswered - MEASURED on this fill's first node-test run, where it reached /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized, /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain, /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD and /casualtyLossDeduction on eleven committed fixtures. This alias is what keeps /knockoutCasualtyGain, and therefore /flowIsKnockedOut, Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: IRC 1033(h)(1)(A)(i) unscheduled home contents (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableIsUnscheduledContentsOfMainHomeInDisasterArea when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means no, which RECOGNIZES the gain - the conservative direction.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, and it is not decoration. Reading the writable BARE inside a <When> makes the whole Switch Placeholder on every event that leaves it unanswered - MEASURED on this fill's first node-test run, where it reached /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized, /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain, /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD and /casualtyLossDeduction on eleven committed fixtures. This alias is what keeps /knockoutCasualtyGain, and therefore /flowIsKnockedOut, Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: IRC 1033(a)(2)(A) postponement elected (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableElectsToPostponeGainUnderSection1033 when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means no election, which recognizes the whole gain.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, and it is not decoration. Reading the writable BARE inside a <When> makes the whole Switch Placeholder on every event that leaves it unanswered - MEASURED on this fill's first node-test run, where it reached /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized, /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain, /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD and /casualtyLossDeduction on eleven committed fixtures. This alias is what keeps /knockoutCasualtyGain, and therefore /flowIsKnockedOut, Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: The section 121 statutory ceiling ($250,000, or $500,000 on a joint return)
Fact.Description:
IRC 121(b)(1) caps the exclusion at $250,000; IRC 121(b)(2)(A) substitutes $500,000 on a joint return. The engine enforces exactly this and nothing else about section 121's quantum - every other qualification is the filer's, carried in ../writableSection121ExclusionClaimed.
THE JOINT CEILING IS READ OFF filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ, BEHIND filingStatus:/isFilingStatusComplete: an unanswered filing status takes the $250,000 arm rather than propagating an Incomplete, which is the CONSERVATIVE direction - the smaller ceiling, which under-excludes rather than over-excludes - and the return is refused by /knockoutCasualtyGain anyway. IRC 121(b)(2)(A) also requires that BOTH spouses meet the use test and that neither is barred by the once-every-two-years rule; neither condition is modelled, so a joint filer who fails one is relying on their own ../writableSection121ExclusionClaimed answer to stay under the ceiling they actually qualify for. That is stated rather than hidden, and it is the same posture the ownership-and-use attestation takes.
The IRC 121(b)(4) surviving-spouse substitution (a $500,000 ceiling for an unmarried individual whose spouse died within 2 years) is NOT modelled, because filingStatus cannot distinguish that filer; the direction is a ceiling that is too LOW, which under-excludes.

Fact.Name: The section 121 exclusion this event actually gets (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
The LESSER of ../writableSection121ExclusionClaimed and ../section121ExclusionCap, but only when ALL THREE of the section 121 intakes are answered the right way: ../mainHomeDestroyed true, ../ownedAndUsedAsMainHomeTwoOfFiveYears true (both complete-safe aliases of their writables), and the claimed amount answered. Otherwise 0.
ALL THREE, not any one, and the conjunction is the whole safety of this arm. A filer who answers only the main-home question changes nothing; a filer who fails the 2-of-5 test gets no exclusion even if they claimed an amount. Every gate is either a complete-safe read or an IsComplete test, so this fact is Complete on EVERY event including one that answers nothing, which it must be: ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure subtracts it and that measure reaches /knockoutCasualtyGain.
ZERO WHEN NONE OF THE THREE IS ANSWERED.

Fact.Name: Reimbursement actually received (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
../writableReimbursementActuallyReceived when answered, else 0 - the same IsComplete idiom ../reimbursementAmount uses for line 3, and it exists for the same reason: a raw Writable should not be read straight into an arithmetic consumer.
ZERO IS AN ANSWER HERE, NOT AN ABSENCE, and the distinction is carried by the CALLER rather than by this fact. ../lineFourReimbursementBeforeSection121 takes its declined-claim arm only when ../writableReimbursementActuallyReceived IsComplete, so the 0 this fact returns for an UNANSWERED amount is never the one that reaches the measure - an unanswered amount falls through to line 3 and keeps the return refused. What DOES reach the measure is an answered 0, which is the ordinary declined-claim case: a filer who declined the claim outright received nothing, so line 4's minuend is 0 and there is no gain. That answered 0 is CORRECT and must not be guarded away with a "> 0" test - such a guard would send a filer who genuinely received nothing back to the full line-3 measure and manufacture a gain the instruction says they cannot realize.

Fact.Name: The line-4 minuend BEFORE the section 121 exclusion is taken out of it
Fact.Description:
THE ONE PLACE THE GAIN'S MEASURE IS DECIDED. Form 4684 line 4 prints a bare subtraction ("If line 3 is more than line 2, enter the difference here") and then sends the reader to the instructions for qualifications on what that "line 3" means. This fact is that qualified figure; ../hasCasualtyGain and ../casualtyGainAmount read it instead of ../reimbursementAmount, so the qualifications live once rather than in each consumer.
THIS FACT IS THE SWITCH; ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure is this figure less ../section121ExclusionAmount, and it is the one the consumers read. The split exists because section 121 does not SELECT a measure the way the arms below do - the IRS has it REDUCE whichever measure the arms produced ("reduce the insurance or other reimbursement by the amount of the exclusion and enter the result on line 3"), so it is a subtraction wrapping a Switch rather than a fourth case inside it.
THE ARMS, IN SWITCH ORDER, each with its own intake: (1) DECLINED CLAIM - ../declinedToFileReimbursementClaim true AND the amount answered: the measure is ../reimbursementActuallyReceivedAmount, because "you can't realize a gain from that payment or reimbursement" and the gain is figured "only from the amount of reimbursement you actually received" (2025 i4684 Line 4). (2) LATER-YEAR RECEIPT - ../reimbursementReceivedInLaterYear true: the measure is 0, because "If you filed a claim for reimbursement but didn't receive it until after the year of the casualty or theft, include the gain in your income in the year you received the reimbursement" (2025 i4684 Line 4). There is no line-4 gain on THIS return. (3) DEFAULT - ../reimbursementAmount, i.e. line 3 as printed. This is the arm every committed return takes, which is why this fill moves no dollar anywhere.
WHEN BOTH ARE ANSWERED, ARM (7) WINS, by Switch order and on purpose. The two instructions have MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE premises - one is about a claim the filer chose never to file, the other about a claim the filer did file and was paid on late - so a return answering both is already inconsistent. Given the inconsistency the declined-claim measure is the one to take: it is a stated AMOUNT the filer supplied, whereas the timing arm's zero is an inference, and taking the stated amount is the direction that keeps income on the return. THE "DON'T ENTER LESS THAN ZERO" FLOOR IS NOT RESTATED HERE, and that is deliberate: it belongs to line 4's OUTPUT, and ../hasCasualtyGain already delivers it exactly - if this measure does not exceed ../adjustedBasis there is no gain and ../casualtyGainAmount is 0. Adding a second floor here would clamp the MINUEND rather than the difference and would be a different rule.
WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT TOUCH: LINE 3 ITSELF. ../reimbursementAmount keeps the full reimbursement the filer was entitled to, and the whole loss chain (../lossAfterReimbursement onward) keeps reading it. That is not an omission but the instructions' own split - the declined-claim rule changes the GAIN measure, while the loss-side consequence of not claiming is IRC 165(h)(4)(E), which no form line states and no intake here collects (arm (10) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain). [2026-09-01, wave 9 lane J5, beside the sentence above rather than over it: "which no form line states and no intake here collects" is FALSE on both counts and was false when written. The printed line 3 caption states it - "Insurance or other reimbursement (whether or not you filed a claim)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 1) - and ../reimbursement collects it: that writable is the amount COVERED, so ../lossAfterReimbursement's subtraction of it is the statute's "taken into account only to the extent not covered". The paragraph's conclusion is unchanged and right: this fact must NOT touch line 3. Arm (10) is discharged on the arithmetic, with a requiredness gate on ../lossAfterReimbursement (line 3 required behind a yes on row 66) closing its one live residue; see ../reimbursement and ../lossAfterReimbursement. THIS fact's complete-safe default arm is deliberately untouched.]
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT. Every arm's gate is a complete-safe Boolean or an IsComplete test, and the default arm reads the complete-safe ../reimbursementAmount, so this resolves on an event that answers nothing at all. That is load-bearing rather than tidy: ../hasCasualtyGain feeds /knockoutCasualtyGain, whose Incompleteness would reach /flowIsKnockedOut.

Fact.Name: Event is a casualty or theft GAIN (reimbursement exceeds basis; Form 4684 line 4)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe per-event gate: TRUE when this event's line-4 REIMBURSEMENT MEASURE (../lineFourReimbursementMeasure) is MORE than its adjusted basis (line 2, ../adjustedBasis) - the exact Form 4684 line-4 condition for a casualty GAIN ("Gain from casualty or theft. If line 3 is more than line 2, enter the difference here"). A gain is recognized income that Form 4684 routes to Schedule D, which this unit does NOT model; a gain-haver is reduced up to /knockoutCasualtyGain so the return is REFUSED rather than silently zeroing the gain and under-reporting income. IsComplete-guarded on ../adjustedBasis (an event whose basis is unanswered has no determinable gain and resolves false), and ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure is itself complete-safe, so this resolves Complete on every event - keeping /knockoutCasualtyGain and thus /flowIsKnockedOut Complete on every scenario (byte-identical: no existing casualty scenario has reimbursement > basis).

Fact.Name: Per-event casualty or theft GAIN (Form 4684 Section A line 4 / Section B line 22)
Fact.Description:
The GROSS REALIZED per-event gain - what line 4 prints, before any section 1033 deferral; the RECOGNIZED figure the form routes is ../recognizedCasualtyGainAmount. ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure minus ../adjustedBasis, FURTHER REDUCED by ../priorYearDeductionNoTaxBenefitPortion (floored at $0) when ../hasCasualtyGain is true, else 0. Section A line 4 and Section B line 22 are the SAME printed subtraction (line 3 over line 2; line 21 over line 20), so one helper serves both sections and the destination fork stays in the consumer, on ../isSectionB.
ROUNDED PER EVENT, not once at the end. Line 4 is a PRINTED per-column line, so the form's own convention is round-then-sum, and every other arithmetic Dollar fact in this module (../fmvDecrease, ../lossBeforeReimbursement, ../lossAfterReimbursement, ../deductibleLossAfterFloor, ../sectionBCasualtyLoss) carries the same Round for the same reason. Two events gaining 50 cents each total $2.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, and the safety is INHERITED rather than re-declared: the subtraction arm is reached only when ../hasCasualtyGain is true, and that gate is itself IsComplete-guarded on ../adjustedBasis, so basis is Complete wherever this subtracts; ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure is complete-safe by construction. No Placeholder anywhere in the chain.
THE MEASURE'S QUALIFICATIONS, all reached through ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure rather than modeled here directly. The DECLINED-CLAIM measure (a filer entitled to a reimbursement who chose not to claim it measures the gain from the reimbursement ACTUALLY RECEIVED, 2025 i4684 lines 511-518) and the LATER-YEAR-PAYMENT timing rule (a reimbursement not received until after the year of the casualty is that later year's gain, lines 520-523) both flow through the intake pair ../writableDeclinedToFileReimbursementClaim / ../writableReimbursementActuallyReceived and ../writableYearReimbursementReceived. The per-casualty qualified-disaster FLOOR FLIP (line 11, $500 to $100 once the summed line-4 gains exceed the line-10 loss, lines 532-541 RIGHT column) is ../qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies, which compares this event's line 10 against /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain; nothing here feeds ../deductibleLossAfterFloor directly, which applies its own floor unconditionally.
WHAT /knockoutCasualtyGain ACTUALLY CONTAINS: its condition is Count(../hasCasualtyGain) more than zero, so it refuses every return on which this fact's SUBTRACTION arm fires. It does NOT refuse a return where every event takes the ZERO arm, and one such population owes a number anyway: a filer who recovers a loss deducted on an earlier year's return against unreduced basis. That population's recovery is ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome, a Schedule 1 line 8z amount rather than a line 4 gain, and where it cannot be measured it is refused by /knockoutPriorYearCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome.
A FOURTH CONSIDERATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT DEFECT LIKE THE THREE ABOVE BUT A CAP ON INCLUSION: IRC 111(a) taxes a recovery of a prior-year deduction only "to the extent such amount did not reduce the amount of tax imposed by this chapter" - the tax-benefit rule. This module carries no cross-year register, so rather than re-deriving a prior year's tax computation, ../priorYearDeductionNoTaxBenefitPortion lets the filer supply the no-tax-benefit portion directly, and this fact subtracts it before the floor at 0. Unanswered subtracts 0 - full inclusion, byte-identical to every pre-existing gain fixture. A filer who enters UNREDUCED basis (rather than basis properly reduced by the earlier deduction under IRC 1016) with reimbursement below that unreduced basis takes ../hasCasualtyGain false and this fact 0, when Pub. 547's reimbursement-after-deducting-loss rule owes an inclusion on a TOTAL loss. That inclusion is NOT a Form 4684 line at all: it is OTHER INCOME for the year of recovery, Schedule 1 line 8z via Recoveries in Pub. 525, computed at ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome, and refused by /knockoutPriorYearCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome where it cannot be measured.

Fact.Name: The MINUEND of Form 4684 line 4 / line 22 - the reimbursement the GAIN is measured from
Fact.Description:
../lineFourReimbursementBeforeSection121 less ../section121ExclusionAmount, floored at zero. This is the figure ../hasCasualtyGain and ../casualtyGainAmount read, so it is where every qualification on the line-4 measure ends up.
THE SUBTRACTION IS THE IRS'S OWN MECHANISM for section 121, not this fill's invention: "If the gain is more than you can exclude, reduce the insurance or other reimbursement by the amount of the exclusion and enter the result on line 3" (2025 i4684, Main home destroyed). The instruction's other half - "If you exclude the gain and the entire gain is excludable, don't report the casualty on Form 4684" - needs no separate arm: an exclusion large enough to push this figure to or below ../adjustedBasis leaves ../hasCasualtyGain false and the event prints no line-4 gain at all. THE ZERO FLOOR is this fill's, and it is a guard rather than a rule: an over-claimed exclusion cannot drive the minuend negative and manufacture arithmetic nobody printed. It does not clamp the GAIN, which is line 4's own "don't enter less than zero" and is delivered by ../hasCasualtyGain.
SECTION 1033 IS NOT HERE. The postponement reduces what is RECOGNIZED, not what line 4 realizes, so it lives downstream at ../recognizedCasualtyGainAmount. IRC 121(d)(5)(B) is what fixes that order: section 1033 is applied to the amount realized "reduced by the amount of gain not included in gross income pursuant to this section", i.e. after section 121.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, because both operands are.

Fact.Name: A section 1033 postponement is elected AND its replacement cost is answered (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE only when ../writableElectsToPostponeGainUnderSection1033 is true AND ../writableCostOfReplacementProperty is answered. An election with no cost behind it does NOT fire: the arithmetic of IRC 1033(a)(2)(A) is entirely the comparison of the reimbursement with that cost, so without it there is nothing to postpone and the return keeps its whole gain. That is the conservative direction and it is a refusal to guess, not a default.
Complete on every event including one that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: Per-event RECOGNIZED casualty or theft gain, after section 1033
Fact.Description:
THE AMOUNT THAT MAY BE ROUTED. ../casualtyGainAmount is the gain line 4 REALIZES; this is what IRC 1033 leaves RECOGNIZED of it, and it is what ../sectionACasualtyGainAmount, ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount and /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized read - the last of which has said "Recognized" in its path since it was written and, until this fill, was not.
THE ARMS, IN SWITCH ORDER: (1) IRC 1033(h)(1)(A)(i), THE MANDATORY RULE, first because it is not an election and nothing overrides it: "No gain is recognized on any insurance proceeds received for unscheduled personal property that was part of the contents of the home" of a main home in a federally declared disaster area (2025 i4684). Recognized gain: 0. (2) IRC 1033(a)(2)(A), THE ELECTION: recognized only "to the extent the reimbursement exceeds the cost of the replacement property", floored at zero and CAPPED AT THE REALIZED GAIN. The cap is load-bearing arithmetic rather than tidiness: the excess of the reimbursement over the replacement cost can exceed the realized gain whenever the cost is below the basis, and without the cap a filer would recognize more than they ever made. (3) DEFAULT: the whole realized gain. Every committed return takes this arm, which is why this fill moves no dollar anywhere.
THE REIMBURSEMENT COMPARED IN ARM (2) IS ../lineFourReimbursementMeasure, the post-section-121 figure, because IRC 121(d)(5)(B) says so: in applying section 1033 the amount realized is "the amount determined without regard to this section, reduced by the amount of gain not included in gross income pursuant to this section".
../hasCasualtyGain IS DELIBERATELY NOT REBODIED TO READ THIS FACT, and that is the whole of this arm's relationship to the guard. /knockoutCasualtyGain's When counts events with a REALIZED line-4 gain, and it still does: a filer who postpones the entire gain under section 1033 is refused today exactly as they were before this fill. Narrowing that population is a guard narrowing, the guard is not narrowed part-way, and five arms still hold it.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT: every gate is complete-safe and every operand is.

Fact.Name: Per-event SECTION A casualty or theft gain (the Form 4684 line 4 term of line 13)
Fact.Description:
../recognizedCasualtyGainAmount restricted to SECTION A, i.e. 0 whenever ../isSectionB is true. This is the per-event addend of Form 4684 line 13, which is a SECTION A line: its instruction reads "Enter on this line the amounts from line 4 of all Forms 4684 reporting a gain", and line 4 is the Section A gain line. "All Forms 4684" quantifies over FORM COPIES (the printed form carries four property columns, so a fifth property needs a second copy), NOT over the two sections - a Section B gain is line 22 and leaves on line 29 or line 34 column (c), never through line 13.
WHY IT IS A SEPARATE FACT AND NOT A FILTER. The sibling total /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized sums BOTH sections deliberately, and this dictionary has no precedent for a CollectionSum over a Filter, so the section restriction is carried per event and summed by /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain. The two totals therefore COINCIDE on an all-Section-A return and differ as soon as a Section B event has a line-22 gain, where line 4 is $8,000, line 22 is $3,500 and the two facts read $8,000 and $11,500.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT: ../casualtyGainAmount is complete-safe by construction and ../isSectionB resolves Complete false when its attestations are unanswered.

Fact.Name: Per-event SECTION B casualty or theft gain (Form 4684 line 22, the Part II column (c) entry)
Fact.Description:
../recognizedCasualtyGainAmount restricted to SECTION B, i.e. 0 whenever ../isSectionB is false. The exact mirror of ../sectionACasualtyGainAmount, and together the two partition ../casualtyGainAmount: every event is on exactly one side of ../isSectionB, so the two restrictions add back to the gross gain with nothing dropped and nothing counted twice.
WHAT IT FEEDS. Line 22 says the gain goes "here and on line 29 or line 34, column (c)", and the instruction for Part II, Column (c) says which: "On line 29, enter the part of line 22 that is from property held for 1 year or less" and "On line 34, enter the part of line 22 that is from property held for more than 1 year". The holding-period fork is ../shortTermSectionBGain and ../longTermSectionBGain.
THE RECAPTURE CARVE-OUT (line 22's "except as provided in the instructions for line 33", spelled out by i4684 Line 33: a long-term gain on certain trade, business, or income-producing property may recapture part or all of the gain as ordinary income onto Form 4797 Part III, with the remainder returning on Form 4684 line 33) IS MODELLED for the section 1245, 1250 and 1254 classes: ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies is the i4684 Line 33 test, ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture is Form 4797 line 25b/26g/28b and ../sectionBPartIIILine32Remainder returns on Form 4684 line 33 through /sectionBCasualtyGainsFromForm4797Line32. It is STILL NOT MODELLED for sections 1252 and 1255, whose intakes do not exist, so a long-term Section B gain on that property class goes to line 34 column (c) whole - THE DIRECTION IS TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE, ordinary income understated and section 1231 gain overstated.
THIS FACT'S ROLE IN THE RECAPTURE CAPS DIFFERS BY CLASS. For section 1245, IRC 1245(a)(1) measures against "the amount realized", so the 1245(b)(4) involuntary-conversion cap's (A) term is ../casualtyGainAmount (the REALIZED gain) rather than this fact (the RECOGNIZED figure), and this fact is instead the (A) term of that cap - no printed line-24 operand changes, since the casualty column's line 24 is form4797:/partIIILine30TotalGainsAllProperties. For sections 1250, 1252, 1254 and 1255 this fact remains the line-24 measure of each class's own involuntary-conversion limit, none of which is built.
THE GUARD THIS FEEDS: it is owed by name as arm (12) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain, which refuses every return this fact is NONZERO on, over Count(../hasCasualtyGain) more than zero (a gain is exactly that condition); it does not refuse a return on which this fact only computes a zero.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT: ../casualtyGainAmount is complete-safe by construction and ../isSectionB resolves Complete false when its attestations are unanswered.

Fact.Name: Event is a SECTION B casualty or theft gain (Form 4684 line 22 fired on business or income-producing property)
Fact.Description: ../hasCasualtyGain AND ../isSectionB - the per-event term /anySectionBCasualtyGain counts. It exists as its own fact because this dictionary has no precedent for a Count over a conjunction, the same reason ../sectionACasualtyGainAmount is a fact rather than a filter. Both limbs are complete-safe, so this is Complete on every event and /anySectionBCasualtyGain is Complete on every return.

Fact.Name: Some event on this return is a Section B casualty or theft gain (Form 4684 line 22)
Fact.Description:
Count(/casualtyEvents/*/hasSectionBCasualtyGain) more than zero, gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so a return with no casualty claim resolves Complete false rather than reading the collection at all - the same collection-"any" shape /knockoutCasualtyGain uses, which mirrors scheduleE:/anyRentalHasAmtDepreciationAdjustment.
WHAT IT IS FOR, and it is the ONLY thing it is for: it is the requiredness switch on /casualtyEvents/*/heldMoreThanOneYear for SECTION B events. Form 4684 Section B Part II sorts every item, gain or loss, into "Casualty or Theft of Property Held One Year or Less" (lines 29 to 32) or "Casualty or Theft of Property Held More Than One Year" (lines 33 to 39), and the printed form asks the question of every filer who completes Part II. This build asks it only where the answer CHANGES A NUMBER, which is exactly when some Section B gain exists: with column (c) identically zero, line 36 and line 37 are both zero, the line-39 test ("less than or equal") is satisfied, line 39 is zero, lines 38a and 38b are zero, and lines 31 and 32 collect every column (b)(i) and every column (b)(ii) loss respectively - which is precisely the pre-2026-08-24 behaviour of /sectionBNetGainOrLoss and /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss, whichever side of the one-year line each loss really sits on. IT CANNOT CIRCLE. Every term below is a gain-side fact - a reimbursement-over-basis test and a section attestation - and none of them reads a holding period.

Fact.Name: Event is deductible (federally-declared-disaster eligibility, complete-safe)
Fact.Description: The eligibility gate: ../federallyDeclaredDisaster when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern). Only a federally-declared-disaster loss is deductible on Schedule A line 15; an ineligible event contributes 0 to the deduction.

Fact.Name: Event is a qualified disaster loss (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: The qualified-disaster gate: ../qualifiedDisasterLoss when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern). When true, this event follows the OBBBA special rules ($500 floor, no 10%-AGI, increases the standard deduction) via ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor and /netQualifiedDisasterLoss, and is EXCLUDED from the ordinary Schedule A line-15 path (../deductibleLossAfterFloor) so the loss is deducted exactly once (World #1 mutual exclusivity). Unanswered resolves Complete false, so every pre-U-066b scenario stays byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Event is a Section B column (b)(i) business/rental/royalty casualty (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: The Section A / Section B gate: ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern). FALSE routes the event down Section A exactly as before this fact existed - the federally-declared-disaster gate, the $100 per-event floor and the 10%-of-AGI floor all apply. TRUE fences the event OFF from both Section A outputs (../deductibleLossAfterFloor and ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor each resolve 0 for it, now via ../isSectionB) and routes its loss through ../sectionBCasualtyLoss and ../sectionBLossColumnBi to /sectionBNetGainOrLoss, Form 4684 lines 31 and 38a, and on to form4797:/casualtyOrTheftNetGainOrLoss (Form 4797 line 14). THE SIBLING COLUMN: ../isIncomeProducingProperty is the same gate for column (b)(ii), and it wins if both are true (../sectionBLossColumnBi). Unanswered resolves Complete false, so every scenario that predates the Section B arm is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Event is a Section B column (b)(ii) income-producing-property casualty (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern, exactly as ../isBusinessOrIncomeProducing). FALSE routes the event down Section A exactly as before this fact existed. TRUE puts the event in Section B column (b)(ii): it is fenced off from both Section A outputs (../deductibleLossAfterFloor and ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor each resolve 0 for it, via ../isSectionB), its loss runs the shared Section B chain to ../sectionBCasualtyLoss, and it exits on ../sectionBLossColumnBii to /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss - Form 4684 lines 32 and 38b, and on to scheduleA:/otherItemizedDeductions (Schedule A line 16). Unanswered resolves Complete false, so every scenario that predates the (b)(ii) arm is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Event belongs in Form 4684 Section B, either loss column (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: THE SECTION A / SECTION B MEMBERSHIP TEST: true when the event is attested as EITHER Section B loss column - ../isBusinessOrIncomeProducing (column (b)(i), trade, business, rental or royalty property) or ../isIncomeProducingProperty (column (b)(ii), income-producing property). The printed section heading is the reason it is one test and not two: "SECTION B-Business and Income-Producing Property" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2) admits both kinds of property, and the whole line 20 to 28 arithmetic (../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement, ../sectionBCasualtyLoss) is shared by them - the columns diverge only in Part II, at ../sectionBLossColumnBi and ../sectionBLossColumnBii. A THIRD LIMB: ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft, the Form 4684 SECTION C (Ponzi-type safe harbor) event. Section C is not a third SECTION of the form in the Section A / Section B sense - it is a substitute computation whose output re-enters Section B: line 51 says "Include this amount on line 28 of Section B, Part I. Do not complete lines 19-27 for this loss. Then complete Section B, Part II" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). So a Section C event IS a Section B event for every purpose this fact serves, and reading it here is what fences it off from Section A's three personal-use limits - correctly, since a Ponzi-type theft loss is a loss on property held for the production of income and not on personal-use property. THIS FACT IS ALSO THE SECTION A FENCE, and that is the load-bearing part. All three of Section A's limits are personal-use rules ("Losses on business property and income-producing property aren't subject to these rules", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 15; "casualty losses of personal-use property are deductible only if the loss is attributable to a federally declared disaster", lines 285-288), so ../deductibleLossAfterFloor and ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor both exclude an event that is true here. Before the (b)(ii) column landed those two exclusions read ../isBusinessOrIncomeProducing directly; had they been left that way, a (b)(ii) event whose ../federallyDeclaredDisaster was true would have been deducted on Schedule A line 15 AND on line 16 - the same loss twice, taxpayer- favourable. Both are built on complete-safe gates, so this is Complete on every event.

Fact.Name: Property was totally destroyed or stolen (complete-safe, Form 4684 line 26 Note)
Fact.Description: ../writableTotallyDestroyedOrStolen when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern). Read only by ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement. Unanswered resolves Complete false, which takes Section B line 26's ordinary smaller-of rule and so under-states the loss of a filer whose property really was totally destroyed - the conservative direction.

Fact.Name: Decline in fair market value (Form 4684 line 7)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 7 = line 5 minus line 6 (FMV before minus FMV after), the decline in fair market value. Floored at 0 (an event where FMV did not decline yields no loss). DIRECT-ENTRY ALTERNATIVE: when ../usedFmvSafeHarborMethod is true, this fact is ../fmvDecreaseFromSafeHarborMethod instead - the filer's own pre-computed Rev. Proc. 2018-08 figure - and lines 5/6 (../fmvBefore, ../fmvAfter) are NOT read, matching the instruction's "do not enter an amount on line 5 or line 6 for each property. Instead, enter the decrease in the FMV determined in the relevant safe harbor method on line 7."

Fact.Name: Loss before reimbursement (Form 4684 line 8)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 8 = the smaller of line 2 (adjusted basis) or line 7 (decline in FMV). For personal-use property the deductible loss is the lesser of what you paid for it (basis) and how much value it lost (Pub 547 "Figuring the Deduction"). DIRECT-ENTRY ALTERNATIVE: when ../usedCorrosiveDrywallProcedure is true, this fact is ../corrosiveDrywallRepairCost instead - the Rev. Proc. 2010-36 special procedure's own line 8, "Enter the amount you paid to repair the damage ... due to corrosive drywall" - and lines 2, 4-7 (../adjustedBasis, ../fmvDecrease and its own inputs) are NOT read for this event, matching Pub. 547's special instructions ("Line 2. Skip this line. ... Lines 4-7. Skip these lines"). This is why the drywall procedure is a SEPARATE intake from the Rev. Proc. 2018-08 safe harbor at ../fmvDecrease rather than sharing its shape: the two procedures replace DIFFERENT printed lines (7 vs. 8).

Fact.Name: Loss after reimbursement (Form 4684 line 9)
Fact.Description:
Form 4684 line 9 = line 8 minus line 3 (reimbursement). If zero or less, 0. Because a single property is modeled per event, this also equals line 10 (the per-event total).
THREE ARMS. (1) SUPPRESSION: when ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear is true this line 10 is a COMPLETE $0 for the event, because the loss belongs to another tax year - either already deducted on an earlier year's return or elected under IRC 165(i) onto the preceding year's return - so a suspended event resolves 0 even with FMV blank.
