(2) THE IRC 165(h)(4)(E) REQUIREDNESS GATE: when ../declinedToFileReimbursementClaim is true this fact reads ../reimbursement BARE, so line 3 is REQUIRED once the filer attests they were entitled to a reimbursement and chose not to claim it - a blank line 3 leaves this fact, ../deductibleLossAfterFloor, /casualtyLossAfterFloors and /casualtyLossDeduction Incomplete rather than silently deducting the full loss including the covered part, which 165(h)(4)(E) forbids. ../reimbursementAmount itself stays complete-safe (../lineFourReimbursementBeforeSection121's "COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT" invariant and the Section B facts read it), so the gate lives here rather than on that alias. (3) THE DEFAULT ARM subtracts ../reimbursementAmount, which resolves a blank line 3 to 0 - deducting the FULL loss including any covered part whenever the filer has not attested a declined claim. When line 3 IS answered arm (2) is value-identical to arm (3).
NOTE (scope): if reimbursement exceeded basis the event would be a casualty GAIN (Form 4684 line 4, to Schedule D), which is not modeled here - the gain itself is ../casualtyGainAmount and its Section A total is /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain (Form 4684 line 13). The floor at 0 keeps a gain-only event out of the loss deduction, but a gain-haver is KNOCKED OUT upstream (../hasCasualtyGain -> /knockoutCasualtyGain) so the floor is never the thing standing between a gain and the return; what /knockoutCasualtyGain still refuses is the ROUTING to Schedule D and Form 4797 and the non-recognition regimes.
THIS FACT'S VALUE IS READ by two more consumers besides ../deductibleLossAfterFloor: the i4684 Line 11 floor flip (../qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies compares THIS line 10 against the summed line-4 gains) and ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor.

Fact.Name: Were this event's property columns A to D answered? (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../properties, the per property collection that holds Form 4684 property columns A through D (item [0] is column A, items [1] to [3] are columns B to D), is answered with at least one item. FALSE when the collection is unanswered, and FALSE when it is answered EMPTY: an empty list states no property, so the event level leaves (../adjustedBasis, ../fmvBefore, ../fmvAfter, ../reimbursement) keep carrying the event as one property, exactly as they did before the collection was asked. Every event level line that adds the columns (line 10 at ../lineTenCasualtyLoss, the line 4 term of line 13 at ../sectionACasualtyGainAmount, line 28 at ../sectionBLineTwentyEightMeasure and the per event gain count at ../hasCasualtyGainInAnyColumn) switches on this one Boolean. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT.

Fact.Name: This event's casualty or theft loss (Form 4684 line 10, the sum of columns A to D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION A line 10, "Casualty or theft loss. Add the amounts on line 9 in columns A through D". When ../propertyColumnsAnswered is true it is the sum of ../properties/*/lossAfterReimbursement, the line 9 cell of every answered column (item [0] is column A); otherwise it is ../lossAfterReimbursement, the event level line 9, which carries the event as a single property. ONE EVENT, ONE FLOOR: every consumer of line 10 (the line 11 floor and line 12 at ../deductibleLossAfterFloor, ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor and ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor, and the i4684 Line 11 flip at ../qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies) reads THIS fact, so a casualty that damaged several properties takes the $100 (or $500) floor once on the column sum, which is Pub. 547's single event rule and its Example 1 (a tornado that destroyed a boat and boating equipment: 500 plus 1,200 is 1,700, less one $100, is 1,600). A column whose line 9 cannot be measured leaves this fact Incomplete; nothing here resolves an unanswered column to zero. The event level line 9 arms (the suspension, the declined claim requiredness gate and the Rev. Proc. 2018-08 and 2010-36 direct entry alternatives) are read only on the event level path; the column path reads each column's own line 9, whose suspension arm mirrors the event's and whose reimbursement is required, and has no per column direct entry alternative.

Fact.Name: Does any property column of this event print a casualty or theft gain? (Form 4684 line 4 or line 22)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the event level ../hasCasualtyGain is true, or when ../propertyColumnsAnswered is true and at least one column's ../properties/*/hasGainColumnCompleteSafe is true, that is its reimbursement exceeds its basis (Form 4684 line 4 in Section A, line 22 in Section B, the same test on the same two operands). This is the per event term /knockoutCasualtyGain counts, so a gain entered in any column is refused exactly as an event level gain is. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT: both terms are complete safe.

Fact.Name: This event's Form 4684 line 28 measure, before the event level overrides (the sum of line 27 over columns A to D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 28, "Casualty or theft loss. Add the amounts on line 27", as measured from the property columns: when ../propertyColumnsAnswered is true, the sum of ../properties/*/sectionBCasualtyLossMeasure over every answered column (item [0] is column A); otherwise the event level line 27, line 26 (../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement) less the nonnegative line 21 (../reimbursementAmount), floored at 0. It is the measure only: ../sectionBCasualtyLoss applies the event level overrides above it (the suspension, the Section C safe harbor figure, the Form 8829 line 35 figure for a home used for a Schedule C business, and the IRC 280A(c)(5) ceiling for a home rented out or used for another business). Form 8829 line 29 reads it through ../homeCasualtyLossForForm8829.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 28 as printed for this event (Section B only)
Fact.Description: ../sectionBCasualtyLoss when the event is a Section B event (../isSectionB, which includes the Section C safe harbor arm whose line 51 goes to line 28), else 0. ../sectionBCasualtyLoss itself is computed on every event and its consumers gate it by column, so the printed line 28 takes this gated twin rather than printing a personal use event's measured loss under the SECTION B heading.

Fact.Name: Does this event keep the 500-dollar qualified-disaster floor? (i4684 Line 11 flip)
Fact.Description:
THE PER-CASUALTY FLOOR FLIP - the fifth IRC 165(h) loss-side coupling, and the one the printed FORM does not state at all: line 11 prints only the outcome, "$100 ($500 if qualified disaster loss rules apply)". The rule lives in the instruction: add the line-4 gains from all Forms 4684 and COMPARE the sum with THIS event's line 10. If line 10 is LARGER, the $500 floor stands. If line 10 is SMALLER, the floor is $100 AND the filer is to "complete the remainder of the form without applying the special rules for qualified disaster losses" - so the flip does not merely change a dollar amount, it moves the event off the increased-standard-deduction path and onto the ordinary Schedule A line-15 path. That is why this Boolean gates BOTH per-event floor facts rather than sitting inside one.
TRUE when the event is an attested qualified disaster loss, is FEDERALLY-DECLARED-DISASTER ELIGIBLE (../isEligible), is not a Section B event, and its line 10 (../lossAfterReimbursement) is strictly GREATER than /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain (Form 4684 line 13, the summed Section A line-4 gains). The QUANTIFIERS are the instruction's own and they differ on the two sides: the gains side is a TAXPAYER-WIDE sum over every Form 4684, while line 10 is per Form 4684 - i.e. PER EVENT in this model, since this dictionary carries one property per event. Two qualified disaster events with the same taxpayer can therefore land on opposite sides of the same comparison.
THE ../isEligible CONJUNCT: every category in i4684's qualified-disaster-loss definition is itself a federally-declared-major-disaster category, so a qualified-disaster loss is a strict SUBSET of a federally-declared-disaster loss - ../isQualifiedDisasterLoss and ../isEligible are not independent intakes, and an event attested QDL=true but federallyDeclaredDisaster=false (or unanswered) is a CONTRADICTORY combination the printed form has no place for. Without this conjunct such an event's line 10 could flip this Boolean TRUE whenever it exceeded the taxpayer's summed line-13 gains, sending an INELIGIBLE loss through ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor into /netQualifiedDisasterLoss and the increased standard deduction, and excluding the event from ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor (gated Not(qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies)), so the loss would additionally escape the IRC 165(h)(5)(B) gain-offset cap entirely rather than being limited to /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain. ../isEligible is complete-safe (its own IsComplete/Switch resolves FALSE when ../federallyDeclaredDisaster is unanswered), so it needs no additional IsComplete guard here. THE INSTRUCTION IS SILENT AT EQUALITY. It says $500 when line 10 is "larger" and $100 when it is "smaller"; the equal case is stated nowhere. THE READING TAKEN IS not-larger to $100: the $500 floor is an exception written for the case where the loss exceeds the gains, and an exception does not extend itself to a case its own text omits. The comparison is therefore GreaterThan, not GreaterThanOrEquals, and the reading is pinned at both edges by a boundary pair - multi-event-qualified-disaster-floor-flip-per-event (line 10 EXACTLY equal to the gain sum, so $100) and boundary-qualified-disaster-floor-flip-one-dollar-over (one dollar more, so $500). If the reading is ever corrected, exactly those two fixtures move.
THE INSTRUCTION'S SECOND DISJUNCT, "or if you are reporting a disaster loss, enter $100", NEEDS NO SEPARATE INTAKE: Pub. 547 defines "disaster loss" as a property of the loss itself (a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster occurring in an area eligible for assistance under the Presidential declaration), distinct from QUALIFIED disaster loss (the enumerated IRC 165(h)(5) list); the preceding-year IRC 165(i) deduction the instruction mentions in the next sentence is an ENTITLEMENT a disaster loss confers, not part of its definition. Read that way, a filer whose loss is a plain disaster loss and NOT a qualified one is told to take $100 and "complete the remainder of the form without applying the special rules for qualified disaster losses" - which is exactly what this Switch's final arm already does, because every earlier arm requires ../isQualifiedDisasterLoss and a non-qualified event falls through to False. THE IRC 165(i) PRECEDING-YEAR ELECTION (../writableElectsSection165iPrecedingYearDeduction) DOES NOT FEED THIS FLIP AND THIS FACT DOES NOT READ IT: the election is a separate rule about WHICH RETURN the loss lands on, wired at ../lossAfterReimbursement. An elected event reaches this comparison with a line 10 of 0, which is not larger than any gain sum, so the flip resolves FALSE for it - the same answer it would give a loss of zero, and no floor is applied to nothing.
AT ZERO GAINS THIS FACT IS INERT, which is why the flip moves no dollar on any return that does not have a casualty gain: with line 13 = 0 any positive line 10 is "larger", so the $500 floor stands exactly as it did before this fact existed, and a line 10 of 0 gives 0 on both arms.
UNANSWERED SAFETY, AND IT IS NOT FREE. ../lossAfterReimbursement is NOT complete on every event: the printed form tells a gain filer to "skip lines 5 through 9 for that column", so a gain-only event legitimately leaves FMV blank and line 10 does not resolve. A bare comparison therefore goes Incomplete, and because this Boolean gates the two per-event floor facts the incompleteness would reach Form 4684 line 14 and line 18 - facts that resolve Complete 0 today. The first Switch arm is the guard: when line 10 is not measurable the event STAYS ON THE PATH ITS ATTESTATION PUT IT ON, i.e. the qualified-disaster path, which is exactly where it sat before this gate existed - making the completeness surface of both floor facts byte-identical to their pre-fill surface. The other operands need no guard: ../isQualifiedDisasterLoss, ../isEligible and ../isSectionB are complete-safe gates, and /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain is gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss. THE GUARD ARM (Case 1) DELIBERATELY DOES NOT READ ../isEligible: it fires only when line 10 itself is unmeasurable, and its job is to preserve the pre-fill completeness surface, not to make the final determination - an ineligible event that lands there still resolves 0 on every consumer (../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor via an Incomplete line 10, or, once measurable, ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor's own IsComplete guard).

Fact.Name: Deductible loss after the 100-dollar floor (Form 4684 lines 11-12, eligibility-gated)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 12 = line 10 (this event's loss after reimbursement) minus line 11 (the 100-dollar-per-event floor). If zero or less, 0. GATED on the federally-declared- disaster eligibility (../isEligible): an ineligible event resolves 0 (its loss is not deductible - it could only offset casualty gains, not modelled). The 100-dollar floor uses the ordinary amount; the qualified-disaster 500-dollar floor is on ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor. MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY: an event is on this path or on ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor, never both, because both gates read the same Boolean, ../qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies (not ../isQualifiedDisasterLoss directly - the two agree on every return without a casualty gain, but a qualified-disaster event whose i4684 Line 11 flip sends it to the $100 floor instead belongs HERE, on the ordinary Schedule A line-15 path, per the instruction's own "complete the remainder of the form without applying the special rules for qualified disaster losses"). SECTION B EXCLUSION: an event in EITHER Section B loss column (../isSectionB) is EXCLUDED here too. Section A's $100 floor, its 10%-of-AGI floor and its federally-declared-disaster gate are all personal-use rules ("Losses on business property and income-producing property aren't subject to these rules", 2025 Pub 547, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 15), and a Section B loss leaves on Form 4684 lines 31/38a to Form 4797 line 14 (column (b)(i)) or on lines 32/38b to Schedule A line 16 (column (b)(ii)), never on Schedule A line 15. Without this exclusion the same loss would be deducted twice, once here under rules that do not apply to it. THE GATE IS ../isSectionB AND NOT ../isBusinessOrIncome- Producing, which matters: the (b)(ii) column landed after the (b)(i) one, and a (b)(ii) event whose ../federallyDeclaredDisaster is true passes ../isEligible - it would have been deducted here AND on Schedule A line 16 had the narrower gate been left in place.

Fact.Name: Qualified disaster loss after the 500-dollar floor (Form 4684 lines 11-12, qualified path)
Fact.Description:
Form 4684 line 12 for a QUALIFIED DISASTER LOSS = line 10 (this event's loss after reimbursement) minus line 11 = the 500-DOLLAR per-event floor (2025 i4684 Line 11: "enter $500 on line 11 of the Form 4684 reporting the qualified disaster losses"). If zero or less, 0. Reuses the same per-event loss chain (../lossAfterReimbursement, Form 4684 line 10) as the ordinary path - only the floor differs ($500 vs $100) and, downstream, the 10%-AGI reduction is skipped. This is the per-event input to /netQualifiedDisasterLoss (Form 4684 line 15).
GATED on the single Boolean ../qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies, which carries three conditions: the event is an attested qualified disaster loss (../isQualifiedDisasterLoss - an event that is not takes the ordinary $100/10%-AGI Schedule A path instead, or is ineligible); the event is NOT in either Section B loss column (../isSectionB) - a qualified disaster loss is by definition "an individual's casualty and theft loss of personal-use property" (2025 Pub 547, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 4), which rules out both Section B columns, business property and income-producing property alike, so the exclusion resolves that contradiction to the Section B arm instead of deducting the loss on both; and the $500 floor stands only while this event's line 10 is LARGER than the summed Form 4684 line-4 gains, per i4684 Line 11. With no gain the comparison is against zero and the floor stands unconditionally, so no return without a casualty gain moves.

Fact.Name: Loss NOT attributable to a federally declared disaster, after the 100-dollar floor (Worksheet 1-1 line 1 term)
Fact.Description:
The per-event addend of Worksheet 1-1 line 1, "Add the amounts from line 12 of all Forms 4684 reporting losses NOT attributable to a federally declared disaster". Same printed line 12 arithmetic as ../deductibleLossAfterFloor - line 10 less the $100 per-casualty floor, floored at 0 - applied to the events that fact EXCLUDES: those whose ../isEligible is false. Pub. 547 says so in as many words: "This reduction applies to each total casualty or theft loss, including those losses not attributable to a federally declared disaster that are applied to reduce your personal casualty gains."
WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL. Since the OBBBA/IRC 165(h)(5) regime a non-disaster personal casualty loss is not deductible, and ../deductibleLossAfterFloor zeroes it. IRC 165(h)(5)(B)(i) carves out ONE use for it: the disaster limitation "shall not apply to the portion of the personal casualty loss not attributable to a Federally declared disaster ... to the extent such loss does not exceed such gains". The loss may OFFSET A CASUALTY GAIN and nothing else. The offset is capped taxpayer-wide, not per event, so this fact is the gross per-event term and the cap lives one level up, at /nonDisasterLossAllowedAgainstGain (Worksheet 1-1 line 3).
THE FLOOR IS $100, NOT $500, ALWAYS. The $500 floor is the qualified-disaster floor, and a qualified disaster loss is by definition attributable to a federally declared disaster, so it cannot reach this line.
THREE EXCLUSIONS, each for its own reason. An ELIGIBLE event (../isEligible) belongs on Worksheet 1-1 LINE 2 instead. A SECTION B event is excluded because Section A's floors and its federally-declared-disaster gate are personal-use rules that do not reach business or income-producing property at all ("Losses on business property and income-producing property aren't subject to these rules", 2025 Pub 547). And an event whose ../qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies is true is excluded so that a CONTRADICTORY attestation - qualifiedDisasterLoss true with federallyDeclaredDisaster false or unanswered - cannot be counted BOTH here and in /netQualifiedDisasterLoss. That combination is incoherent on its face and the form has no place for it; the exclusion makes it resolve to the qualified-disaster arm alone rather than deducting the same loss twice (World #1).
AT ZERO GAINS THIS FACT MOVES NO DOLLAR. It is nonzero on any return with an ineligible loss event, but its only consumer caps the total at the gain (/nonDisasterLossAllowedAgainstGain = LesserOf(this total, line 13)), so with line 13 = 0 the cap is 0 and Form 4684 line 14 is unchanged.
UNANSWERED SAFETY IS THE IsComplete LEG ON ../lossAfterReimbursement, AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Line 10 does not resolve on a gain-only event, because the printed form tells that filer to "skip lines 5 through 9 for that column" and leave FMV blank - and a gain-only event is NOT eligible and NOT Section B, so without the guard it falls straight into this fact's computing arm. An unmeasured line 10 resolves 0 here, which is the conservative direction: it withholds an offset against the gain rather than inventing one.

Fact.Name: Section B loss before reimbursement (Form 4684 line 26, incl. its totally-destroyed Note)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 26 = "Enter the smaller of line 20 or line 25" (adjusted basis or the decline in fair market value), EXCEPT under the line's own Note - "If the property was totally destroyed by casualty or lost from theft, enter on line 26 the amount from line 20" - in which case it is the adjusted basis outright (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2). Section B lines 20, 23, 24 and 25 are Section A lines 2, 5, 6 and 7 verbatim, so this reuses ../adjustedBasis and ../fmvDecrease unchanged; the Note is the ONE place the two sections' arithmetic differs, and it is why this is a separate fact rather than a reuse of ../lossBeforeReimbursement (which implements Section A line 8 and must not move). A SECTION C EVENT IS EXCLUDED HERE TOO, and the exclusion is what keeps this fact Complete for that filer. Form 4684 Section C line 51 says "Do not complete lines 19-27 for this loss" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3), so a Ponzi-type safe-harbor filer answers no ../adjustedBasis, ../fmvBefore or ../fmvAfter at all; without the ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft exclusion on BOTH Section B arms this fact would read an unanswered basis and resolve Result.Incomplete, taking /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss and Schedule A with it. The Section C amount enters at ../sectionBCasualtyLoss (line 28) instead, which is exactly where the printed form puts it. GATED on ../isSectionB: a Section A event resolves 0 here. THE GATE IS THE UNION OF BOTH SECTION B COLUMNS, because lines 20 to 28 are printed ABOVE the Part II column split and are therefore shared by column (b)(i) and column (b)(ii) alike - the columns first diverge at ../sectionBLossColumnBi and ../sectionBLossColumnBii, which split this chain's output rather than re-running it. The gate is also what keeps the arm complete-safe in the destroyed case - a totally-destroyed or stolen property has no meaningful "fair market value after", and the true-Note arm never reads ../fmvDecrease at all, so an unanswered ../fmvBefore or ../fmvAfter does not make this Result.Incomplete for that filer.

Fact.Name: Section B casualty or theft loss for this event (Form 4684 lines 27-28, both columns)
Fact.Description:
Form 4684 SECTION B line 27 = "Subtract line 21 from line 26. If zero or less, enter -0-" (line 26 minus insurance or other reimbursement), which line 28 then totals across the event's property columns: "Casualty or theft loss. Add the amounts on line 27. Enter the total here and on line 29 or line 34" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2). Because this module models ONE property per event (see /casualtyEvents), line 28 equals line 27 and the two lines are one fact - the same collapse Section A's ../lossAfterReimbursement makes for lines 9 and 10.
NO $100 FLOOR AND NO 10%-OF-AGI FLOOR APPLY: those are Section A lines 11 and 17, and "Losses on business property and income-producing property aren't subject to these rules" (2025 Pub 547, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 15). NO FEDERALLY-DECLARED-DISASTER GATE APPLIES either: that limitation is written for "casualty losses of personal-use property" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p547.pdf, page 4), so ../isEligible is deliberately NOT read on this arm. It resolves 0 for a Section A event, via ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement's own gate.
THE SECTION C ARM: for an event where ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft is true this fact IS ../ponziDeductibleTheftLoss - Form 4684 Section C line 51, taken whole, with no line 21 reimbursement subtracted, because line 51 says "Include this amount on line 28 of Section B, Part I. Do not complete lines 19-27 for this loss" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3) and lines 21 and 27 are among the lines not completed. The Section C recoveries (lines 48 and 49) are the reimbursement analogue and are already subtracted inside line 51.
BOTH COLUMNS SHARE THIS FACT. Lines 20 to 28 are printed above the Part II column split, so this is the whole Section B per-event loss regardless of which column the event sits in; the split happens once, downstream, at ../sectionBLossColumnBi and ../sectionBLossColumnBii, which is why widening the gate to ../isSectionB does not duplicate any arithmetic.
A LOSS IS POSITIVE HERE, matching the form: both loss columns are printed with parentheses around their entries, and the sign flip to a net "(loss)" happens once, at /sectionBNetGainOrLoss (lines 31 and 38a) - the Schedule A line 16 exit (/incomeProducingCasualtyLoss) does NOT flip, because line 16 is a positive deduction column.
THE LOSS-SUSPENSION CASE LEADS, ahead of the Section C arm. When ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear is true this fact is a COMPLETE $0: the loss was already deducted on an earlier year's return (IRC 165(a) allows a deduction for a loss sustained "during the taxable year" - once), or the IRC 165(i) election deems the casualty to have occurred in the preceding year (165(i)(2)). Neither rule is written for personal-use property: 165(a) carries no personal/business restriction at all, and 165(i)(1) reaches "any loss occurring in a disaster area and attributable to a federally declared disaster". THIS is Section B's single post-reimbursement, post-special-rules choke point: both Part II columns (../sectionBLossColumnBi and ../sectionBLossColumnBii) read it and nothing else, so zeroing it once empties Form 4797 line 14 and Schedule A line 16 coherently and no leg needs its own copy of the gate. It is also the ONLY point that reaches the Section C population, since line 51 bypasses ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement entirely; hence the Case LEADS. WHICH HALF OF THE GATE REACHES A PONZI EVENT: the already-deducted half only, since IRC 165(i) is gated on ../isEligible, the federally-declared-disaster attestation, which a theft-only Section C event need not carry. ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement and ../ponziDeductibleTheftLoss are both UNTOUCHED - the measurements still compute, it is line 28 that is empty on THIS return. The When reads ../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear BARE and that is correct rather than an oversight: it is COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT (an Any over two complete-safe aliases, neither of which reads a writable bare).
THE IRC 280A(c)(5) CEILING, a THIRD leading Case ahead of the ordinary catchall: a home used for business or rented out (the non-Schedule-C half of the i4684 "Home Used for Business or Rented Out" fork - the Schedule-C/Form 8829 half is a named gap for a successor unit) caps the deductible loss at the gross income the use produced (../grossIncomeFromBusinessOrRentalUse), LesserOf-style against the same ordinary computation the catchall Case performs. THE CAP IS TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE, NOT EXACT: 280A(c)(5)(B) further reduces the ceiling by other deductions already allocable to the same use, which this direct intake does not ask for; the built ceiling (gross income alone) is therefore never SMALLER than the true statutory one.

Fact.Name: This event's Section B loss in column (b)(i), trade/business/rental/royalty property
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section B Part II, the column-(b)(i) share of this event's line 28 loss. Part II carries every Section B loss into ONE of two loss columns - "(i) Trade, business, rental, or royalty property" or "(ii) Income-producing property" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2) - on lines 29/30 (held one year or less) and 34/35 (held more than one year). This is the (b)(i) column; ../sectionBLossColumnBii is the other one. Together they partition ../sectionBCasualtyLoss, so no loss is counted twice and none is dropped. THE TIE-BREAK, which is the only thing this fact decides. The two attestations describe ONE property, so at most one should be true; if a filer answers BOTH true the printed form gives no rule, and this build resolves it to column (b)(ii) - i.e. this fact is 0 and ../sectionBLossColumnBii carries the whole loss. That is the conservative resolution, not an arbitrary one: column (b)(i) exits to Form 4797 line 14 and thence Schedule 1 line 4, an ABOVE-THE-LINE ordinary loss that needs no itemizing, while column (b)(ii) exits to Schedule A line 16, an itemized deduction worth nothing to a filer who does not itemize (/claimsItemizedDeductions is an attestation, not an automatic greater-of). Resolving the contradiction toward (b)(ii) can therefore only reduce the deduction, never inflate it. The alternative - refusing the return with a knockout - was not taken because an under-stated deduction is the World-#1-safe direction and the /netQualifiedDisasterLoss precedent builds rather than refuses in exactly this situation. A SECTION C EVENT IS EXCLUDED FROM THIS COLUMN OUTRIGHT, even if its filer also answered ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing true. The Schedule A line 16 instruction's closed list names the destination in terms: "Casualty and theft losses of income-producing property (including losses from financial scams) from Form 4684, lines 32 and 38b" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sca.pdf, page 11) - lines 32 and 38b are the column (b)(ii) totals, and a Ponzi-type investment loss is the financial scam that parenthesis names. Sending it down the (b)(i) door instead would put it on Form 4797 line 14 and thence Schedule 1 line 4, ABOVE the line and with no itemizing required: the same taxpayer-favourable error the (b)(ii) tie-break above exists to avoid, and here the printed instruction settles it rather than a tie-break. NAMED NARROWING: a claimant whose Ponzi-type investment really was a trade or business asset gets the itemized destination anyway, which is never larger. AN EMPLOYEE-USE EVENT IS EXCLUDED FROM THIS COLUMN OUTRIGHT, on ../usedInPerformingServicesAsEmployee, and unlike the Section C exclusion above it does NOT redirect to ../sectionBLossColumnBii - it is simply barred. The 2025 i4684 Caution under Section B is unconditional: "business casualty and theft losses of property used in performing services as an employee cannot be deducted or applied in the netting process to offset gains" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 10). Column (b)(i) had no test for this at all before this exclusion landed, so an employee-use-property filer who answered the (b)(ii) attestation FALSE (correctly, since the property was never income-producing property) could still have the loss deducted in full through THIS column instead of barred, an over- deduction the (b)(ii) column's own employee carve-out cannot reach because it never sees a (b)(i)-attested event. Resolves 0 for every Section A event through ../sectionBCasualtyLoss's own gate, and 0 on every event that predates the (b)(ii) column since ../isIncomeProducingProperty is Complete false there - so this fact equals ../sectionBCasualtyLoss on the whole existing corpus. /sectionBNetGainOrLoss does not read this fact directly: it reads Form 4684 lines 31 and 38a, the holding-period split of this column (../shortTermSectionBLossColumnBi and ../longTermSectionBLossColumnBi), one step further from the total than this fact but byte-identical to it on the whole existing corpus.

Fact.Name: This event's Section B loss in column (b)(ii), income-producing property
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section B Part II, the column-(b)(ii) share of this event's line 28 loss - the other half of the partition ../sectionBLossColumnBi describes. Carries the whole loss whenever ../isIncomeProducingProperty is true, INCLUDING the case where ../isBusinessOrIncomeProducing is also true (the tie-break argued at ../sectionBLossColumnBi). 0 otherwise, so every event that predates this column - and every Section A event - resolves 0 and every pre-existing scenario is byte-identical. CARRIES EVERY SECTION C EVENT TOO, on the ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft limb, whatever ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty says - the argument is at ../sectionBLossColumnBi and it rests on the Schedule A line 16 closed list naming "losses from financial scams" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sca.pdf, page 11). AN EMPLOYEE-USE EVENT IS EXCLUDED FROM THIS COLUMN TOO, the same bar ../sectionBLossColumnBi already applies on ../usedInPerformingServicesAsEmployee. Lines 32 and 38b both end "(Do not include any loss on property used as an employee.)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2) - a bar printed on the column's own destination lines, not merely the instruction's Caution, and it names no exception for the tie-break or the Section C limb. Before this bar, a filer who contradictorily attested BOTH ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing and ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty true, plus ../writableUsedInPerformingServicesAsEmployee true, had the loss barred from column (b)(i) but carried through unbarred here by the tie-break's own isIncomeProducingProperty leg - the exact over-deduction this exclusion closes. A filer who answers ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty true and never answers ../writableIsBusinessOrIncomeProducing true is unaffected: the employee-use question is only ever asked on a (b)(i)-attested event, so ../usedInPerformingServicesAsEmployee stays its complete-safe FALSE there and this conjunct changes nothing. Feeds /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss (Form 4684 lines 32 and 38b), which exits to Schedule A line 16, NOT to Form 4797 line 14.

Fact.Name: This event's Section B gain if it is SHORT-TERM (Form 4684 line 29, column (c))
Fact.Description: ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is false, else 0. The per-event addend of /sectionBShortTermGain, which is Form 4684 line 30 column (c). The instruction says which cell in as many words: "On line 29, enter the part of line 22 that is from property held for 1 year or less." NOT GATED ON THE GAIN ITSELF, deliberately, and the reason is the mirror of ../shortTermSectionANetAmount's: ../heldMoreThanOneYear resolves a complete FALSE on every return with no Section B gain, so on those returns this fact is simply ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount - which is 0 there because no event has one - and the requiredness lives once, at /anySectionBCasualtyGain.

Fact.Name: This event's Section B gain if it is LONG-TERM (Form 4684 line 34, column (c))
Fact.Description:
../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is true, else 0 - the exact mirror of ../shortTermSectionBGain, so the two partition ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount. The per-event addend of /sectionBLongTermGain (line 36). "On line 34, enter the part of line 22 that is from property held for more than 1 year."
THE RECAPTURE CARVE-OUT: i4684 Line 33 sends a long-term gain on depreciable business property through Form 4797 Part III "instead of Form 4684, line 34" for the section 1245, 1250 and 1254 classes - the Switch below carries a ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies arm, tested before the holding-period arm, that returns 0 for such an event, and this cell is 0.00 against an 18,000 gain on those classes. The gain that leaves here for those classes arrives instead as /casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture (ordinary, Form 4797 line 31 to Part II line 13) plus /sectionBCasualtyGainsFromForm4797Line32 (line 33); the two sum back to ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount exactly ONLY where the IRC 1245(b)(4)(B) involuntary-conversion term is zero - on a section 1033 election with a non-section-1245 replacement, ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture is capped at the recognized gain plus the replacement's fair market value and can exceed the recognized gain, in which case ../sectionBPartIIILine32Remainder is floored at 0 rather than going negative. Sections 1252 and 1255 still land the whole gain here, which is item (18) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain.

Fact.Name: Section 1245 property attested on this casualty event (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsSection1245CasualtyProperty when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means the Form 4797 Part III route does not apply, which leaves the event exactly where it was before arm (12) landed. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, and it is not decoration - the alias exists for a measured reason: reading a writable Boolean BARE inside a <When> makes the whole Switch Placeholder on every event that leaves it unanswered, and the Placeholder travels as far as /casualtyLossDeduction.

Fact.Name: Depreciation allowed or allowable on this casualty property (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
FORM 4797 PART III LINE 22, "Depreciation (or depletion) allowed or allowable", carried to line 25a (the section 1245 block) and to the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 1 through ../sectionBUnrecapturedSection1250GainComponent. An answered negative is floored at $0 before those recapture consumers; the writable's Limit Min declaration is not enforced by resolution.
A REQUIREDNESS ALIAS ON ONE POPULATION, THE ../heldMoreThanOneYear IDIOM ("unanswered means REFUSED, but only where the answer changes a number"): an event whose gain routes through Part III (../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies) and which attests section 1245 or section 1250 reads the writable BARE, so an unanswered line 22 is Result.Incomplete and the return stops. A section-1254-only event is NOT asked, because line 28a and line 28b never read line 22 on this collection. Everywhere else - every Section A event, every Section B event with no gain, every event attesting no modeled class - the answer defaults to $0, which is what keeps the Placeholder off /casualtyLossDeduction on the whole committed corpus.

Fact.Name: Section 1250 property attested on this casualty event (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsSection1250CasualtyProperty when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern, the ../isSection1245CasualtyProperty idiom verbatim). Unanswered means the Form 4797 Part III line-26 block does not apply, which leaves the event exactly where it was before item (18) landed. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, and for the reason its section 1245 sibling records: reading a writable Boolean BARE inside a <When> makes the whole Switch Placeholder on every event that leaves it unanswered, and the Placeholder travels as far as /casualtyLossDeduction.

Fact.Name: Fair market value of the replacement property that is not section 1245 property (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
THE IRC 1245(b)(4)(B) TERM OF THE INVOLUNTARY-CONVERSION RECAPTURE CAP, and it is a REQUIREDNESS alias rather than a complete-safe one. On an event that attests section 1245 property AND carries an answered section 1033 election - which is exactly where the question is askable - this reads ../writableFmvOfNonSection1245ReplacementProperty BARE, so a blank leaves it Result.Incomplete and the return STOPS. Everywhere else it resolves a Complete $0, which leaves the cap at (b)(4)(A) alone, i.e. the recognized gain - byte-for-byte the arithmetic ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture carried before this fill.
WHY REQUIREDNESS RATHER THAN A $0 DEFAULT. A $0 default is fail-OPEN in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction, and the cost is not hypothetical: on a return whose section 1033 election postpones the WHOLE gain (replacement cost equal to the reimbursement, so the recognized gain is $0), a $5,000 answer recaptures $5,000 of ordinary income onto Form 4797 line 13 and line 31, and the SAME return with the question merely unasked recaptures nothing - an unasked question deleting $5,000 from a printed line. That is the direction this collection's own ../writableDeclinedToFileReimbursementClaim already refuses in as many words, and it is the same posture ../lossAfterReimbursement takes for its own IRC 165(h)(4)(E) requiredness gate. IT DOES NOT REOPEN THE COLLECTION-QUANTIFIER TRAP. A writable Dollar read BARE with no guard would make ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture a Placeholder on every Section A event that leaves it unanswered, and the Placeholder travels to /casualtyLossDeduction. The guard above prevents that only because BOTH its operands are complete-safe, so it resolves a complete FALSE rather than an Incomplete on every event outside the asked-when.

Fact.Name: Additional depreciation after 1975 on this casualty property (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableCasualtyAdditionalDepreciationAfter1975 when answered, else $0 (the IsComplete pattern) - Form 4797 Part III line 26a, carried into line 26b. Zero recaptures nothing, which is the outcome an unattested event already had, and it is also the printed answer for a straight-line or post-1986 MACRS property.

Fact.Name: This event's Form 4797 Part III line 26g section 1250 ordinary recapture (into line 31)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 26g, "Add lines 26b, 26e, and 26f", for a CASUALTY disposition. It is LINE 26b ALONE and the two dropped terms are dropped by POPULATION, not by convenience - the same reading the sale-side twin form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/section1250OrdinaryRecaptureContribution takes and for the same two reasons. Line 26f is the "Section 291 amount (corporations only)" and this dictionary files individual returns. Line 26e is "Enter the smaller of line 26c or 26d" and line 26d is "Additional depreciation after 1969 and before 1976" - pre-1976-era property, outside the TY2025 population entirely - so line 26d is 0 and line 26e is min(26c, 0) = 0 whatever line 26c's sign is, which is why line 26c needs no fact either. LINE 26b IS "Applicable percentage multiplied by the smaller of line 24 or line 26a" = 100% x min(line 24, line 26a). Line 24 for a casualty is ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount, exactly as it is for the section 1245 block: Part III line 20 is the Form 4684 line-21 reimbursement and line 23 is the Form 4684 line-20 adjusted basis, so their difference is the figure Form 4684 line 22 already computes. Line 26a is ../casualtyAdditionalDepreciationAfter1975. THE APPLICABLE PERCENTAGE IS 100% AND IS NOT A FACT, the sale side's posture unchanged. IRC 1250(a)(1)(B)(v) sets it - "in the case of all other section 1250 property, 100 percent" - the residual clause under which every disposition an individual reports on this form falls; clauses (i) through (iv) are pre-1976-era low-income housing. The instructions say the same in one line: "Generally, use 100% as the percentage for this line." NO GreaterOf FLOOR IS NEEDED HERE and its absence is deliberate rather than an omission: the sale-side twin floors line 24 at zero because a SALE item's line 24 may be negative, but this fact is only ever evaluated behind ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies, which requires ../hasSectionBCasualtyGain, so line 24 is strictly positive on every event that reaches the arithmetic. That is the same reason ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture's section 1245 arm carries no floor either. THE CLASS PRECEDENCE IS 1245 BEFORE 1250, the sale side's order (form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/ordinaryRecaptureContribution tests its section 1245 arm FIRST), written here as an explicit $0 arm rather than as Switch position, because THIS FACT IS SUMMED ON ITS OWN by /casualtyPartIIISection1250OrdinaryRecapture. If a double-attested event contributed line 25b to line 31 and line 26g to the section 1250 legibility total, the two totals would not tie. The precedence keeps them tied by construction: an event attesting BOTH classes is a section 1245 event everywhere. WHERE THE SALE SIDE REFUSES A CONTRADICTION, THIS SIDE ORDERS IT. form4797 has ../hasContradictorySection1254ClassAttestation and knocks a multi-class item out of ../isInScope; no equivalent refusal is written on /casualtyEvents, because a refusal fact on this collection would have to be Complete on every Section A event to avoid the completeness contagion the (12) fill measured, and because the whole population is already refused by /knockoutCasualtyGain. The precedence direction is the conservative one for a truthfully entered pair: line 25b (all the depreciation) is never smaller than line 26g (only the excess over straight line) for the same property. 0 whenever the route does not apply or the event is not a section 1250 event, so this fact is Complete $0 on the whole committed corpus.

Fact.Name: Section 1254 property attested on this casualty event (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsSection1254CasualtyProperty when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern, the ../isSection1245CasualtyProperty idiom verbatim). Unanswered means the Form 4797 Part III line-28 block does not apply. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, for the reason its two siblings record: a bare writable Boolean inside a <When> makes the whole Switch Placeholder on every event that leaves it unanswered.

Fact.Name: Section 1254 expenditures and depletion on this casualty property (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 28a, carried into line 28b. Zero recaptures nothing, which is the outcome an unattested event already had. [2026-08-25, unit form4684-part-iii-casualty-intake-obligations. THIS FACT IS NO LONGER A BARE IsComplete PASS-THROUGH and the sentence it used to open with - "../writableCasualty Section1254Expenses when answered, else $0 (the IsComplete pattern)" - is superseded rather than deleted, because it is still exactly what the second and third Cases do. IT IS NOW THE FORK i4797 "Line 28a" prints: when ../casualtyPropertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987 is true the line is ../casualtySection1254ExpensesPre1987, the section 263(c) intangible drilling and development costs ALONE; otherwise it is the post-1986 figure, the section 263/616/617 deductions plus section 611 depletion. The pre-1987 arm is FIRST because the post-1986 arm is an unconditional pass-through that would otherwise swallow an event answering both fields. Item (21) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain.]

Fact.Name: Property placed in service before 1987 attested on this casualty event (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableCasualtyPropertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987 when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern, the ../isSection1254CasualtyProperty idiom verbatim). Unanswered means "placed in service after 1986", which routes Form 4797 line 28a to the post-1986 question ../casualtySection1254Expenses - the behaviour this module had before item (21) was built, unchanged for every event that does not answer.

Fact.Name: Section 263(c) intangible drilling and development costs on this pre-1987 casualty property (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableCasualtySection1254ExpensesPre1987 when answered, else $0 (the IsComplete pattern) - the PRE-1987 leg of Form 4797 Part III line 28a, carried into line 28b through ../casualtySection1254Expenses. Zero recaptures nothing, which is the outcome an unattested event already had.

Fact.Name: This event's Form 4797 Part III line 28b section 1254 ordinary recapture (into line 31)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 28b, "Enter the smaller of line 24 or 28a", for a CASUALTY disposition: the smaller of this event's total gain and the section 263/616/617 expenditures and section 611 depletion the taxpayer DEDUCTED instead of capitalizing. IT IS THE STATUTE'S OWN LESSER-OF, not a form-only convention, which is why this line needs no applicable percentage the way lines 26b, 27b and 29a do. IRC 1254(a)(1): "If any section 1254 property is disposed of, the lesser of- (A) the aggregate amount of- (i) expenditures which have been deducted by the taxpayer or any person under section 263, 616, or 617 ... and (ii) the deductions for depletion under section 611 which reduced the adjusted basis of such property, or (B) the excess of- (i) in the case of- (I) a sale, exchange, or involuntary conversion, the amount realized ... over (ii) the adjusted basis of such property, shall be treated as gain which is ordinary income." Leg (A) is line 28a; leg (B) is line 24. CLAUSE (B)(i)(I) NAMES THE INVOLUNTARY CONVERSION EXPLICITLY, which is how a casualty enters this section at all. LINE 24 FOR A CASUALTY IS ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount, the same identity the section 1245 and section 1250 blocks use on this collection: Part III line 20 is the Form 4684 line-21 reimbursement and line 23 is the Form 4684 line-20 adjusted basis. NO GreaterOf FLOOR, deliberately: this fact is only ever evaluated behind ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies, which requires ../hasSectionBCasualtyGain, so line 24 is strictly positive wherever the arithmetic runs. The sale-side twin floors because a SALE item's line 24 may be negative. THE CLASS PRECEDENCE IS 1245 > 1250 > 1254, written here as two explicit $0 arms for the reason ../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture gives: this fact is summed on its own by /casualtyPartIIISection1254OrdinaryRecapture, and without the precedence a double-attested event would put dollars in that total that line 31 never sees. THE SALE SIDE DOES THE OPPOSITE for this class - form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/hasContradictorySection1254ClassAttestation REFUSES a multi-class section 1254 item outright, because line 28b is ordered against neither line 25b nor line 26g by anything printed. That refusal is not available on /casualtyEvents (a refusal fact here would have to be Complete on every Section A event, and the whole population is already refused by /knockoutCasualtyGain), so this build ORDERS what the sale side REFUSES, and the divergence is stated rather than hidden. It is a DIVERGENCE, not a correction: for a truthfully entered single-class event the two agree exactly, and no committed case attests more than one class. THE 1245-BEFORE-1254 PRECEDENCE UNDER-STATES LINE 31 RELATIVE TO THE PRINTED FORM, and that is a real residual rather than a tie-break: line 31 adds "lines 25b, 26g, 27c, 28b, and 29b" WITHIN one property column, and sections 1245 and 1254 are NOT mutually exclusive the way 1245 and 1250 are (i4797 "Line 26" defines section 1250 property as "depreciable real property (other than section 1245 property)" - an explicit exclusion the section 1254 definition has no counterpart to), so a property that is both should report 25b AND 28b. The evidence that the blocks are ADDITIVE rather than alternative is line 29b's own instruction, which is the ONLY one that reduces for another provision: "If any part of the gain shown on line 24 is treated as ordinary income under sections 1231 through 1254 (for example, section 1252), enter the smaller of (a) line 24 reduced by the part of the gain treated as ordinary income under the other provision, or (b) line 29a." Lines 25b, 26g and 28b carry no such reduction. Taking only the higher-precedence block therefore UNDER-states ordinary income - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the same direction as items (18) and (19). IT IS DELIBERATE: the alternative is a refusal /casualtyEvents cannot carry, and the sale side REFUSES the same combination rather than adding it, so neither side computes the printed sum today. Named as item (18)'s own residual on the rebody contract. 0 whenever the route does not apply or the event is not a section 1254 event.

Fact.Name: Section 1252 farm land attested on this casualty event (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsSection1252CasualtyProperty when answered, else FALSE (the IsComplete pattern, the ../isSection1254CasualtyProperty idiom verbatim). Unanswered means "not section 1252 property", which is where every event stood before this fill, and that is what keeps this fill ADDITIVE across the committed corpus.

Fact.Name: Full years the farm land was held before the casualty (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableCasualtyFarmlandFullYearsHeld when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern). The IRC 1252(a)(3) band index that ../casualtySection1252Line27b switches on. ZERO IS THE 100 PERCENT BAND, which is the LARGEST recapture and therefore the taxpayer-ADVERSE reading of an unanswered count. That is why an unanswered count defaults here instead of refusing: a refusal buys nothing where the default already runs against the filer, and the sale-side twin ../farmlandFullYearsHeld took the same posture for the same reason. IT DOES NOT LET AN UNANSWERED EVENT SLIP THE EXPENSES GATE: 0 is under 9, so ../casualtySection1252Expenses still reads its writable BARE on an event that answers neither intake.

Fact.Name: Soil, water and land clearing expenses on this casualty farm land (complete-safe outside the bands, REQUIRED inside them)
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 27a, carried into line 27b. IT IS A REQUIREDNESS ALIAS ON ONE POPULATION and a complete-safe $0 everywhere else - the ../casualtyDepreciationAllowed idiom, not the module's usual bare IsComplete pass-through. An event whose gain actually routes through Part III (../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies), which attests section 1252, and which sits INSIDE the percentage bands (fewer than 9 full years held) reads the writable BARE, so an unanswered line 27a is Result.Incomplete and the return stops. Everywhere else - every Section A event, every Section B event with no gain, every event attesting no modeled class, and every attested event in the tenth year or later - the $0 stands, which is what keeps the Placeholder off /casualtyLossDeduction on the whole committed corpus. WHY REQUIREDNESS RATHER THAN A REFUSAL FACT. The sale side spends a refusal on this (form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/hasUnansweredSection1252ExpensesGain); this collection cannot, because a refusal fact here would have to be Complete on every Section A event or the Placeholder travels. The DIRECTION is the sale side's and it is why an answer is demanded at all: unanswered-is-zero would give zero section 1252 recapture and send the whole gain to Part I, where it can become long-term capital gain - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, so it cannot be a silent default. THE STAND-DOWN CONJUNCT IS PRINTED, NOT REASONED, and it is what makes this gate narrower than its section 1255 sibling: "Skip line 27 if you dispose of such farmland during the 10th or later year after you acquired it", and IRC 1252(a)(3) gives 0 percent from ten years on. At 9 or more full years line 27b is zero whatever line 27a holds, so an unanswered figure cannot move a number and refusing would refuse a filer the instructions excuse from the line altogether. AN UNANSWERED YEAR COUNT DOES NOT ESCAPE THE GATE: ../casualtyFarmlandFullYearsHeld reads 0, which is under 9. The narrow arm needs an ANSWERED count of 9 or more. NO CYCLE: ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies reads ../isSectionB, the five class attestations, ../hasSectionBCasualtyGain and ../heldMoreThanOneYear, none of which reads this fact.

Fact.Name: Line 27a multiplied by the IRC 1252(a)(3) applicable percentage, for a casualty (Form 4797 Part III line 27b)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 27b, "Line 27a multiplied by applicable percentage. See instructions", for a CASUALTY or theft disposition. THE ONE PLACE ON THIS COLLECTION WHERE AN AGE DISCOUNT IS COMPUTED rather than carried in: line 26b's percentage is the constant 100 percent, line 28b has no percentage at all, line 29a arrives with its percentage already applied by the filer, and this line is the exception - which is exactly the division of labour the sale side's ../section1252Line27b already runs. THE TABLE, band by band, from IRC 1252(a)(3) with the instructions' wording beside it. The driver is ../casualtyFarmlandFullYearsHeld, the WHOLE years between acquisition and the casualty, and each band is exactly one value of that count because every band boundary is an anniversary: 0 to 4 full years is "Within 5 years after the date it was acquired" and takes 100 percent; 5 is "Within the sixth year after it was acquired", 80 percent; 6 is the seventh year, 60 percent; 7 is the eighth year, 40 percent; 8 is the ninth year, 20 percent; 9 or more is the tenth year or later, 0 percent. THE TENTH-YEAR BAND IS THE INSTRUCTIONS' AND NOT THE STATUTE'S, and the gap is named rather than papered over - the same reading the sale side took, re-derived here against the same two sources. IRC 1252(a)(3)'s table runs "Within the ninth year" straight to "10 years or more years after it was acquired", leaving the TENTH year (9 full years held, but under 10) unlisted, while subsection (a)(1) applies the section only to farm land "held for less than 10 years" - so the statute alone leaves the tenth-year disposition inside the section with no percentage. The instructions close it: "Skip line 27 if you dispose of such farmland during the 10th or later year after you acquired it." This fact follows the instructions and gives the tenth year 0 percent, which is what skipping the line means arithmetically. The alternative - carrying the ninth year's 20 percent into the tenth - has no printed support and would recapture where the form prints no entry. WRITTEN AS DESCENDING THRESHOLDS, not as equality tests, so an out-of-range count cannot fall through: 15 full years takes the same 0 percent arm as 9, and the final arm is the 100 percent band, which is where an unanswered count lands through ../casualtyFarmlandFullYearsHeld's zero. NOT CAPPED AGAINST LINE 24 HERE. Line 27c applies the only cap the form draws. NOT GATED ON THE CLASS OR ON THE ROUTE, deliberately: this fact is pure arithmetic over two complete-safe inputs, and ../sectionBSection1252OrdinaryRecapture carries every gate. On an event that attests no class both inputs are 0 and this resolves a Complete $0.

Fact.Name: This event's Form 4797 Part III line 27c section 1252 ordinary recapture (into line 31)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 27c, "Enter the smaller of line 24 or 27b", for a CASUALTY disposition: the smaller of this event's total gain and the age-discounted share of the section 175 soil and water conservation deductions. IT IS THE STATUTE'S OWN LOWER-OF. IRC 1252(a)(1): "if farm land which the taxpayer has held for less than 10 years is disposed of, the lower of- (A) the applicable percentage of the aggregate of the deductions allowed under section 175 ... or (B) the excess of- (i) the amount realized (in the case of a sale, exchange, or involuntary conversion) ... over (ii) the adjusted basis of such land, shall be treated as ordinary income." Fact.Name: This event's Form 4797 Part III ordinary recapture, all modeled classes (line 25b, 26g, 28b or 27c, plus line 29b, into line 31, thence Part II line 13)

THE GAIN IS THE RECOGNIZED ONE, not the realized one: ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount is already net of the section 1033 postponement and every other measure arm, so a gain wholly postponed under section 1033 recaptures nothing here. That is the right order - IRC 1245(a)(1) recaptures "the amount by which the lower of (A) the recomputed basis of the property, or (B)(i) in the case of a sale, exchange, or involuntary conversion, the amount realized ... exceeds the adjusted basis of such property", and section 1033 acts on the amount realized before this section sees it. [CORRECTED 2026-08-25, fix round, beside the sentence above rather than over it, because THE LAST CLAUSE IS WRONG ON THE LAW even though the arithmetic it defends is right. SECTION 1033 DOES NOT REDUCE THE AMOUNT REALIZED - it defers RECOGNITION of the gain; the amount realized on the conversion is what it always was. The rule that actually limits the recapture on an involuntary conversion is IRC 1245(b)(4): "If property is disposed of and gain (determined without regard to this section) is not recognized in whole or in part under section 1031 or 1033, then the amount of gain taken into account by the transferor under subsection (a)(1) shall not exceed the sum of - (A) the amount of gain recognized on such disposition (determined without regard to this section), plus (B) the fair market value of property acquired which is not section 1245 property and which is not taken into account under subparagraph (A)." SO THE CAP IS (b)(4)(A) PLUS (b)(4)(B), and reading ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount - the RECOGNIZED gain - as the line-24 operand implements (b)(4)(A) exactly: a gain wholly postponed under section 1033 recognizes nothing, so the (A) term is 0 and the recapture is 0. THE (B) TERM IS NOT COLLECTED, and that is a real residual rather than a rounding: where the replacement property is NOT section 1245 property - a filer who replaces destroyed equipment with a building, say - (b)(4)(B) adds its fair market value to the cap, so this fact can UNDER-state the ordinary recapture. The direction is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the same direction as items (12) and (18), and it is named as item (19) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain. It cannot be reached today: /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain.] The section 1245 arm is LesserOf( the (a)(1) amount, the (b)(4) cap ), where the (a)(1) amount is LesserOf(../casualtyGainAmount, ../casualtyDepreciationAllowed) - the REALIZED gain, because 1245(a)(1)(B)(i) says "in the case of a sale, exchange, or involuntary conversion, the amount realized" and the flush text recognizes the result "notwithstanding any other provision of this subtitle" - and the cap is Add(../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount, ../fmvOfNonSection1245ReplacementProperty). The (B) term is collected as ../writableFmvOfNonSection1245ReplacementProperty with the complete-safe alias ../fmvOfNonSection1245ReplacementProperty. The residual is the other classes: sections 1250 (IRC 1250(d)(4)(A), a GREATER-OF with two uncollected sub-terms), 1254 (imported through 1254(b)(1); 26 CFR 1.1254-2(c) is NOT vendored) and 1252/1255. 0 whenever ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies is false, which is every event that does not attest section 1245 property - so this fact is Complete $0 on the whole corpus. [2026-08-25, unit form4684-part-iii-other-recapture-classes, beside the paragraphs above rather than over them. THIS FACT IS NO LONGER LINE 25b - IT IS A CLASS SWITCH over line 25b, line 26g and line 28b, the same shape form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/ordinaryRecaptureContribution has carried on the sale side since 2026-08-17. The first paragraph above describes the SECTION 1245 ARM, which is unchanged in arithmetic and in operands; the section 1250 arm is ../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture and the section 1254 arm is ../sectionBSection1254OrdinaryRecapture, each of which carries its own statute, its own involuntary-conversion limit and its own line identity. THE PRECEDENCE IS 1245 > 1250 > 1254, the sale side's order. "which is every event that does not attest section 1245 property" IS NOW FALSE as a description of the $0 population: it is every event that attests NONE of the three modeled classes. The Complete $0 claim on the committed corpus is unchanged and still true - no committed scenario answers any class attestation. THE (b)(4)-STYLE INVOLUNTARY-CONVERSION LIMIT IS TAKEN PER CLASS, not inherited from the section 1245 paragraph above: IRC 1250(d)(4)(A) for the section 1250 arm and IRC 1254(b)(1)'s "rules similar to ... the rules of subsections (b) and (c) of section 1245" for the section 1254 arm. Each arm's own fact quotes its own subsection, and each names the term it does not collect. Item (19) of the rebody contract now covers all three.] LINE 31 ADDS LINE 29b TO THE OTHER BLOCKS. This fact is now the sum of ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecaptureBeforeSection1255 (the 1245 > 1250 > 1254 > 1252 class Switch, one block per event) and ../sectionBSection1255OrdinaryRecapture (line 29b). Fact.Name: This event's Form 4797 Part III line 32 remainder, returning on Form 4684 line 33
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 32, "Subtract line 31 from line 30. Enter the portion from casualty or theft on Form 4684, line 33. Enter the portion from other than casualty or theft on Form 4797, line 6" - this event's part of it, which is by construction the CASUALTY portion, so it goes to Form 4684 line 33 and NEVER to Form 4797 line 6. = ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount less ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture, and never negative, because the recapture is a LesserOf capped at that same gain. 0 whenever the recapture route does not apply. THE PARTITION IS EXACT AND IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE ARM: for a recapture event the gain that used to arrive at line 34 in one piece now arrives as an ordinary part (line 31 to Form 4797 Part II line 13) plus this remainder (line 33 to Form 4684 line 36), and the two sum back to ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount exactly. "never negative, because the recapture is a LesserOf capped at that same gain" and "the two sum back to ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount exactly" ARE TRUE ONLY WHERE THE IRC 1245(b)(4)(B) TERM IS ZERO, which is every return that makes no section 1033 election. 1245(b)(4) caps the recapture at the RECOGNIZED gain PLUS the fair market value of non-section-1245 replacement property, and 1245(a)(1) recognizes the result "notwithstanding any other provision of this subtitle" - so on a section 1033 election with a non-1245 replacement the ordinary recapture legitimately exceeds what section 1033 leaves recognized, and this remainder is 0 rather than negative. Without the GreaterOf a NEGATIVE dollar would reach Form 4684 line 33 itself, the PDF-bound field f2_53 (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS4684/en/configuration.yml). The (b)(4)(B) term binds only when the depreciation exceeds the recognized gain, and this remainder is positive only when it does not, so the cap and a positive line 33 are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. Fact.Name: This event's unrecaptured section 1250 gain (Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet lines 1-3, casualty column)
Fact.Description: The CASUALTY twin of form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent - the Schedule D Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's lines 1 through 3, which are PER PROPERTY and therefore live on the event rather than on Schedule D. Line 1: "If you have a section 1250 property in Part III of Form 4797 for which you made an entry in Part I of Form 4797 (but not on Form 6252), enter the smaller of line 22 or line 24 of Form 4797 for that property." Line 2: "Enter the amount from Form 4797, line 26g, for the property for which you made an entry on line 1." Line 3: "Subtract line 2 from line 1." WHAT IT IS, IN ONE SENTENCE: the depreciation this destroyed property gave back as gain but did NOT give back as section 1250 ORDINARY recapture - the slice taxed in the 25% rate group instead of at the long-term capital gain rate. Omitting it is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE and that is exactly the gap item (20) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain named. THE THREE OPERANDS ARE THIS COLLECTION'S OWN Form 4797 Part III figures, the same ones ../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture already uses. Line 22 ("Depreciation allowed or allowable") is ../casualtyDepreciationAllowed. Line 24 ("Total gain") is ../sectionBCasualtyGainAmount - Part III line 20 is the Form 4684 line-21 reimbursement and line 23 is the Form 4684 line-20 adjusted basis, so their difference is the figure Form 4684 line 22 already computes, exactly as ../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture argues. Line 26g is ../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture itself. THE GATE IS ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies, AND IT IS ONE FACT WHERE THE SALE SIDE NEEDS TWO. The sale-side twin tests ../isInScope and ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod separately for line 1's "in Part III of Form 4797" and "for which you made an entry in Part I of Form 4797" clauses. On this collection both clauses are inside ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies, which is the printed i4684 Line 33 test (a Section B event, a gain, HELD MORE THAN ONE YEAR, and a modeled Part III class) - and reading it rather than its operands is not a convenience: its Switch short-circuits on ../isSectionB FIRST precisely because a Section A event's ../heldMoreThanOneYear can be Incomplete, and an All() over the operands here would read every one of them and carry that Incomplete into the Schedule D worksheet on every return with a Section A event. The gate order below is that fact's order, unchanged. THE CLASS PRECEDENCE IS 1245 BEFORE 1250, tested as an explicit $0 arm exactly as ../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture tests it, and for the same reason: a double-attested event is a section 1245 event everywhere, its whole depreciation is already ordinary income at line 25b, and a 25% slice computed against a line 26g nobody used would double-count it. THE FLOOR IS NOT PRINTED AT LINE 3 and is justified from the per-property rule instead: "If you had more than one property described on line 1, complete lines 1 through 3 for each property on a separate worksheet. Enter the total of the line 3 amounts for all properties on line 3." Each property's line 3 is computed on its OWN sheet before the total is taken, so one property's negative may not net against another's positive. Here the floor is defence in depth rather than the only guard - line 24 is strictly positive behind ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies (it requires ../hasSectionBCasualtyGain) and line 26g is a LesserOf capped at line 26a - but it is written because the sale-side twin writes it and because a future line-22 intake change must not be able to make this negative silently. ROUNDING SITS HERE, one step earlier than the Schedule D worksheet block's own "one Round at the end" discipline, and the seam is named rather than hidden: this module rounds per event throughout Part III (../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture, ../sectionBPartIIILine32Remainder), the sale-side twin rounds per item for the same reason, and scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250GainLine3 says "UNROUNDED" while summing rounded terms. The divergence is bounded by 50 cents per event. TWO BOUNDARIES ARE NAMED RATHER THAN CLOSED, both left as gaps because the whole population is refused by /knockoutCasualtyGain and neither can reach a filed return today. (a) LINE 22 UNANSWERED READS $0 (../casualtyDepreciationAllowed's IsComplete posture), so a filer who attests section 1250 and answers only line 26a gets line 1 = min(0, gain) = 0 and a $0 component - an UNDER-statement of the 25% rate group, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the same direction as the gap this fact closes. The intake exists (../writableCasualtyDepreciationAllowed) and the fix is requiredness, not arithmetic. [2026-08-25, unit form4684-part-iii-casualty-intake-obligations, beside (a) rather than over it. BOUNDARY (a) IS CLOSED, by exactly the fix it named. ../casualtyDepreciationAllowed reads its writable BARE on an event that attests section 1245 or section 1250 behind ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies, so "LINE 22 UNANSWERED READS $0" is FALSE for this fact's own population: line 1 is now Result.Incomplete there and so, MEASURED rather than predicted, is this component - and with it /casualtyUnrecapturedSection1250GainTotal and scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250GainLine3, none of which appears in the snapshot at all. The return stops instead of under-stating the 25% rate group. The sentence's own reasoning is untouched and is why the fix was requiredness. BOUNDARY (b) was carried as the residual of a tracked issue and is now settled by the statute, see (b) below.] (b) A PARTLY LOSS-ABSORBED LINE 39 DOES NOT REDUCE THIS COMPONENT, BY STATUTE. /sectionBNetGainToForm4797 nets Section B long-term losses against the line 33 gains before anything reaches Form 4797 Part I, so a positive line 39 can be smaller than this event's remainder. The only limit the law puts on unrecaptured section 1250 gain from section 1231 conversions is the AGGREGATE one in IRC 1(h)(6)(B): it "shall not exceed the net section 1231 gain" for the year. Worksheet line 7 ("the smaller of line 6 or the gain from Form 4797, line 7") is that limit, and Form 4797 line 7 already includes line 39 net of those losses. So a loss that absorbs part of the remainder lowers the cap, not the per-property line 3: with no other section 1231 gain the cap binds at line 39; with other section 1231 gain the remainder is reported whole, which is what the statute says. No per-property allocation exists and none is applied. NON-NEGATIVE, integer cents. CONSUMED by /casualtyUnrecapturedSection1250GainTotal, which scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250GainLine3 adds to the sale-side CollectionSum. COMPLETE $0 ON THE WHOLE COMMITTED CORPUS: no committed scenario answers a section 1250 casualty attestation, and every gate is a complete-safe wrapper or this collection's own arithmetic.
