Its ONE consumer is scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250GainLine3, which adds it to the sale-side CollectionSum over form4797:/section1245Dispositions/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent. That addend is the whole point of this unit and it discharges item (20) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain. IT ADDS A SECOND ADDEND, AND UNLIKE ITS PART III SIBLINGS THAT IS CORRECT. The line-31 legibility totals (/casualtyPartIIISection1250OrdinaryRecapture and its section 1254 twin) each say in as many words that they add no second addend, because line 31 is ONE printed line that /casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture already performs. Worksheet line 3 is not that: it is a per-property line whose printed rule is to TOTAL the separate worksheets, and a casualty column is a separate property from every sale item, so its total is a genuine second term rather than a second count of the first. GATED ON /claimsCasualtyLoss FIRST, the idiom every taxpayer-level fact on this collection uses, so a return with no casualty collection never reads the collection and resolves Complete $0 - which is what keeps the Schedule D worksheet block Complete on the whole committed corpus, the completeness trap a new addend of a shipping total has to clear. GATED SECOND ON FORM 4684 LINE 39 BEING POSITIVE, and this gate is printed rather than prudential. Worksheet line 1 wants a property "for which you made an entry in Part I of Form 4797". A casualty remainder reaches Part I only down line 39's branch, "If the loss on line 37 is less than or equal to the gain on line 36 ... enter this amount on Form 4797, line 3"; down the OTHER branch, line 38a, the whole Section B long-term net goes to Form 4797 line 14 (Part II, ordinary) and NOTHING is entered in Part I, so no casualty property qualifies for line 1 at all. /sectionBNetGainToForm4797 IS line 39, is 0 on the line-38 branch by its own Switch, and is Complete on every return. Without this gate a return whose Section B losses swallow its casualty gains would still report a 25% slice whenever some unrelated section 1231 sale kept Form 4797 line 7 positive, which worksheet line 7's cap does not catch. A PARTLY LOSS-ABSORBED LINE 39 IS HANDLED BY THE AGGREGATE CAP, NOT HERE: when line 39 is positive but smaller than the line 33 gains this total still reports each remainder in full, and scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250GainLine7 limits the block to the net section 1231 gain on Form 4797 line 7, which is the only limit IRC 1(h)(6)(B) imposes. See boundary (b) on ../sectionBUnrecapturedSection1250GainComponent. Nothing files through this leg today because /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every Section B casualty gain. THE ROUND IS DEFENCE IN DEPTH - every addend arrives rounded from the per-event fact - and is written for the reason /casualtyPartIIISection1250OrdinaryRecapture writes its own. Complete $0 on the entire committed corpus.

Fact.Name: This event's column (b)(i) loss if it is SHORT-TERM (Form 4684 line 29, column (b)(i))
Fact.Description: ../sectionBLossColumnBi when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is false, else 0. The per-event addend of /sectionBShortTermLossColumnBi (line 30, column (b)(i)). THE SORT COVERS LOSSES AS WELL AS GAINS - "Enter on line 29 all gains and losses on property held 1 year or less" - which is why the holding-period intake is asked of every Section B event on a gain-bearing return rather than only of the gaining ones. POSITIVE, like the column fact it reads; the sign flip to a net "(loss)" happens once, at /sectionBShortTermNetGainOrLoss (line 31).

Fact.Name: This event's column (b)(i) loss if it is LONG-TERM (Form 4684 line 34, column (b)(i))
Fact.Description: ../sectionBLossColumnBi when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is true, else 0 - the mirror of ../shortTermSectionBLossColumnBi, so the two partition ../sectionBLossColumnBi. The per-event addend of /sectionBLongTermLossColumnBi (line 35, column (b)(i)).

Fact.Name: This event's column (b)(ii) loss if it is SHORT-TERM (Form 4684 line 29, column (b)(ii))
Fact.Description: ../sectionBLossColumnBii when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is false, else 0. The per-event addend of /sectionBShortTermLossColumnBii, which is Form 4684 line 30 column (b)(ii) and therefore line 32 - the ONE Part II exit that is unconditional on the printed form. POSITIVE, like the Schedule A line-16 destination it feeds.

Fact.Name: This event's column (b)(ii) loss if it is LONG-TERM (Form 4684 line 34, column (b)(ii))
Fact.Description: ../sectionBLossColumnBii when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is true, else 0 - the mirror of ../shortTermSectionBLossColumnBii. The per-event addend of /sectionBLongTermLossColumnBii (line 35, column (b)(ii)), which is the ONE amount in Part II whose DESTINATION depends on the line 36 / line 37 branch: on the line-38 branch it exits at line 38b to Schedule A line 16, and on the line-39 branch it is netted into line 39 and leaves on Form 4797 line 3 instead. That branch dependence is why /sectionBLongTermIncomeProducingLoss exists as a separate fact from this column total. A SECTION C (Ponzi-type) EVENT REACHES THIS CELL like any other column (b)(ii) event - ../sectionBLossColumnBii carries it - and a Section C event has no holding-period intake of its own, so it sorts on the same ../heldMoreThanOneYear as every other event.

Fact.Name: This event is a Ponzi-type theft loss figured under the Rev. Proc. 2009-20 safe harbor (Form 4684 Section C)
Fact.Description: THE SECTION C GATE, and it is an ATTESTATION of both printed entry conditions at once. The 2025 Instructions for Form 4684 say "Fill out Section C if you claim a theft loss deduction for a Ponzi-type investment scheme and you meet both of the following conditions" - "You qualify to use Revenue Procedure 2009-20, as modified by Revenue Procedure 2011-58" and "You choose to follow the procedures in the guidance" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 12). Both are the filer's to assert: the first is a legal qualification the return cannot test, the second is an ELECTION (the safe harbor is "optional", Rev. Proc. 2009-20 SECTION 1, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-irbs/irb09-14.pdf, page 19). WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT MODELLED, named rather than silently folded into this one boolean. Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 4 defines "qualified loss" (4.02 - the lead figure charged by indictment, information or criminal complaint, as widened by Rev. Proc. 2011-58 SECTION 4.01 to the dead-lead-figure and civil-complaint cases), "qualified investor" (4.03 - a United States person who generally qualifies to deduct theft losses under section 165, had no actual knowledge of the fraud, and for whom the arrangement is not a tax shelter) and "discovery year" (4.04, also rewritten by Rev. Proc. 2011-58 SECTION 4.02). NONE of those tests is a computation this return could perform - they turn on court filings and on the filer's own knowledge - and Form 4684 Section C Part II is itself a block of signed declarations saying so ("I am a qualified investor, as defined in section 4.03 of Revenue Procedure 2009-20", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). So this fact carries the whole qualification, exactly as the printed form does. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means NOT a Section C event, which leaves the event on the ordinary Section A / Section B lines 19-27 chain it was already on. Every event in the pre-existing corpus leaves this unanswered, so the whole Section C arm resolves 0 there.

Fact.Name: Initial investment in the fraudulent arrangement (Form 4684 line 40)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 40, "Initial investment" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3) - Appendix A line 1 of Rev. Proc. 2009-20, whose section 4.06(1)(a)(i) names it "The total amount of cash, or the basis of property, that the qualified investor invested in the arrangement in all years". OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered resolves 0 through ../ponziInitialInvestmentAmount, the posture ../reimbursement already takes - a blank line on the printed form is a zero.

Fact.Name: Subsequent investments in the fraudulent arrangement (Form 4684 line 41)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 41, "Subsequent investments (see instructions)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). The instruction is "Enter the amounts of cash or the basis of property that you invested after you made the initial investment (including amounts reinvested)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 12), so REINVESTED purported income counts as an investment here as well as being reported income on line 42; that is the printed rule and not a double count, because line 42 is what the filer INCLUDED IN INCOME and line 41 is what was put back in. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered resolves 0 through ../ponziSubsequentInvestmentsAmount.

Fact.Name: Income from the arrangement reported in years before the discovery year (Form 4684 line 42)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 42, "Income reported on your tax returns for tax years prior to the discovery year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 4.06(1)(a)(ii) is the full rule: "The total amount of net income with respect to the specified fraudulent arrangement that, consistent with information received from the specified fraudulent arrangement, the qualified investor included in income for federal tax purposes for all taxable years prior to the discovery year, including taxable years for which a refund is barred by the statute of limitations". The refund-barred clause is why this amount is added rather than recovered by amending: section 6.02(2)'s own agreement is "Not to file returns or amended returns to exclude or recharacterize income reported with respect to the investment arrangement in taxable years preceding the discovery year". OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered resolves 0 through ../ponziPriorYearIncomeReportedAmount.

Fact.Name: Withdrawals from the arrangement in all years (Form 4684 line 44)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 44, "Withdrawals for all years (see instructions)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). The instruction is "Enter the total amount of cash or property that you withdrew from the investment arrangement in all years (whether designated as income or principal)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 13), and Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 4.06(1)(b) says the same. The parenthetical is the operative part: a "distribution" the arrangement called income is a withdrawal here, because the income it purported to distribute was fictitious. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered resolves 0 through ../ponziWithdrawalsAmount. That is the TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE direction on this one line (an unanswered withdrawal enlarges the qualified investment), and it is taken anyway because it is what the printed form does with a blank line and because ../reimbursement - the module's existing line whose blank likewise enlarges a loss - already sets that precedent. The filer's Section C Part II declaration ("I have written documentation to support the amounts reported in Part I of this Section C", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3) is what stands behind the blank.

Fact.Name: Investor is pursuing or intends to pursue a potential third-party recovery (Form 4684 line 46 fork)
Fact.Description: THE 95%/75% FORK. Form 4684 Section C line 46: "Enter 0.95 (95%) if you have no potential third-party recovery. Enter 0.75 (75%) if you have potential third-party recovery" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). TRUE here means the 75% multiplier. UNANSWERED TAKES 75%, and the ground is printed rather than chosen. The 95% figure is available only to "a qualified investor that does not pursue any potential third-party recovery" (Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 5.02(1)(a)), and Section C Part II makes claiming it a signed declaration: "If I have determined the amount of my theft loss deduction using 0.95 on line 46 above, I declare that I have not pursued and do not intend to pursue any potential third-party recovery" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). A filer who has not made that declaration has not met the condition for 95%, so the absent answer resolves to the 75% arm at ../ponziHasPotentialThirdPartyRecovery. It is also the conservative direction - the smaller deduction - but the declaration is the reason. NOTE WHAT "third-party recovery" IS NOT: Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 4.10 defines it as the claims that are NOT potential insurance/SIPC recovery (4.08) and NOT potential direct recovery against the responsible group (4.09). The insurance/SIPC amount has its own line (49) and subtracts; the potential DIRECT recovery neither subtracts nor changes this fork, because section 5.02 closes "The amount of the deduction calculated under this section 5.02 is not further reduced by potential direct recovery or potential third-party recovery".

Fact.Name: Actual recovery received in the discovery year (Form 4684 line 48)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 48, "Actual recovery" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 4.07: "Actual recovery means any amount a qualified investor actually receives in the discovery year from any source as reimbursement or recovery for the qualified loss". The instruction adds the exclusion that keeps this line from overlapping the ones that do NOT subtract: "Don't include amounts that are potential direct recoveries (defined earlier) or potential third-party recoveries (defined earlier)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 13). OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered resolves 0 through ../ponziActualRecoveryAmount.

Fact.Name: Potential insurance/SIPC recovery (Form 4684 line 49)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 49, "Potential insurance/Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC) recovery" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 4.08 defines it as the sum of all actual or potential claims for reimbursement that, as of the last day of the discovery year, are attributable to insurance policies in the investor's name, to non-insurance contractual arrangements that guaranteed or protected against the loss, or to amounts payable from SIPC under the Securities Investor Protection Act of 1970 (or a similar entity under a similar provision); the 2025 instructions restate the same three bullets at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4684.pdf, page 13. This is the ONLY potential recovery that reduces the deduction - potential direct recovery (4.09) and potential third-party recovery (4.10) do not, per section 5.02's closing sentence. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered resolves 0 through ../ponziPotentialInsuranceSipcRecoveryAmount.

Fact.Name: Section C applies to this event (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsPonziSafeHarborTheft when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern). Complete on every event, so every fact that reads it stays Complete and the entire pre-existing corpus - where the attestation is unanswered on every event - resolves exactly as before. THIS IS THE SWITCH THAT REPLACES THE PRINTED LINES 19 TO 27 FOR THIS EVENT. Form 4684 Section C line 51 says the Section C amount goes on "line 28 of Section B, Part I. Do not complete lines 19-27 for this loss" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3), so a true event bypasses ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement entirely (which is why that fact excludes it and resolves 0 rather than reading an ../adjustedBasis a Section C filer never answers) and ../sectionBCasualtyLoss takes ../ponziDeductibleTheftLoss instead. IT ALSO PUTS THE EVENT IN SECTION B. ../isSectionB reads this fact, which fences the event off from all three Section A limits ($100 floor, 10%-of-AGI floor, federally-declared- disaster gate) - correctly, because those are personal-use rules and this is a loss on property held for the production of income.

Fact.Name: Potential third-party recovery, complete-safe (Form 4684 line 46 fork)
Fact.Description: ../writablePonziHasPotentialThirdPartyRecovery when answered, else TRUE - and the direction of that default is the whole point of this fact, argued at the writable: the 0.95 multiplier is conditioned on a signed Part II declaration that no potential third-party recovery is pursued or intended, so an event that has not made the declaration has not met the condition and takes 0.75. Complete on every event.

Fact.Name: Initial investment, complete-safe (Form 4684 line 40)
Fact.Description: ../writablePonziInitialInvestment when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern, as ../reimbursementAmount) - a blank Section C line is a zero.

Fact.Name: Subsequent investments, complete-safe (Form 4684 line 41)
Fact.Description: ../writablePonziSubsequentInvestments when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern, as ../reimbursementAmount).

Fact.Name: Prior-year reported income, complete-safe (Form 4684 line 42)
Fact.Description: ../writablePonziPriorYearIncomeReported when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern, as ../reimbursementAmount).

Fact.Name: Withdrawals for all years, complete-safe (Form 4684 line 44)
Fact.Description: ../writablePonziWithdrawals when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern, as ../reimbursementAmount).

Fact.Name: Actual recovery, complete-safe (Form 4684 line 48)
Fact.Description: ../writablePonziActualRecovery when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern, as ../reimbursementAmount).

Fact.Name: Potential insurance/SIPC recovery, complete-safe (Form 4684 line 49)
Fact.Description: ../writablePonziPotentialInsuranceSipcRecovery when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern, as ../reimbursementAmount).

Fact.Name: Total invested plus income reported (Form 4684 line 43)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 43 = "Add lines 40, 41, and 42" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3) - the initial investment, the subsequent investments and the income the filer reported on returns for years before the discovery year. Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 4.06(1)(a) is the same sum stated as "The sum of" its two clauses, the form splitting the first clause's "all years" into lines 40 and 41. Complete on every event (all three addends are complete-safe), and 0 on every event that does not use Section C.

Fact.Name: Total qualified investment (Form 4684 line 45)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 45 = "Subtract line 44 from line 43. This is your total qualified investment" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). FLOORED AT 0, AND THE FLOOR IS SOURCED RATHER THAN CHOSEN. The printed line 45 carries no "if zero or less, enter -0-" (compare Section A line 9 and Section B line 27, which do), but the term it computes is defined by the revenue procedure the section implements: "Qualified investment means the excess, if any, of - (a) The sum of ... over (b) The total amount of cash or property that the qualified investor withdrew in all years" (Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 4.06(1), https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-irbs/irb09-14.pdf, page 20, middle column). "The excess, if any, of X over Y" is zero when Y exceeds X. Without the floor an investor who withdrew more than was ever invested would carry a NEGATIVE qualified investment into line 47 and a negative deduction onto Schedule A line 16, which is not a thing the form can mean. Complete on every event; 0 on every event that does not use Section C.

Fact.Name: Safe-harbor percentage of the qualified investment (Form 4684 lines 46-47)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C lines 46 and 47 in one fact: line 46 is the multiplier - "Enter 0.95 (95%) if you have no potential third-party recovery. Enter 0.75 (75%) if you have potential third-party recovery" - and line 47 is "Multiply line 46 by line 45" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). The two lines are one fact because line 46 has no independent existence: it is a constant selected by a boolean, and Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 5.02(1) states the selection and the multiplication as one step ("Multiply the amount of the qualified investment by - (a) 95 percent, for a qualified investor that does not pursue any potential third-party recovery; or (b) 75 percent, for a qualified investor that is pursuing or intends to pursue any potential third-party recovery"). The fork reads ../ponziHasPotentialThirdPartyRecovery, whose unanswered default is TRUE (the 75% arm) because the 95% figure is gated on a signed Part II declaration. Complete on every event; 0 on every event that does not use Section C.

Fact.Name: Total recovery (Form 4684 line 50)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 50 = "Add lines 48 and 49. This is your total recovery" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3): the actual recovery plus the potential insurance/SIPC recovery, and NOTHING ELSE. Rev. Proc. 2009-20 section 5.02(2) names the same two terms ("Subtract from this product the sum of any actual recovery and any potential insurance/SIPC recovery") and its closing sentence forecloses the two that a reader might expect to be here: "The amount of the deduction calculated under this section 5.02 is not further reduced by potential direct recovery or potential third-party recovery". Potential direct recovery (section 4.09, claims against the responsible group) and potential third-party recovery (section 4.10) therefore have no intake in this module at all - the second one only picks the multiplier at ../ponziSafeHarborAmount. Complete on every event; 0 on every event that does not use Section C.

Fact.Name: Deductible theft loss under the safe harbor (Form 4684 line 51, to Section B line 28)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 Section C line 51 = "Subtract line 50 from line 47. This is your deductible theft loss. Include this amount on line 28 of Section B, Part I. Do not complete lines 19-27 for this loss. Then complete Section B, Part II" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). This is the Section C output and the ONLY thing this arm exports into the rest of the module: ../sectionBCasualtyLoss (Section B line 28) takes it whole for an event where ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft is true. GATED on ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft, so it resolves 0 on every other event - including one whose filer entered Section C amounts and then did not claim the safe harbor. FLOORED AT 0, and this floor is NOT printed - it is this build's, flagged as such. Line 51 carries no "if zero or less" instruction, but the quantity it names is "your deductible theft loss", and a negative deduction would reach Schedule A line 16 and REDUCE other itemized deductions, which no printed line contemplates. Rev. Proc. 2009-20 says what happens when the recovery outruns the deduction, and it is a LATER-YEAR event, not a current-year negative: section 5.03, "The qualified investor may have income or an additional deduction in a year subsequent to the discovery year depending on the actual amount of the loss that is eventually recovered" (see section 1.165-1(d); Rev. Rul. 2009-9). That subsequent-year consequence is CROSS-YEAR state this graph does not hold and is a NAMED RESIDUAL of this fill, not something the floor pretends away. Complete on every event.

Fact.Name: Total SECTION A personal casualty and theft gain (Form 4684 line 13)
Fact.Description:
Form 4684 line 13 = "Add the amounts on line 4 of all Forms 4684". CollectionSum over /casualtyEvents/*/sectionACasualtyGainAmount, gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so a return with no casualty claim resolves Complete 0 rather than Incomplete.
THIS IS THE SECTION A FIGURE AND THE SIBLING /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized IS NOT. That fact is the GROSS line-4-plus-line-22 total across BOTH sections, published deliberately in un-netted form; line 13 is a Section A line and a Section B gain reaches line 29 or line 34 column (c) instead, never line 13. The two coincide on an all-Section-A return and differ the moment a Section B event has a gain.
IT IS STILL THE REALIZED GAIN, NOT THE RECOGNIZED ONE. Every disclosure on /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized applies unchanged to this narrower total: no IRC 1033 deferral (neither the 1033(a)(2)(A) election nor the MANDATORY 1033(h)(1)(A)(i) rule for unscheduled personal property in a disaster area), no IRC 121 main-home exclusion, no declined-claim measure, no later-year timing term. Those are arms 4, 5, 7 and 8 of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain, which continues to refuse every return this fact is nonzero on.
WHAT IT IS USED FOR, all three inside this module: Worksheet 1-1 line 3 (the cap on the non-disaster loss offset), the two arms of Form 4684 line 15, and the i4684 line-11 floor flip.

Fact.Name: Total losses NOT attributable to a federally declared disaster, after floors (Worksheet 1-1 line 1)
Fact.Description:
2025 i4684 Worksheet 1-1 line 1 = "Add the amounts from line 12 of all Forms 4684 reporting losses not attributable to a federally declared disaster". CollectionSum over /casualtyEvents/*/nonDisasterLossAfterFloor, gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss.
THE QUANTIFIER IS EVERY SUCH EVENT, not any: "all Forms 4684 reporting losses not attributable" is a sum over the whole collection, which is why this is a CollectionSum and not a Count or a first-match. The per-event term is 0 for every event that does not qualify, so the sum needs no filter.
THIS IS THE GROSS FIGURE, UNCAPPED. IRC 165(h)(5)(B)(i) lets a non-disaster loss be used only against a casualty gain; the cap is Worksheet 1-1 line 3 (/nonDisasterLossAllowedAgainstGain) and is applied there, exactly as the worksheet applies it. Pub. 547 states the same rule in one sentence: "Losses not attributable to a federally declared disaster can be used only to offset gains."

Fact.Name: Total losses attributable to a federally declared disaster, after floors (Worksheet 1-1 line 2)
Fact.Description:
2025 i4684 Worksheet 1-1 line 2 = "Add the amounts from line 12 of all Forms 4684 reporting losses attributable to a federally declared disaster". CollectionSum over /casualtyEvents/*/deductibleLossAfterFloor, gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss. This body is EXACTLY what /casualtyLossAfterFloors was before this fill: the same sum, the same gate, the same value. What changed is only that the sum is now one line of a worksheet rather than the whole of line 14, so it was moved to its own fact and named for the worksheet line it is.
ONE DEPARTURE FROM THE PRINTED WORKSHEET, INHERITED AND NOT INTRODUCED HERE. A QUALIFIED disaster loss is also "attributable to a federally declared disaster", so the printed line 2 includes it. This module has always routed a surviving qualified disaster event to the increased-standard-deduction path instead (/casualtyEvents/*/qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor -> /netQualifiedDisasterLoss) and excluded it from the Schedule A line-15 chain, so that the same loss is never deducted twice. That exclusion lives in the per-event fact and is preserved here unchanged. Where the omitted amount is needed as part of the PRINTED line 14 - and it is needed, by both arms of line 15 - it is added back explicitly by /casualtyLossAfterFloorsIncludingQualifiedDisaster.
[APPENDED 2026-08-30, reconciliation sweep: A SECOND ADDEND, /form4684SectionDLossAfterFloor. The CollectionSum above covers the events on THIS return's page 1; the Section D election under IRC 165(i) carries a loss sustained in the FOLLOWING tax year that 165(i)(2) deems to have occurred in the year the deduction is claimed, i.e. here, and it is by definition attributable to a federally declared disaster, so worksheet line 2 is exactly its row. This is the wire /writableForm4684SectionDElectedLossAmount's own Description had been recording as owed ("print only until /casualtyLossDeduction consumes it"). NOTHING MOVES on a return that never opens Section D: the new addend is Complete 0 there, so the sum keeps the value it had, and the whole Add still sits inside the /claimsCasualtyLoss arm.]

Fact.Name: Non-disaster loss allowed against the casualty gain (Worksheet 1-1 line 3)
Fact.Description:
2025 i4684 Worksheet 1-1 line 3 = "Enter the smaller of line 1 or line 13 of Form 4684": LesserOf(/nonDisasterCasualtyLossAfterFloors, /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain), gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss.
THIS IS IRC 165(h)(5)(B)(i) IN ONE LINE. Since the OBBBA regime a personal casualty loss not attributable to a federally declared disaster is not deductible at all; clause (i) says the limitation "shall not apply to the portion of the personal casualty loss not attributable to a Federally declared disaster ... TO THE EXTENT SUCH LOSS DOES NOT EXCEED SUCH GAINS". The worksheet implements "to the extent" as a LesserOf, and Pub. 547 restates it as "Losses not attributable to a federally declared disaster can be used only to offset gains."
THE CAP IS TAXPAYER-WIDE, NOT PER EVENT - line 1 is already a total and line 13 is already a total, so a filer with three non-disaster losses and one gain gets ONE cap across all three. That is why /casualtyEvents/*/nonDisasterLossAfterFloor is deliberately uncapped.
WITH NO GAIN THIS IS ZERO AND NOTHING MOVES. LesserOf(anything, 0) is 0, so every return without a casualty gain reaches Form 4684 line 14 with the same figure it had before this fill.

Fact.Name: Casualty losses after the floors, Schedule A path (Form 4684 line 14 via Worksheet 1-1)
Fact.Description:
Form 4684 line 14, computed the way the printed line 14 tells the filer to compute it once a casualty GAIN is in play: "Add the amounts on line 12 of all Forms 4684. If you have losses not attributable to a federally declared disaster, see the instructions", and the instruction sends the filer to Worksheet 1-1. This fact is Worksheet 1-1 line 4, "Add lines 2 and 3. Enter the result here and on Form 4684, line 14" - i.e. /disasterCasualtyLossAfterFloors (worksheet line 2) plus /nonDisasterLossAllowedAgainstGain (worksheet line 3). Gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so a return with no casualty loss resolves Complete 0.
THE SUM has two addends: worksheet line 2 (/disasterCasualtyLossAfterFloors, the CollectionSum over /casualtyEvents/*/deductibleLossAfterFloor) and worksheet line 3 (/nonDisasterLossAllowedAgainstGain, LesserOf(non-disaster losses, Form 4684 line 13)). ON EVERY RETURN WITHOUT A CASUALTY GAIN LINE 13 IS ZERO, SO LINE 3 IS ZERO and this fact equals worksheet line 2 alone; line 3 moves a dollar only on returns with a casualty gain.
IT IS NOT THE WHOLE PRINTED LINE 14, and the difference matters twice. This module routes a surviving QUALIFIED disaster loss to the increased-standard-deduction path instead of Schedule A line 15, so worksheet line 2 as modeled omits it, while the PRINTED worksheet line 2 - "losses attributable to a federally declared disaster" - includes it. Both arms of Form 4684 line 15 compare against the printed total, so they read /casualtyLossAfterFloorsIncludingQualifiedDisaster instead of this fact. What this fact IS, exactly, is the part of line 14 that can still reach Schedule A line 15, which is why line 16 (/casualtyLossAfterGainOffset) is computed from it.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 14 AS PRINTED, qualified disaster losses included
Fact.Description:
The printed Form 4684 line 14: every Form 4684's line 12 that is attributable to a federally declared disaster, PLUS the non-disaster losses admitted by Worksheet 1-1 line 3. = /casualtyLossAfterFloors (this module's Schedule-A-path subtotal) plus the total of /casualtyEvents/*/qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor. Gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss.
WHY THE MODULE NEEDS TWO LINE-14 FACTS. A qualified disaster loss IS "attributable to a federally declared disaster", so the printed Worksheet 1-1 line 2 includes it; this module has always excluded it from the Schedule A line-15 chain instead, because it travels the increased-standard-deduction path and must not be deducted twice. That exclusion is right for the DEDUCTION and wrong for the COMPARISON: Form 4684 line 15 asks whether line 13 is more than, equal to, or less than LINE 14, and it means the printed line 14. Comparing against the truncated subtotal instead would be a real error, not a presentational one: for a filer with a $3,000 gain, $2,900 of ordinary disaster loss and $4,500 of qualified disaster loss the printed line 14 is $7,400 and the filer has a net LOSS, while the truncated subtotal is $2,900 and would manufacture a $100 "net gain" bound for Schedule D and zero a $4,400 net qualified disaster loss at the same time. Both halves of that error would be filed.
AT ZERO GAINS IT CHANGES NOTHING. Its only consumers are the two arms of line 15, and both reduce to their pre-fill values when line 13 is zero: the net-gain arm is GreaterOf(0 - this, 0) = 0, and the qualified-disaster arm is LesserOf(this - 0, the qualified total) = the qualified total, which is exactly what /netQualifiedDisasterLoss was before this fill.

Fact.Name: Net personal casualty gain (Form 4684 line 15, NET GAIN case - WIRED to Schedule D lines 4 and 11 since 2026-08-24)
Fact.Description:
Form 4684 line 15, first bullet: "If line 13 is more than line 14, enter the difference here and on Schedule D. Do not complete the rest of this section." = GreaterOf(/sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain minus /casualtyLossAfterFloorsIncludingQualifiedDisaster, 0), gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss.
THE FLOOR AT 0 CARRIES THE OTHER TWO PRINTED CASES, so the single Switch arm covers all three: line 13 EQUAL to line 14 prints -0- ("If line 13 is equal to line 14, enter -0- here"), and line 13 LESS than line 14 with no qualified disaster loss also prints -0- ("enter -0- here and go to line 16"). The remaining case - line 13 less than line 14 WITH qualified disaster losses subject to the $500 reduction - is the same printed line carrying a different quantity, and it is /netQualifiedDisasterLoss. The two facts are mutually exclusive by the printed line's own conditions, never both nonzero. Both edges are pinned: boundary-line14-equals-line13-net-gain-is-zero and boundary-line14-one-dollar-under-line13-net-gain-is-one.
THE DESTINATION IS NOT WIRED, AND THAT IS WHY /knockoutCasualtyGain STILL REFUSES. The form sends this amount to Schedule D, and the instruction splits it by holding period on the way - "Combine your short-term gains with your short-term losses and include the net short-term gain or (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 4", with the long-term half going to Schedule D line 11. This dictionary has no holding-period intake for a casualty event (the contract node /casualtyEvents/*/writableCasualtyGainPropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear is still unfilled), and the instruction's split needs one on LOSS events as well as gain events, so the amount is computed here and routed nowhere. Nothing in scheduleD consumes it. This fact is EXPORTED so the owed leg can consume it when it lands, exactly as /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized is. [APPENDED 2026-08-24, frontier fill form4684-casualty-gain, beside the paragraph above rather than over it, because EVERY OPERATIVE CLAUSE IN IT IS NOW FALSE. Each was true when written and each is false at HEAD: (a) "THE DESTINATION IS NOT WIRED" - it is wired. This amount now splits by holding period into /netShortTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD and /netLongTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD, which are consumed by scheduleD:/shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover (line 7, carrying Schedule D line 4) and scheduleD:/longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover (line 15, carrying line 11), each as one addend OUTSIDE the Schedule D writables - the same placement form4797:/section1231LtcgPortion already had. (b) "This dictionary has no holding-period intake for a casualty event (the contract node /casualtyEvents/*/writableCasualtyGainPropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear is still unfilled)" - that contract node is DELETED, and the intake ships WIDER, as /casualtyEvents/*/writablePropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear, answered on Section A LOSS events as well as gain events, exactly because "the instruction's split needs one on LOSS events as well as gain events" - the one clause of that sentence that was right and is why the name no longer says "CasualtyGain". (c) "routed nowhere. Nothing in scheduleD consumes it" - two facts in scheduleD consume it. (d) "AND THAT IS WHY /knockoutCasualtyGain STILL REFUSES" - the guard still refuses and this is no longer the reason. The reason is now the MEASURE: the amount routed is the REALIZED gain (no section 1033 including the mandatory 1033(h)(1)(A)(i), no section 121, no declined-claim measure, no later-year timing term) and no intake exists to DETECT which filers those reach, so a narrowed When would file OVER-recognized income; and a SECTION B gain still has no route to Form 4797 line 3. What survives unchanged: the arithmetic above, the three printed line-15 cases, the Export, and the two boundary witnesses.]
ONE CONSEQUENCE OF THE ROUTING GAP IS ALREADY CORRECT HERE. "Do not complete the rest of this section" zeroes the Schedule A leg on a net-gain return, and /casualtyLossAfterGainOffset delivers that zero by arithmetic (line 14 minus line 13 is negative, floored at 0) rather than by a branch. The half that is missing is the Schedule D leg, not the Schedule A one.

Fact.Name: Event's property was held more than one year (required on a gain return, read where answered on Section B)
Fact.Description:
../writablePropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear, read BARE where the answer must be supplied, read behind IsComplete where it is merely useful, and resolved to a complete FALSE everywhere else. THREE ARMS, disjoint by construction.
SECTION A (the first arm) reads the writable BARE when BOTH hold: /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD is more than zero (there is a Form 4684 line-15 net gain, so something actually travels to Schedule D and has to pick Part I or Part II), and this event is NOT a Section B event.
SECTION B WITH A GAIN ON THE RETURN (the second arm) reads the writable BARE on every Section B event when /anySectionBCasualtyGain is true, i.e. when some event on the return fires Form 4684 line 22. The two BARE arms are DISJOINT - the Section A arm requires NOT ../isSectionB and this one requires it - so a Section A event on a return that has a Section B gain but no Section A net gain is still not asked. WHY THE GATE IS "ANY SECTION B GAIN" AND NOT "A POSITIVE LINE 39": line 39 is downstream of the sort this alias feeds, so gating on it would circle; /anySectionBCasualtyGain reads only reimbursement-over-basis and the section attestations, none of which reads a holding period. WHY THE ANSWER IS REQUIRED ONLY THERE is argued in full at /anySectionBCasualtyGain: with column (c) identically zero, Part II's two halves collect the same amounts.
SECTION B WITH THE ANSWER SUPPLIED ANYWAY (the third arm) reads the writable on a Section B event whenever it IS answered, gain on the return or not. The printed form asks the question of every filer who completes Part II - "Enter on line 29 all gains and losses on property held 1 year or less. Enter on line 34 all gains and losses on property held more than 1 year" - so an answered holding period is the filer's own record of which half a LOSS row belongs in, and discarding it printed every Section-B loss-only return under the line 29 heading regardless. THE DOLLARS DO NOT MOVE, and that is a proof rather than a hope: with column (c) identically zero, the short half's lines 31 and 32 and the long half's lines 38a and 38b collect the same column (b)(i) and column (b)(ii) losses, and /sectionBNetGainOrLoss and /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss each ADD the two halves, so both exits - Form 4797 line 14 and Schedule A line 16 - are invariant under the sort. THE THIRD ARM IS IsComplete-GATED, WHICH IS WHAT KEEPS IT ADDITIVE. It reads the writable only where the filer has already answered it, so an unanswered holding period on a Section-B loss-only return still falls through to the complete FALSE below: no existing return goes Incomplete and no un-asked question is forced on anyone.
THE BARE ARMS ARE THE OPPOSITE OF THE USUAL IsComplete IDIOM, ON PURPOSE. Every other complete-safe alias in this module answers "unanswered means false"; this one answers "unanswered means REFUSED, but only where the answer changes a number". Defaulting an unknown holding period to short-term would silently route a long-term casualty gain into Schedule D Part I, which moves the tax on a return that files - the exact failure class /knockoutCasualtyGain exists to prevent. Defaulting it everywhere ELSE is safe and necessary: without the gate every return in the corpus that has a casualty event and no gain would go Incomplete, which is the trap the retired contract node named by hand.
THE GATE CANNOT CIRCLE. /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD is Form 4684 line 13 less the printed line 14, and neither term reads a holding period; the split facts below read this one, never the other way round.

Fact.Name: This event's whole SECTION A line-12 loss, whichever of the three paths carries it
Fact.Description:
../deductibleLossAfterFloor plus ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor plus ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor. The three are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE by construction - each is gated on a condition the other two negate (../isEligible with the flip off, the flip on, and neither, respectively) - so this Add is a selection, not a sum of overlapping amounts, and at most one term is ever nonzero. A Section B event contributes 0 to all three and therefore 0 here.
WHAT IT IS FOR: the per-event term of the PRINTED Form 4684 line 14 on a net-gain return. The printed line 14 is /casualtyLossAfterFloorsIncludingQualifiedDisaster, which is Worksheet 1-1 line 2 (the disaster total) plus worksheet line 3, and worksheet line 3 CAPS the non-disaster total at line 13. THE CAP CANNOT BIND ON A NET-GAIN RETURN, which is the lemma this whole leg rests on: write G for line 13, D for the disaster total (ordinary plus qualified) and N for the non-disaster total, all of them at least zero. Printed line 14 is D + LesserOf(N, G). If LesserOf(N, G) were G, line 14 would be D + G, which is at least G, so line 13 would NOT be more than line 14 and there would be no net gain at all. So whenever /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD is positive, LesserOf(N, G) = N and printed line 14 is exactly the sum of this fact over the collection.

Fact.Name: This event's SECTION A net position: its line-4 gain less its line-12 loss
Fact.Description:
../sectionACasualtyGainAmount minus ../sectionALossAfterFloor. MAY BE NEGATIVE, and the negative case is the whole point: i4684 Line 15 tells a net-gain filer to "Combine your short-term gains with your short-term losses" and to combine long with long, so the quantity each half of Schedule D receives is a NET, not a gross gain.
AN EVENT IS NEVER BOTH. The printed form says so - line 4's Note is "If line 2 is more than line 3, skip line 4", and line 4 itself says to "skip lines 5 through 9 for that column" - so at most one of the two terms is nonzero on any event. The subtraction is written anyway because it is what the instruction's word "combine" means, and because a reader checking the identity below should not have to know the exclusivity to check it.
THE IDENTITY THIS FACT EXISTS TO MAKE TRUE: summed over the collection, it is line 13 minus the printed line 14 whenever there is a net gain (see ../sectionALossAfterFloor for why the Worksheet 1-1 cap cannot bind there), i.e. exactly Form 4684 line 15. So the two Schedule D legs below always add back to /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD, and every net-gain fixture asserts all three figures rather than trusting the algebra.

Fact.Name: This event's Section A net position if it is SHORT-TERM (i4684 Line 15, first bullet)
Fact.Description: ../sectionANetGainOrLoss when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is false, else 0. The per-event addend of /netShortTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD. IT IS NOT GATED ON THE NET GAIN ITSELF, deliberately: ../heldMoreThanOneYear already resolves a complete false on every return without one, so this fact is simply the event's net position there, and the gate that stops anything reaching Schedule D lives once, at the collection total below, rather than being restated per event. [A SECTION B SHORT-CIRCUIT WAS ADDED 2026-08-24, frontier fill form4684-section-b, and it moves no dollar: ../sectionANetGainOrLoss is already identically 0 on a Section B event (../sectionACasualtyGainAmount is 0 there by its own gate and ../sectionALossAfterFloor is 0 there through all three of its terms). What the short-circuit protects is COMPLETENESS. Once ../heldMoreThanOneYear became REQUIRED on Section B events too, reading it here would have turned this fact into a Placeholder on every return carrying an unanswered Section B holding period - and would have dragged /netShortTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD and Schedule D with it on a return whose SECTION A holding periods were all answered, which is a completeness regression with no arithmetic behind it. Reading ../isSectionB first keeps the Schedule D legs Complete for exactly the returns whose Schedule D amount is knowable.]

Fact.Name: This event's Section A net position if it is LONG-TERM (i4684 Line 15, second bullet)
Fact.Description: ../sectionANetGainOrLoss when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is true, else 0. The per-event addend of /netLongTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD, and the exact mirror of ../shortTermSectionANetAmount - the two partition the collection, so their sums add back to the sum of ../sectionANetGainOrLoss with nothing dropped and nothing counted twice. [THE SAME SECTION B SHORT-CIRCUIT WAS ADDED 2026-08-24 for the same completeness reason; the argument is at ../shortTermSectionANetAmount and it moves no dollar. The mirror is preserved: both halves now return 0 on a Section B event, so the partition still adds back to ../sectionANetGainOrLoss, which is itself 0 there.]

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 15's SHORT-TERM half, bound for Schedule D line 4
Fact.Description:
The sum of /casualtyEvents/*/shortTermSectionANetAmount when /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD is more than zero, else 0. Consumed by scheduleD:/shortTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover (Schedule D line 7), which is where Schedule D line 4 enters this dictionary.
THE ZERO ARM IS THE FORM'S OWN WORDS, not a convenience. Line 15 sends an amount to Schedule D only on the net-gain branch; the other three printed branches say "enter -0- here" or route a qualified disaster loss to Schedule A line 16 instead, and in every one of them nothing reaches Schedule D. So the gate is line 15's own condition, read off the fact that already implements it.
IT ADDS BACK. This fact plus /netLongTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD equals /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD on every net-gain return, because the two per-event halves partition the collection and the per-event nets sum to line 13 less the printed line 14 (the argument is on /casualtyEvents/*/sectionALossAfterFloor). Three fixtures assert all three numbers rather than the identity.
IT MAY BE NEGATIVE even on a net-gain return - a filer with a large long-term gain and a smaller short-term loss reports a short-term LOSS on Schedule D line 4, which is why the printed line says "short-term gain or (loss)". No floor is applied.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, named rather than left silent. (a) A filer whose ONLY capital item is this casualty gain still has to answer scheduleD:/writableNetShortTermGainOrLoss, because scheduleD:/netShortTermGainOrLoss reads that writable BARE on a return with no Form 8949 detail; the casualty leg is added OUTSIDE it, at line 7, exactly as the Form 4797 leg is. (b) The gain reaching Schedule D is still the REALIZED gain: no IRC 1033 deferral, no IRC 121 exclusion, no declined-claim measure and no later-year timing term. Both are arms of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain, which is why that guard still refuses every return this fact is nonzero on.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 15's LONG-TERM half, bound for Schedule D line 11
Fact.Description: The long-term mirror of /netShortTermCasualtyGainToScheduleD: the sum of /casualtyEvents/*/longTermSectionANetAmount when /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD is more than zero, else 0. Consumed by scheduleD:/longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover (Schedule D line 15), which is where Schedule D line 11 enters this dictionary and where the Form 4797 section 1231 leg already enters. Every note on the short-term twin applies unchanged: the zero arm is line 15's own condition, the two halves add back to /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD, the figure may be negative, the Schedule D intake still has to be answered separately, and the gain is REALIZED rather than recognized.

Fact.Name: Casualty loss after the gain offset (Form 4684 line 16)
Fact.Description:
Form 4684 line 16 = "Add lines 13 and 15. Subtract the result from line 14". Implemented as GreaterOf(/casualtyLossAfterFloors minus /sectionAPersonalCasualtyGain, 0), gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss - which is the same number as the printed subtraction in every one of the printed line-15 branches, and the derivation is written out here because the two expressions do not look alike.
Write L for the PRINTED line 14 (/casualtyLossAfterFloorsIncludingQualifiedDisaster), S for this module's Schedule-A-path subtotal (/casualtyLossAfterFloors), Q for the qualified disaster total, so L = S + Q, and G for line 13. - NET GAIN, G more than L: the form says "Do not complete the rest of this section", so line 16 is not completed and this fact must resolve 0. G more than L implies G more than S, so GreaterOf(S - G, 0) = 0. - EQUAL, G = L: line 15 is -0-, so line 16 = L - G = 0. And S - G = -Q, at most 0, so the floor gives 0 as well. - NET LOSS with no qualified disaster loss, Q = 0: line 15 is -0-, so line 16 = L - G = S - G, which is positive on this branch. - NET LOSS with qualified disaster losses, Q more than 0: line 15 = LesserOf(L - G, Q), so line 16 = L - G - LesserOf(L - G, Q) = GreaterOf(L - G - Q, 0) = GreaterOf(S - G, 0). All four branches collapse to the one expression, so the fact needs no branch of its own and no dependency on either line-15 fact.
THIS IS IRC 165(h)(5)(B)(ii), the no-double-count clause: "the amount of personal casualty gains taken into account under paragraph (2)(A) shall be reduced by the portion of such gains taken into account under clause (i)". Clause (i) is the offset already spent at Worksheet 1-1 line 3, which is inside S; subtracting the WHOLE of G here would spend it twice, and it does not, because worksheet line 3 raised S by exactly the amount of G it consumed. The arithmetic is Pub. 547's sentence "Any excess gain is used to reduce losses from a federally declared disaster."
IT CORRECTS A COLLAPSE, NOT A VALUE. Before this fill /casualtyLossDeduction subtracted line 17 from line 14 directly, because with no gain modeled lines 13 and 15 were both zero and line 16 equalled line 14. That is still true whenever there is no gain, so this fact is equal to /casualtyLossAfterFloors on every return that does not have one. THIS SUBTRACTION IS ALSO IRC 165(h)(4)(A). The statute: "In any case to which paragraph (2)(A) applies, the deduction for personal casualty losses for any taxable year shall be treated as a deduction allowable in computing adjusted gross income to the extent such losses do not exceed the personal casualty gains for the taxable year" (26 U.S.C. 165, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section165&num=0&edition=2024). Paragraph (2)(A) is the NET-LOSS case (losses exceed gains, line 78). Write G for line 13 and L for line 14 with L more than G. The statute's picture: G is in gross income (165(h)(3)(A) gain), G of the losses is deducted FOR AGI, so AGI moves by +G - G = 0; the excess L - G is the itemized deduction subject to the 10-percent floor (2)(A)(ii). The form's picture: line 15 is -0- (with no qualified disaster loss subject to the $500 reduction, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 1; the other branch sends line 15 to Schedule A, never to Schedule D) so nothing reaches Schedule D and G is NOT in gross income; this fact takes G off L so the matched losses are NOT deducted anywhere; AGI moves by 0; line 16 = L - G goes on to lines 17 and 18. The two pictures agree on AGI (unchanged), on the 10-percent floor (10 percent of the same AGI) and on Schedule A (L - G less the floor); because AGI is the same, every item that reads /agi reads the same figure under both pictures. They do NOT agree on the items that read income:/totalIncome DIRECTLY, which is where G would appear under the statute and does not under the form's netting. Readers of that fact outside its module: taxCalculations:/agi itself (totalIncome less /allowableAdjustmentsToIncome - nets by construction); estimatedPayments:/farmerFishermanTwoThirdsArmCurrentYear (three reads; its denominator IS "gross income from all sources", so the farmer-fisherman waiver and through it the Form 2210 required annual payment could differ); taxCalculations:/magiForStudentLoanInterestDeduction (built as totalIncome less a subset of adjustments - nets only if the above-the-line casualty deduction were added to that pool); and form6251's /alternativeTaxNolCarryoverMayOmitCurrentYearLoss disclosure flag (moves no dollar). /magiForIraDeduction does not read it. None of these moves a dollar today, because every return carrying a casualty gain is refused by /knockoutCasualtyGain.

Fact.Name: 10% of AGI (Form 4684 line 17)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 17 = 10% of adjusted gross income (Form 1040 line 11b). Gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so returns with no casualty loss resolve Complete 0 (keeping existing scenarios byte-identical - AGI is nonzero on most returns). AGI is above-the-line, so no circularity with this below-the-line itemized deduction.

Fact.Name: Personal casualty and theft loss deduction (Form 4684 line 18, to Schedule A line 15)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 18 = line 16 minus line 17. If zero or less, 0. This is the amount that flows to Schedule A (Form 1040) line 15. Gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so it is Complete 0 on every return without a casualty loss. EXPORTED for Schedule A and MeF. [APPENDED 2026-08-21, frontier fill form4684-casualty-gain-residual, beside the sentence this replaced rather than over it - the removed sentence read "With only losses modeled (no gains), line 16 equals line 14 (/casualtyLossAfterFloors)", and it was true when written and is now only HALF true. Line 16 is a real fact, /casualtyLossAfterGainOffset, and this fact now subtracts line 17 from THAT instead of from line 14. The collapse the removed sentence described still holds whenever line 13 is zero - line 16 equals line 14 on every return without a casualty gain, so no such return moves a dollar - but on a return WITH a gain the two are different numbers and this fact must read the later one. 2025 Pub 547 Example 2 is the witness: line 14 is $6,370, line 16 is $4,370, and the printed deduction of $-0- follows from the second, not the first.]. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Net qualified disaster loss (Form 4684 line 15, increases the standard deduction)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 15 (net-loss, qualified-disaster case) = the total of each qualified disaster event's line 12 (loss after the 500-dollar floor). CollectionSum over /casualtyEvents/*/qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor, gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so returns with no casualty loss resolve Complete 0 (keeping every existing scenario byte-identical). The 10%-of-AGI reduction (Form 4684 line 17) does NOT apply to qualified disaster losses (2025 i4684 "your net casualty loss from these qualified disasters doesn't need to exceed 10% of your adjusted gross income"). This is the amount that INCREASES the standard deduction: the standard-deduction filer adds it to their standard deduction (2025 i4684 "Increased standard deduction reporting"), so a qualified disaster loss is deductible WITHOUT itemizing. The line-13 term is REAL: this fact is LesserOf(GreaterOf(printed line 14 minus line 13, 0), the qualified-disaster line-12 total), which is the printed line 15 third bullet in full. Whenever line 13 is zero it reduces to the qualified-disaster line-12 total, because LesserOf(line 14 - 0, the qualified total) is the qualified total - line 14 as printed INCLUDES the qualified amounts, which is why the fact reads /casualtyLossAfterFloorsIncludingQualifiedDisaster and not /casualtyLossAfterFloors. So no return without a casualty gain moves, and a return with one does not over-claim: a filer with a $3,000 gain, $2,900 of ordinary disaster loss and $4,500 of qualified disaster loss gets $4,400 here, not $4,500. THE OUTER FLOOR AT 0 IS THE NET-GAIN BRANCH: when line 13 exceeds line 14 the form says "Do not complete the rest of this section" and the amount on this line is the net gain instead, carried by /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD. The two facts are the same printed line and are never both nonzero. A SECOND EFFECT ARRIVES THROUGH THE PER-EVENT TOTAL: an event is counted here only while /casualtyEvents/*/qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies holds, so i4684 Line 11 can move an event OUT of this total and onto the ordinary Schedule A path when its line 10 is not larger than the summed line-4 gains. With no gain the comparison is against zero and every attested event stays. EXPORTED (downstreamFacts) - consumed by standardDeduction:/standardDeduction. The itemize-with-Schedule-A-line-16 alternative (a taxpayer who itemizes AND has a qualified disaster loss) is NOT separately modeled: this unit implements the increased-standard-deduction path; an itemizing filer's qualified disaster loss would be under-deducted here (the conservative direction), FLAGGED in the memo.

Fact.Name: Section B short-term column (b)(i) losses (Form 4684 line 30, column (b)(i))
Fact.Description: Line 30, "Totals. Add the amounts on line 29", taken in column (b)(i): the sum of /casualtyEvents/*/shortTermSectionBLossColumnBi. POSITIVE. Feeds line 31 only.

Fact.Name: Section B short-term column (b)(ii) losses (Form 4684 line 30, column (b)(ii))
Fact.Description: Line 30 taken in column (b)(ii): the sum of /casualtyEvents/*/shortTermSectionBLossColumnBii. POSITIVE. Line 32 is this amount unconditionally, which is why /sectionBShortTermIncomeProducingLoss is a separate fact with no branch in it.

Fact.Name: Section B short-term gains (Form 4684 line 30, column (c))
Fact.Description: Line 30 taken in column (c), "Gains from casualties or thefts includible in income": the sum of /casualtyEvents/*/shortTermSectionBGain. POSITIVE. THIS IS THE FACT WHOSE ARRIVAL KILLS THE OLD COLLAPSE. Until 2026-08-24 both /sectionBNetGainOrLoss and /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss argued that Part II's two holding-period halves could be added without a fork because every column (c) term was identically zero; each carried an explicit marker saying the argument dies when column (c) gets an intake. This fact and /sectionBLongTermGain are that intake.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 31, the short-term Part II exit to Form 4797 line 14
Fact.Description: Line 31: "Combine line 30, columns (b)(i) and (c). Enter the net gain or (loss) here and on Form 4797, line 14." Column (b)(i) prints its entries in parentheses, so "combine" is the gain LESS the loss: /sectionBShortTermGain minus /sectionBShortTermLossColumnBi. MAY BE POSITIVE, and that is new - before column (c) had an intake this quantity could only be a loss. UNCONDITIONAL. Unlike the long-term half, line 31 sits under no branch on the printed form; the line 36 / line 37 test governs lines 38 and 39 only, both of which are long-term lines. So a short-term Section B gain reaches Form 4797 line 14 as ORDINARY income even on a return whose long-term half takes the line-39 section 1231 route - which is the printed form's own answer to the holding-period question and not a modelling choice.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 32, the short-term column (b)(ii) exit to Schedule A line 16
Fact.Description: Line 32: "Enter the amount from line 30, column (b)(ii), here. Individuals, enter the amount from income-producing property on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16 ... (Do not include any loss on property used as an employee.)" A pass-through of /sectionBShortTermLossColumnBii, POSITIVE, and UNCONDITIONAL - line 32 carries no branch, which is the asymmetry that makes its long-term twin /sectionBLongTermIncomeProducingLoss a different shape. One of the two addends of /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss.

Fact.Name: Section B long-term column (b)(i) losses (Form 4684 line 35, column (b)(i))
Fact.Description: Line 35, "Total losses. Add amounts on line 34, columns (b)(i) and (b)(ii)", taken in column (b)(i): the sum of /casualtyEvents/*/longTermSectionBLossColumnBi. POSITIVE. Read twice on the printed form - by line 37 (with its (b)(ii) sibling) and by line 38a (alone) - which is why it is its own fact rather than a term inside either.

Fact.Name: Section B long-term column (b)(ii) losses (Form 4684 line 35, column (b)(ii))
Fact.Description: Line 35 taken in column (b)(ii): the sum of /casualtyEvents/*/longTermSectionBLossColumnBii. POSITIVE. THIS IS THE OPERAND FORM 4797 LINE 18a NAMES BY NUMBER, and line 18a is NOT built here. i4797's Line 18a instruction is fully specific - "You must complete this line if there is a gain on Form 4797, line 3; a loss on Form 4797, line 11; and a loss on Form 4684, line 35, column (b)(ii). Enter on this line the smaller of the loss on Form 4797, line 11, or the loss on Form 4684, line 35, column (b)(ii)." - so the computation is knowable; what stops it is that its destination is scheduleA:/otherItemizedDeductions, which this fill holds no grant over, and that every return that could reach it is refused by /knockoutCasualtyGain (line 18a needs a GAIN on Form 4797 line 3, which needs a positive line 39, which needs a Section B casualty gain, which fires the guard). It is owed by name as arm (13) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain rather than left silent. [APPENDED 2026-08-25, frontier fill form4684-section-b-recapture-and-line18a, beside the paragraph above rather than over it. ARM (13) IS DISCHARGED AND "line 18a is NOT built here" IS NOW FALSE - it is built, in the module that prints it, at form4797:/lossFromForm4684ColumnBiiOnLineEleven, and THIS FACT IS ITS SECOND OPERAND, read cross-module. Both obstacles named above are answered: the grant over scheduleA:/otherItemizedDeductions was held by this fill, and the "every return that could reach it is refused" sentence is still TRUE and was never a reason not to build - the Descriptions of the shipping Section B facts are full of amounts that only a refused return can carry. THE REFUSAL IS UNCHANGED: /knockoutCasualtyGain's Derived body, its Export and its BlockSubmissionOnTrue are byte-identical to base 1c6758b26.]

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 33, casualty or theft gains from Form 4797, line 32
Fact.Description: Line 33: "Casualty or theft gains from Form 4797, line 32." The sum of /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPartIIILine32Remainder, gated on /claimsCasualtyLoss so it is Complete $0 on every return without a casualty collection. THE FIRST ADDEND OF LINE 36, beside the line-34 column (c) sum. It is 0 on every event that does not attest section 1245 property, which is every committed scenario and every committed fixture but the two this fill added, so it is byte-identical additive for the corpus. [2026-08-25, unit form4684-part-iii-other-recapture-classes: read "does not attest ANY of the three modeled classes" - sections 1250 and 1254 now route here too, and five committed fixtures rather than two carry a nonzero value. No committed SCENARIO answers any class attestation, so the byte-identical-additive claim is unchanged.] NOT A SECOND ROUTE FOR THE SAME DOLLAR: an event whose remainder enters here has ../longTermSectionBGain forced to 0 by the same ../sectionBPartIIIRecaptureApplies gate, because i4684 Line 33 says to complete line 33 "instead of Form 4684, line 34". The two per-event facts partition the gain; nothing is counted twice and nothing is dropped.

Fact.Name: The casualty share of Form 4797 Part III line 31, ordinary recapture to Form 4797 Part II line 13
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 31, "Add property columns A through D, lines 25b, 26g, 27c, 28b, and 29b. Enter here and on line 13" - the part of it contributed by CASUALTY or theft dispositions, which are Part III property columns like any other. The sum of /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture, gated on /claimsCasualtyLoss. WHY IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN form4797. Every operand is a Form 4684 fact: the gain is /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBCasualtyGainAmount and the depreciation is a per-event intake on this collection. form4797:/section1245Dispositions models a SALE and carries its own gross sales price; admitting a casualty into it would ask the filer for the same property twice, once on each form. So the arithmetic is done here and the TOTAL crosses the module boundary, exactly as /sectionBNetGainToForm4797 (line 39) already does for Part I line 3. ITS CONSUMER is form4797:/section1245OrdinaryRecapture, which is that module's name for line 31 and which carries it to Part II line 13 and thence into form4797:/form4797OrdinaryIncome and Schedule 1 line 4 - ORDINARY income, which is the whole point of the arm. Complete $0 on every return whose casualty events do not attest section 1245 property, which is the entire committed corpus. This fact is the sum of a CLASS SWITCH over lines 25b, 26g and 28b, so read "do not attest any of the three modeled classes". Its two per-class legibility siblings are /casualtyPartIIISection1250OrdinaryRecapture and /casualtyPartIIISection1254OrdinaryRecapture, which tie to this fact's per-class shares by construction.

Fact.Name: The casualty share of Form 4797 Part III line 26g, section 1250 ordinary recapture (legibility sibling)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer-level total of the per-event section 1250 casualty recapture (Form 4797 Part III line 26g summed across the casualty property columns). The CASUALTY twin of form4797:/section1250OrdinaryRecapture, gated on /claimsCasualtyLoss so a return with no casualty collection resolves Complete $0. IT ADDS NO SECOND ADDEND TO ANY TOTAL, AND THAT IS THE POINT - the same sentence its sale-side counterpart carries, for the same reason. The printed join is line 31, "Add property columns A through D, lines 25b, 26g, 27c, 28b, and 29b. Enter here and on line 13" - ONE line, which /casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture already performs now that /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture carries line 26g on its section 1250 arm. A second addend would count every section 1250 casualty recapture TWICE. ITS ONE CONSUMER is form4797:/section1250OrdinaryRecapture, the sale-side legibility head for the same printed line, which gains this as an addend in BOTH arms exactly as form4797:/section1245OrdinaryRecapture gained /casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture: a filer whose only Part III column is a casualty has no /section1245Dispositions item at all, so the addend has to sit outside the /claimsSection1245Disposition gate. IT TIES TO THE SECTION 1250 SHARE OF LINE 31 BY CONSTRUCTION - the double-attested event reads 5,000.00 at ../sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture and 0.00 at ../sectionBSection1250OrdinaryRecapture, and this fact reads 2,000.00, the second event's line 26g alone. Complete $0 on the entire committed corpus: no committed scenario answers a class attestation on a casualty event.

Fact.Name: The casualty share of Form 4797 Part III line 28b, section 1254 ordinary recapture (legibility sibling)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer-level total of the per-event section 1254 casualty recapture (Form 4797 Part III line 28b summed across the casualty property columns). The CASUALTY twin of form4797:/section1254OrdinaryRecapture, gated on /claimsCasualtyLoss so a return with no casualty collection resolves Complete $0. IT ADDS NO SECOND ADDEND TO ANY TOTAL - the printed join is line 31 and /casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture already performs it, now that /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture carries line 28b on its section 1254 arm. Its one consumer is form4797:/section1254OrdinaryRecapture, which gains it as an addend in BOTH arms, outside the /claimsSection1245Disposition gate, for the same reason its section 1250 and line-31 siblings did. IT SUMS ONLY THE EVENTS THAT TOOK THE SECTION 1254 ARM, which is one place it differs from its sale-side counterpart: form4797:/section1254OrdinaryRecapture sums its per-item line 28b UNCONDITIONALLY, harmlessly, because that fact is $0 for any item whose line 28a is unanswered. Here the per-event fact carries the class precedence in its own body, and this fact is the 2,500.00. Complete $0 on the entire committed corpus.

Fact.Name: The casualty share of Form 4797 Part III line 27c, section 1252 ordinary recapture (legibility sibling)

The CASUALTY twin of form4797:/section1252OrdinaryRecapture, gated on /claimsCasualtyLoss so a return with no casualty collection resolves Complete $0. IT ADDS NO SECOND ADDEND TO ANY TOTAL - the printed join is line 31 and /casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture already performs it, now that /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture carries line 27c on its section 1252 arm. Its one consumer is form4797:/section1252OrdinaryRecapture, which gains it as an addend in BOTH arms, outside the /claimsSection1245Disposition gate, for the same reason its section 1250, section 1254 and line-31 siblings did. Fact.Name: The casualty share of Form 4797 Part III line 29b, section 1255 ordinary recapture (legibility sibling)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer-level total of the per-event section 1255 casualty recapture (Form 4797 Part III line 29b summed across the casualty property columns).
