Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 36, total long-term Section B gains
Fact.Description: Line 36: "Total gains. Add lines 33 and 34, column (c)." The line-34 column (c) term is the sum of /casualtyEvents/*/longTermSectionBGain. LINE 33 IS STRUCTURALLY ZERO IN THIS BUILD AND IS NOT A FACT, which is a NAMED GAP rather than an omission. Line 33 is "Casualty or theft gains from Form 4797, line 32" - the remainder of a Form 4797 Part III recapture computation, which arrives here INSTEAD OF line 34 when a long-term gain is on depreciable property (i4684 Line 33: "If recapture applies, complete Form 4797, Part III, and this line, instead of Form 4684, line 34"). This dictionary's Form 4797 Part III models SALES of section 1245/1250/1254 property (form4797:/section1245Dispositions), never a casualty or theft disposition, and /casualtyEvents carries no depreciation-allowed intake, so no amount can reach line 33 by any route and no $0 leg is written for it. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT NEUTRAL: because the same gain would otherwise have been SPLIT - an ordinary recapture part on Form 4797 line 31 and thence Part II line 13, and only the remainder back here - routing the whole long-term gain to line 34 understates ordinary income and overstates section 1231 gain, which is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. That is arm (12) of the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain, and it is one of the reasons the guard still refuses the whole Section B population. [APPENDED 2026-08-25, frontier fill form4684-section-b-recapture-and-line18a, beside the paragraph above rather than over it. LINE 33 IS A FACT NOW and the sentence "LINE 33 IS STRUCTURALLY ZERO IN THIS BUILD AND IS NOT A FACT" is FALSE: it is /sectionBCasualtyGainsFromForm4797Line32, the first addend of the Add below, and /casualtyEvents now carries a depreciation-allowed intake (../writableCasualtyDepreciationAllowed) and a property-class attestation (../writableIsSection1245CasualtyProperty). The claim that "this dictionary's Form 4797 Part III models SALES ... never a casualty or theft disposition" is still true OF THAT COLLECTION and is no longer the whole story: the casualty Part III arithmetic is done HERE, on /casualtyEvents, and only its two totals cross to form4797 - the line-31 recapture through /casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture into form4797:/section1245OrdinaryRecapture, and the line-32 remainder back here as line 33. THE "CONSEQUENCE IS NOT NEUTRAL" PARAGRAPH SURVIVES FOR A SMALLER POPULATION, and that is the honest statement of what landed. The split now happens for an attested SECTION 1245 event. It does NOT happen for the other Part III classes - sections 1250, 1252, 1254 and 1255 - because none of their intakes exists on a casualty event: section 1250 alone would need an additional-depreciation-after-1975 figure and the applicable percentage. For those classes the whole long-term gain still routes to line 34, ordinary income is still understated and section 1231 gain still overstated, taxpayer-FAVOURABLY. THAT RESIDUAL IS WHY ARM (12) IS DISCHARGED FOR THE SECTION 1245 CLASS ONLY, and it is recorded on the rebody contract as item (18) rather than left as silence. [2026-08-25, unit form4684-part-iii-other-recapture-classes: "It does NOT happen for the other Part III classes - sections 1250, 1252, 1254 and 1255 - because none of their intakes exists on a casualty event: section 1250 alone would need an additional-depreciation-after-1975 figure and the applicable percentage" is FALSE for sections 1250 and 1254 as of today. Both intakes exist, the applicable percentage is the constant 100% rather than an intake, and the split happens for all three modeled classes. The residual is sections 1252 and 1255 alone.] It is also unreachable in production: /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain, of any class.]

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 37, total long-term Section B losses across both columns
Fact.Description: Line 37: "Add amounts on line 35, columns (b)(i) and (b)(ii)." /sectionBLongTermLossColumnBi plus /sectionBLongTermLossColumnBii, POSITIVE - a magnitude, because the printed line-35 entries sit in parentheses and line 38 speaks of "the loss on line 37" as a quantity to be compared with a gain. This is the ONE quantity Part II tests: line 38 fires when it is MORE than line 36, line 39 when it is less than or equal.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 38a, the long-term column (b)(i) exit to Form 4797 line 14
Fact.Description: Line 38a, taken ONLY on the line-38 branch: "If the loss on line 37 is more than the gain on line 36: a Combine line 35, column (b)(i), and line 36, and enter the net gain or (loss) here ... All others, enter this amount on Form 4797, line 14." So it is /sectionBLongTermGain minus /sectionBLongTermLossColumnBi, and 0 whenever line 37 is less than or equal to line 36 - because that is the line-39 branch, where the whole long-term half leaves on Form 4797 line 3 instead and line 38a is not completed at all. MAY BE POSITIVE EVEN ON ITS OWN BRANCH. The branch test compares line 36 with BOTH loss columns, while line 38a subtracts only column (b)(i), line 37 is 11,000 and this fact is 2,000. THE BOUNDARY IS AT EQUALITY AND THE FORM IS NOT SILENT ABOUT IT, unlike i4684 Line 11: line 38 says "more than" and line 39 says "less than or equal to", so equality belongs to line 39 and this fact is 0 there.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 38b, the long-term column (b)(ii) exit to Schedule A line 16
Fact.Description: Line 38b, taken ONLY on the line-38 branch: "Enter the amount from line 35, column (b)(ii), here. Individuals, enter the amount from income-producing property on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16 ... (Do not include any loss on property used as an employee.)" So it is /sectionBLongTermLossColumnBii on that branch and 0 on the other. POSITIVE. The second addend of /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss. THE BRANCH IS WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM LINE 32, and it is the whole reason /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss can no longer be the plain sum of column (b)(ii). On the line-39 branch a long-term income-producing loss does NOT reach Schedule A line 16: it is netted into line 39 and leaves on Form 4797 line 3, where the printed form's own redistribution mechanism is Form 4797 line 18a - which this build does not model, for the reasons at /sectionBLongTermLossColumnBii. On the LINE-39 branch this fact is 0 and Form 4797 line 18a (form4797:/lossFromForm4684ColumnBiiOnLineEleven) is the route; on the LINE-38 branch this fact carries the loss and 18a is 0. The two branches are complementary, so the loss is deducted exactly once. Where Form 4797 line 7 is a GAIN there is no loss on Form 4797 line 11, line 18a's own first printed condition fails, and the loss reaches Schedule A line 16 as nothing at all.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 39, the long-term net GAIN exit to Form 4797 Part I line 3
Fact.Description: Line 39: "If the loss on line 37 is less than or equal to the gain on line 36, combine lines 36 and 37 and enter here ... All others, enter this amount on Form 4797, line 3." So it is /sectionBLongTermGain minus /sectionBLongTermLossTotal on that branch and 0 on the other. NON-NEGATIVE BY ITS OWN BRANCH CONDITION, not by a floor: the branch is taken exactly when line 37 is at most line 36, so the subtraction cannot go below zero, and no GreaterOf is written because writing one would hide a future arithmetic error rather than prevent one. The Form 4797 side reads it as a gain and says so: line 3 is "Gain, if any, from Form 4684, line 39". WHAT IT CARRIES, AND IT IS NOT ONLY GAIN: line 37 is BOTH long-term loss columns, so a column (b)(ii) income-producing loss travels inside this figure on this branch instead of reaching Schedule A line 16 at line 38b. The printed form's redistribution for that is Form 4797 line 18a, unbuilt here - see /sectionBLongTermLossColumnBii. THE SHORT-TERM HALF NEVER COMES HERE. Line 31 is unconditional and goes to Form 4797 line 14; only the long-term half forks, which is why a return can report a positive line 31 and a positive line 39 at the same time. EXPORTED. The sole consumer is form4797:/casualtyGainFromForm4684, Form 4797 Part I line 3, which is an addend of form4797:/netSection1231GainOrLoss (line 7). ADDITIVITY: gated through /sectionBLongTermGain and /sectionBLongTermLossTotal, both of which are gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss, so a return with no casualty claim resolves Complete 0; and on a return with Section B LOSSES ONLY, line 36 and line 37 are both 0, the branch is taken, and this fact is 0 - so every scenario predating this arm is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Net gain or (loss) from Section B business property (Form 4684 lines 31 and 38a, to Form 4797 line 14)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B Part II, the column (b)(i) exit. Line 31: "Combine line 30, columns (b)(i) and (c). Enter the net gain or (loss) here and on Form 4797, line 14" (the property held one year or less). Line 38a: "Combine line 35, column (b)(i), and line 36, and enter the net gain or (loss) here ... All others, enter this amount on Form 4797, line 14" (the property held more than one year). Form 4797 line 14 is the sum of both (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2). WHY THERE IS NO HOLDING-PERIOD FORK HERE, which is the one non-obvious modelling choice in this arm. The two halves of Part II differ only by the GAIN terms they carry, and every Section B gain term is identically zero in this build: column (c) ("Gains from casualties or thefts includible in income") has no intake, because a casualty GAIN - Section B line 22, "Gain from casualty or theft. If line 21 is more than line 20" - is REFUSED by /knockoutCasualtyGain, whose Count(/casualtyEvents/*/hasCasualtyGain) test is Section A line 4's reimbursement-over-basis condition and is therefore already Section B line 22's condition, collection-wide, with no edit; and line 33, "Casualty or theft gains from Form 4797, line 32", has no intake anywhere in this dictionary and enters as nothing. With the gain terms zero, line 31 + line 38a collapses to the NEGATIVE of every column (b)(i) loss regardless of holding period, and line 39 (the net-gain branch, which would leave on Form 4797 line 3 instead) is zero too. SHOULD A LATER UNIT GIVE LINE 33 OR COLUMN (c) AN INTAKE, THIS COLLAPSE IS INVALID AND THE HOLDING-PERIOD FORK BECOMES REQUIRED - this sentence is the marker for that. SIGN: SIGNED, and negative for the loss-only population this arm models (the printed line says "net gain or (loss)" and column (b)(i) prints its entries in parentheses). Gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so every return without a casualty loss resolves Complete 0, and built from /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLossColumnBi, which is 0 on every event that is not attested column (b)(i) - so every scenario predating this arm is byte-identical. EXPORTED; the sole consumer is form4797:/casualtyOrTheftNetGainOrLoss (Form 4797 line 14). COLUMN (b)(ii) IS STILL NOT HERE, and now it is elsewhere rather than nowhere: income- producing property leaves on lines 32 and 38b to Schedule A line 16, as /incomeProducingCasualtyLoss. This sum reads the per-event (b)(i) COLUMN fact, not /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBCasualtyLoss itself, precisely so that widening the shared Section B chain's gate to cover both columns did not pull (b)(ii) losses onto Form 4797 line 14 - which would move an itemized deduction above the line, the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE error. This fact is line 31 plus line 38a as the printed form computes each of them, i.e. /sectionBShortTermNetGainOrLoss plus /sectionBLongTermNetGainOrLoss, and the holding-period sort behind them reads /casualtyEvents/*/heldMoreThanOneYear. It can be POSITIVE, because line 31 combines a column (c) gain with a column (b)(i) loss and carries no floor. Line 33 has no intake: see /sectionBLongTermGain. With column (c) zero, /casualtyEvents/*/heldMoreThanOneYear resolves a complete FALSE on every event, so every column (b)(i) loss sorts short-term; line 31 is then 0 minus the whole column; line 36 and line 37 are both 0, so the line-39 branch is taken and line 38a is 0.

Fact.Name: Casualty or theft loss of income-producing property (Form 4684 lines 32 and 38b, to Schedule A line 16)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B Part II, the column (b)(ii) exit. Line 32: "Enter the amount from line 30, column (b)(ii), here. Individuals, enter the amount from income-producing property on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16 ... (Do not include any loss on property used as an employee.)" (the property held one year or less). Line 38b says the same of line 35, column (b)(ii) (held more than one year). Schedule A line 16 is the sum of both (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2), and the Schedule A instructions name exactly those two lines in the closed line-16 list: "Casualty and theft losses of income-producing property (including losses from financial scams) from Form 4684, lines 32 and 38b, or Form 4797, line 18a" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sca.pdf, page 11). SIGN: POSITIVE, unlike its column (b)(i) sibling /sectionBNetGainOrLoss. Schedule A line 16 is a deduction column whose other terms (/gamblingLossDeduction, /otherItemizedWriteIn) are positive; the negative "net gain or (loss)" convention belongs to Form 4797 line 14, which this column never touches. The per-event source ../sectionBLossColumnBii is already positive. WHY THERE IS NO HOLDING-PERIOD FORK, argued from the printed lines rather than inherited from the sibling. Line 32 is unconditional. Line 38b sits under line 38, "If the loss on line 37 is more than the gain on line 36", and line 36 ("Total gains. Add lines 33 and 34, column (c)") is identically ZERO in this build for the reasons /sectionBNetGainOrLoss sets out: column (c) has no intake because a casualty GAIN is refused by /knockoutCasualtyGain, and line 33 has no intake anywhere in this dictionary. So whenever any Section B loss exists line 37 exceeds line 36 = 0, the line-38 branch is always the one taken, and line 32 + line 38b = every column (b)(ii) loss regardless of holding period. IF A LATER UNIT GIVES LINE 33 OR COLUMN (c) AN INTAKE, THIS COLLAPSE DIES exactly as the sibling's does. FORM 4797 LINE 18a IS THE OTHER ROUTE TO SCHEDULE A LINE 16, AND IT IS ZERO IN THIS SCOPE - stated here because the instruction quoted above says "or", i.e. the two routes feed the SAME line and a live line 18a alongside this fact would DOUBLE-COUNT. Line 18a reads "If the loss on line 11 includes a loss from Form 4684, line 35, column (b)(ii), enter that part of the loss here" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1). RE-DERIVED 2026-08-03 at this landing, and the ground the Section B landing gave is NOT the ground that holds. That landing argued line 18a keys off Form 4797 line 11, "which no Form 4684 amount reaches in this dictionary - line 14 is a Part II line". Line 14 is indeed a Part II line, but line 18a does not travel by line 14: the printed route is Form 4684 line 35 column (b)(ii) into line 37 ("Add amounts on line 35, columns (b)(i) and (b)(ii)"), into line 39 ("If the loss on line 37 is less than or equal to the gain on line 36 ... enter this amount on Form 4797, line 3"), into Form 4797 PART I line 3 ("Gain, if any, from Form 4684, line 39"), line 7, line 11 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1). That path exists on the printed forms. What makes line 18a zero HERE is contingent, not structural, and is two things: Form 4797 Part I line 3 has no intake in this dictionary at all, and the line-39 branch it would travel requires line 36 (total casualty GAINS) to equal or exceed line 37, which cannot happen while /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return with a casualty gain. So line 18a is identically 0, line 18b equals line 17, and this fact is the only thing reaching Schedule A line 16 from a casualty. THE MARKER: a unit that lifts the gain knockout, or gives line 33 or column (c) an intake, must model line 18a AND make it mutually exclusive with this fact. THIS LINE ALSO CARRIES THE SECTION C (Ponzi-type safe harbor) LOSS, and the instruction quoted above is what says so rather than an inference: its parenthesis, "(including losses from financial scams)", is the only place in the Schedule A line-16 closed list where a Ponzi-type theft loss can be. The route is Form 4684 Section C line 51 to Section B Part I line 28 (/casualtyEvents/*/sectionBCasualtyLoss) to column (b)(ii) (/casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLossColumnBii) to here, and the holding-period collapse argued above applies to it unchanged. ADDITIVITY: gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so every return without a casualty loss resolves Complete 0, and built from ../sectionBLossColumnBii, which is 0 on every event whose ../writableIsIncomeProducingProperty AND ../writableIsPonziSafeHarborTheft are both unanswered - i.e. on the entire pre-existing corpus. EXPORTED; the sole consumer is scheduleA:/otherItemizedDeductions. This fact is line 32 plus line 38b as the form computes each - /sectionBShortTermIncomeProducingLoss plus /sectionBLongTermIncomeProducingLoss - and the short-term half is unconditional. When long-term gains at least equal long-term losses the LINE-39 branch is taken, line 38b is not completed, and the long-term column (b)(ii) loss does not reach Schedule A line 16 at all: it is netted inside line 39 and leaves on Form 4797 line 3 (form4797:/casualtyGainFromForm4684). Line 33 is still zero and still has no intake. With line 36 and line 37 both 0 the line-39 branch is taken, line 38b is 0, every loss sorts short-term through a complete-FALSE /casualtyEvents/*/heldMoreThanOneYear, and line 32 collects the whole column (b)(ii).. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540) Part II line 29 worksheet line 16 exclusions).

Fact.Name: Total REALIZED casualty and theft gain, both sections, before section 1033/121 non-recognition (Form 4684 line 4 / line 22)
Fact.Description:
The GROSS total of every event's casualty or theft gain: CollectionSum over /casualtyEvents/*/casualtyGainAmount, gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss so a return with no casualty claim resolves Complete 0 rather than Incomplete. ONE fact sums BOTH sections because /casualtyEvents/*/hasCasualtyGain does not consult the section fork - Section A line 4 and Section B line 22 are the same subtraction - so a Schedule-D-only successor would have left a Section B gain refused while the burn-down read clean.
PLAINLY: THIS FACT IS THE REALIZED GAIN, NOT THE RECOGNIZED ONE. The path name is the discharged contract's own name and is kept for that reason, but the figure it carries is the pre-1033/pre-121 amount - reimbursement over adjusted basis, form-stated, nothing more. Section 1033 non-recognition on involuntary conversions (including the MANDATORY rule of 1033(h)(1)(A)(i) for a federally declared disaster - not an election at all) and the section 121 main-home exclusion are NOT applied by this fact or by anything downstream of it today. Modeling both is a named successor.
THIS DISCHARGES THE ARITHMETIC HALF OF THE /knockoutCasualtyGain CONTRACT AND NOTHING ELSE. The guard is NOT retired. It still blocks submission on every return that has a casualty gain, so this fact moves no dollar on any return today. It is exported so the owed legs can consume it when they land.
NINE THINGS THIS FACT DOES NOT DO, each named rather than left for a reader to assume.
(1) IT DOES NOT ROUTE. Section A line 15 sends the netted gain to Schedule D ("If line 13 is more than line 14, enter the difference here and on Schedule D", f4684 line 58) and Section B line 39 sends one to Form 4797 line 3 (f4684 lines 138-139). Neither destination is wired by this fill, and ../isSectionB is not consulted here.
(2) IT IS THE GROSS LINE-4-PLUS-LINE-22 TOTAL, AND IT IS NEITHER SECTION A LINE 13 NOR LINE 15. Line 13 is "Add the amounts on line 4 of all Forms 4684" - Section A only - so this fact COINCIDES with line 13 on a return whose events are all Section A, and exceeds it as soon as a Section B event has a line-22 gain, because a Section B gain leaves on line 29 or line 34 column (c), never through line 13. Line 15 is a different quantity again: line 13 over line 14, i.e. the gains NET of the floored losses. This fact is the UN-NETTED sum, published in exactly that form so a later line-13 / line-15 fact can net and split it rather than re-derive it.
(3) IT CARRIES NO HOLDING PERIOD. Schedule D splits Part I (assets held one year or less) from Part II (more than one year), so an amount arriving there must pick a side. The intake /casualtyEvents/*/writableCasualtyGainPropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear is CONTRACTED in the records overlay and is not built here; this total therefore cannot pick one. [APPENDED 2026-08-24, frontier fill form4684-casualty-gain, beside item (3) rather than over it, because ITS SECOND SENTENCE IS NOW FALSE. The intake IS built, and not at the path named: that contract node is DELETED and what ships is the WIDER /casualtyEvents/*/writablePropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear, answered on Section A LOSS events as well as gain events. A SECTION B gain, which is inside this total and outside that one, still has no route to Form 4797 line 3.]
(4) IT APPLIES NO IRC 1033 DEFERRAL. 1033(a)(2)(A) is an ELECTION, never automatic, bounded by a replacement period (2 years under 1033(a)(2)(B)(i); 4 years for a principal residence in a disaster area under 1033(h)(1)(B)), and partial when the replacement costs less than the reimbursement. 1033(h)(1)(A)(i) is NOT an election at all - insurance proceeds for UNSCHEDULED personal property that was part of the contents of a principal residence in a disaster area are non-recognized as a matter of law. Neither the election nor the replacement-cost intake exists in this dictionary. Modeling this is the same successor.
(5) IT APPLIES NO IRC 121 MAIN-HOME EXCLUSION. Pub. 547 states that the gain from a destroyed main home is excludable as if the home had been sold, and only the excess is a candidate for the 1033 postponement. This dictionary models no section 121 exclusion anywhere, and this fact does not invent one. Modeling this is also that successor.
(6) IT DOES NOT MOVE THE FIVE IRC 165(h) LOSS-SIDE COUPLINGS a casualty gain reshapes. FIVE, not the four the guard's own supervisor rows still say: the four they name, plus the per-casualty floor flip at (v), which no record in this module named before this unit's condition enumeration. (i) 165(h)(2)(A): the 10-percent-of-AGI limit applies to the EXCESS of losses over gains and the gains are added back, so a gain RAISES the allowable loss ("such losses shall be allowed for the taxable year only to the extent of the sum of-", usc26-165 line 78, with clauses (i) and (ii) at lines 80 and 82). THE FACT THAT MUST CHANGE IS NOT /casualtyLossTenPercentAgi: that fact is Round(10/100 times taxCalculations:/agi) and per the form should have no gain term, because line 17 is "Enter 10% of your adjusted gross income", full stop. The gain enters at LINE 16, which has no fact of its own - /casualtyLossDeduction computes GreaterOf(/casualtyLossAfterFloors minus /casualtyLossTenPercentAgi, 0) - i.e. line 14 minus line 17, which collapses line 16 and line 18 into one node because lines 13 and 15 are BOTH zero for as long as the gain is refused. Same arithmetic, different fact. (ii) 165(h)(4)(A): losses matched against gains become "a deduction allowable in computing adjusted gross income to the extent such losses do not exceed the personal casualty gains for the taxable year" (line 108). The shipping chain routes the whole loss to Schedule A line 15 through /casualtyLossDeduction. (iii) 165(h)(5)(B)(i): once a gain exists, the federally-declared-disaster limitation "shall not apply to the portion of the personal casualty loss not attributable to a Federally declared disaster ... to the extent such loss does not exceed such gains" (line 136), while /casualtyEvents/*/isEligible zeroes a non-disaster event unconditionally. Clause (ii) is a SUB-RULE of this same coupling, not a sixth one: it is the no-double-count rule, "the amount of personal casualty gains taken into account under paragraph (2)(A) shall be reduced by the portion of such gains taken into account under clause (i)" (line 138). (iv) 165(h)(2)(B): when the gains exceed the losses the CHARACTER of everything flips - "all such gains shall be treated as gains from sales or exchanges of capital assets" (line 88), with the mirror for losses at line 90. (v) THE PER-CASUALTY FLOOR FLIP, the fifth coupling. The 2025 i4684 line-11 instruction adds the line-4 gains from all Forms 4684 and compares the sum with line 10: $500 if line 10 is larger, $100 if it is smaller OR if the filer is reporting a (non-qualified) disaster loss - the instruction's own second disjunct (i4684 lines 532-541, RIGHT column). That floor reaches the standard-deduction comparison through Schedule A, and /casualtyEvents/*/deductibleLossAfterFloor applies it unconditionally today.
(7) IT DOES NOT WIDEN THE DOOR. /claimsCasualtyLoss asks whether the filer had a casualty or theft LOSS. A filer with a casualty GAIN and no loss answers no, /casualtyEvents is never populated, and the gain is today neither computed, nor refused, nor reported - it falls outside the model entirely. The contract names widening that intake as the successor's scope; this fill carries the gate forward unchanged and says so.
(8) IT ASSUMES THE REIMBURSEMENT WAS CLAIMED AND RECEIVED. Where the filer was entitled to a reimbursement and chose not to file a claim, line 4 is measured from the amount ACTUALLY RECEIVED rather than from line 3 (i4684 lines 511-518, LEFT column). No intake distinguishes the two, so every gain fixture states in its own description that the proceeds were received and the claim filed.
(9) IT HAS NO TIMING TERM. A reimbursement not received until after the year of the casualty is included in income in the LATER year (i4684 lines 520-523, LEFT column). Nothing here asks when the payment arrived.
None of the nine is silenced. Each is a MISSING INPUT FACT or an unbuilt leg, and each is owed by name on the rebody contract at /knockoutCasualtyGain - which is why the refusal stays.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a casualty or theft event has a net GAIN (reimbursement exceeds basis)
Fact.Description: Submission-blocking knockout: fires when the return claims a casualty loss AND any event is a casualty GAIN (/casualtyEvents/*/hasCasualtyGain - reimbursement over basis, Form 4684 line 4). A gain is RECOGNIZED INCOME that Form 4684 routes to Schedule D; this unit models the LOSS deduction only and does not compute the gain, so silently flooring it at 0 (the prior behavior) would DELETE taxable income and under-report the return - an unbounded World-#1 violation, since the under-payment and its penalty exposure are the taxpayer's and reimbursement has no cap. Rather than file a wrong return, the engine REFUSES. Dual-wired like every sibling knockout (its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue + membership in flow /flowIsKnockedOut). Gated by /claimsCasualtyLoss and built on the complete-safe per-event gate, so it resolves Complete false on every return without a casualty gain - byte-identical additive (no existing scenario has reimbursement > basis). Section B line 22 is Section A line 4's condition verbatim - "Gain from casualty or theft. If line 21 [reimbursement] is more than line 20 [basis]" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 2) - and ../hasCasualtyGain is a collection-wide test that does not consult the section fork, so a business-property gain is refused for the same reason a personal one is. Only the DESTINATION differs and neither is modeled: a Section A gain would route to Schedule D (line 4), a Section B gain to Form 4797 line 3 via line 39 ("If the loss on line 37 is less than or equal to the gain on line 36, combine lines 36 and 37 ... enter this amount on Form 4797, line 3", lines 138-139). Computing either is a separate unit; note that such a unit must also restore the holding-period fork /sectionBNetGainOrLoss's Description explains away. [APPENDED 2026-08-21, frontier fill, beside the sentences above rather than over them: the successor's ARITHMETIC half now SHIPS in this file as /personalAndBusinessCasualtyGainRecognized, the gross Form 4684 line-4 / line-22 total across both sections, summed from the per-event /casualtyEvents/*/recognizedCasualtyGainAmount [CORRECTED 2026-08-25, frontier lane c, unit form4684-casualty-gain-missing-inputs: this sentence named /casualtyEvents/*/casualtyGainAmount, the REALIZED line-4 gain, which made this fact's own path name - "Recognized" - false of it. Fact.Name: This event recovers a loss deducted on an earlier year's return and prints no line-4 gain (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE on an event where all three of these hold: the filer attests the loss on this property was already deducted on an EARLIER year's return (../lossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn), a reimbursement for it is measured in the tax year (../lineFourReimbursementMeasure is more than zero), and Form 4684 line 4 prints nothing because that measure does not exceed the basis entered on line 2 (../hasCasualtyGain is false).
THE POPULATION, stated plainly: a filer who entered basis UNREDUCED by the earlier deduction - which is what line 2's caption asks for, "Cost or other basis of each property" - and is reimbursed BELOW that basis. Line 4 is skipped, this module resolves a zero gain, and the return carries no income anywhere for the money that came back. Pub. 547 owes an inclusion: "If you recover an amount you deducted as a loss in an earlier year, you may have to include the amount recovered in your income for the year of recovery", capped by IRC 111(a) at the part of the deduction that reduced tax. The direction of the error is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE (income omitted), and the taxpayer carries the under-payment, so the return is REFUSED at /knockoutPriorYearCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome rather than filed.
THE REMEDY IS NOT A BIGGER FORM 4684 GAIN. Reducing basis by the earlier deduction coincides with the owed inclusion only on a total loss; the recovery is other income for the year of recovery (Pub. 547 sends the reader to Recoveries in Pub. 525), i.e. a Schedule 1 line 8z leg, computed at ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome when ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIsMeasurable is true and refused by /knockoutPriorYearCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome otherwise.
EVERY OPERAND IS READ IsComplete-FIRST, so an unanswered answer never refuses. All three are complete-safe by construction today and the wrappers keep this fact safe if one of them ever stops being. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, including an event that answers nothing.

Fact.Name: How much casualty or theft loss deduction for this event was allowed on the earlier year's return?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "How much of this loss did you actually deduct on your return for the earlier year, after the $100 and 10%-of-AGI reductions?" Shown once per event that answered ../writableLossDeductedOnEarlierYearReturn TRUE, a personal-use (Section A) event, and a reimbursement in this tax year that does not exceed the basis entered for the property.
HELP TEXT: Enter the deduction that was ALLOWED for this event on the earlier return, not the loss before the reductions: the Form 4684 Section A amount after line 11's $100 reduction and the 10%-of-AGI reduction on line 17, as it reached Schedule A or the increased standard deduction. If you later receive a reimbursement for a loss you deducted, you include it in income in the year you get it, but only up to the part of the earlier deduction that reduced your tax.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED, not defaulted. Without this figure the recovery cannot be measured, so the return stays blocked by /knockoutPriorYearCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome caps the includible recovery at this amount less ../priorYearDeductionNoTaxBenefitPortion. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0; a negative answer is floored at $0 where it is used.

Fact.Name: How much reimbursement for this event had you expected, and subtracted, but not yet received when you figured the earlier year's deduction?
Fact.Description:
QUESTION TEXT: "When you figured the deduction on your earlier year's return, how much reimbursement did you expect to receive later and subtract from the loss?" Shown with ../writablePriorYearAllowedCasualtyDeduction, on the same events. Enter $0 if you expected none.
HELP TEXT: A reimbursement you already subtracted as expected was never deducted, so receiving it is not income. Only the part of this year's reimbursement above what you expected is a recovery of the earlier deduction; if you receive exactly what you expected, none of it is income.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED, not defaulted. Assuming $0 would include a reimbursement the filer never deducted, so the return stays blocked by /knockoutPriorYearCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome until this is answered.
WHAT IT FEEDS: ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome subtracts it from this year's reimbursement before the cap. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0; a negative answer is floored at $0 where it is used.

Fact.Name: This event's recovery of an earlier-year casualty deduction can be measured (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../priorYearDeductionRecoveredWithNoLineFourGain is true, the event is a personal-use (Section A) event, both ../writablePriorYearAllowedCasualtyDeduction and ../writablePriorYearExpectedReimbursementNotYetReceived are answered, and this year's reimbursement is not LESS than the reimbursement expected. Only then does ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome compute a recovery; otherwise the event is counted by /knockoutPriorYearCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome. A reimbursement below what was expected is not measurable here because it owes the opposite adjustment, an additional LOSS for the year no more reimbursement is expected, which this module does not compute, so that event is refused rather than filed without the loss. A Section B (business or income-producing) event is never measurable here: a recovery of a deduction taken in figuring adjusted gross income is not an itemized-deduction recovery and no printed line this dictionary has vendored sends it to Schedule 1 line 8z. Complete on every event.

Fact.Name: Recovery of an earlier year's casualty or theft deduction included in income (Schedule 1 line 8z)
Fact.Description:
The part of this tax year's reimbursement that recovers a casualty or theft loss deducted on an earlier year's return, included in income for this year as other income on Schedule 1 line 8z. It is this year's reimbursement (../lineFourReimbursementMeasure) less the reimbursement already expected when the earlier deduction was figured, floored at $0, and then capped at the earlier ALLOWED deduction less the part of it that did not reduce tax (../priorYearDeductionNoTaxBenefitPortion), floored at $0. $0 on every event that is not measurable (see ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIsMeasurable), including every event with a Form 4684 line 4 gain. Positive, integer cents.
THE TAX-BENEFIT LIMIT IS APPLIED ONCE PER EVENT. An event with a line 4 gain has the no-tax-benefit portion subtracted from ../casualtyGainAmount and is never measurable here; an event measured here has no line 4 gain, so that subtraction does not reach it.

Fact.Name: This event recovers an earlier-year casualty deduction that cannot be measured (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../priorYearDeductionRecoveredWithNoLineFourGain is true and ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIsMeasurable is false: a Section B event, a personal-use event whose earlier allowed deduction or outstanding expected reimbursement is unanswered, or one reimbursed less than was expected. Read only by /knockoutPriorYearCasualtyLossRecoveryIncome. Complete on every event.

Fact.Name: Recoveries of earlier-year casualty and theft deductions included in income, all events
Fact.Description: The sum of ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome over every casualty event: the amount of casualty and theft loss deductions from earlier years recovered this year and included in income as other income on Schedule 1 line 8z. $0 on a return with no casualty events, including one that never opened the casualty questions. Positive, integer cents.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a casualty loss deducted in an earlier year is recovered and the recovery income is not computed
Fact.Description:
Submission-blocking knockout. Fires when any event resolves ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryNotMeasured true: the loss was deducted on an earlier year's return, a reimbursement is measured in the tax year, Form 4684 line 4 prints nothing because the reimbursement does not exceed the basis the filer entered, AND the recovery cannot be measured - the event is a Section B (business or income-producing) event, the earlier year's allowed deduction or the reimbursement already expected when it was figured is unanswered, or this year's reimbursement is less than the reimbursement expected (which owes an additional loss, not income). That return owes the recovery as income under Pub. 547 and IRC 111(a) and this dictionary cannot compute it, so filing it would UNDER-REPORT income by up to the whole recovery. Rather than file a wrong return, the engine REFUSES.
WHAT NO LONGER REFUSES: a personal-use event with both intakes answered. Its recovery is computed at ../priorYearDeductionRecoveryIncome and reaches Schedule 1 line 8z through /priorYearCasualtyDeductionRecoveryIncome.
DUAL-WIRED like every sibling knockout in this module: its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue plus membership in flow /flowIsKnockedOut. Gated on IsComplete(/casualtyEvents) so a return that never opens the collection does not make the Any Incomplete, and built on the complete-safe per-event gate, so it resolves Complete false on every return outside the population and keeps /flowIsKnockedOut Complete everywhere.

Fact.Name: This Section B financial-scam event is missing its perpetrator name (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: True when this event actually prints Section B Part I, the financial-scam attestation is answered true, and its required line-19 perpetrator name is unanswered. Section C is a Section B loss destination but does not print lines 19-27, so it must not trigger this Section B identity requirement. An unanswered scam attestation is complete-safe false. The identification number and address are not tested because the instructions qualify those fields "if known". This fact is read only by the top-level refusal.

Fact.Name: A Section B financial-scam loss is missing its perpetrator name (refusal)
A Rev. Proc. 2009-20 safe-harbor claim is missing its required Part II perpetrator identity (refusal)
Fact.Description:
THE REFUSAL, NOT A SILENT BLANK. Form 4684 Section C Part II's "Required Statements and Declarations" carries three captions for the individual or entity that ran the fraudulent arrangement: "Name of individual or entity", "Taxpayer identification number (if known)" and "Address" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4684.pdf, page 3). Two of the three - NAME and ADDRESS - carry NO "(if known)" qualifier; only the TIN does. The safe harbor itself is granted only to a filer who signs these Part II statements, so a claim with the identity blank is claiming the safe harbor without evidencing its own conditions.
WHY NAME AND ADDRESS AND NOT TIN. The printed form itself draws the line: TIN alone carries "(if known)", so ../writablePonziPerpetratorTin stays genuinely optional (its own Description was never self-contradictory - it never claimed to be "required text"). Name and Address carry no such qualifier and are therefore required whenever a filer attests ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft.
WHY BlockSubmissionOnTrue AND NOT A SILENT DEFAULT. Zeroing an unanswered required field would let the full Rev. Proc. 2009-20 deduction (../ponziDeductibleTheftLoss, potentially 95% of the loss) reach Form 4684 line 28 with the identity caption blank - the safe harbor claimed without its own required evidencing. This mirrors the shipping BlockSubmissionOnTrue idiom (hsa.xml /hasHsaDistributionsWithoutActivity, dividendReports.xml /secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ): a per-event Boolean, Counted at the top level, compared GreaterThan 0.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT: ../casualtyEvents/*/ponziIdentityRequiredButMissing is built from ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft (complete-safe) and Not(IsComplete(...)) on the two String writables (IsComplete itself never resolves Incomplete), so this Count-based fact is complete-safe too.

Fact.Name: FEMA DR- major-disaster declaration number for this event
Fact.Description: The FEMA DR- (major disaster) declaration number the filer enters beside the Section A federally-declared-disaster checkbox on Form 4684 page 1. A faithful-record intake: the engine gates deductibility on the attestation /casualtyEvents/*/federallyDeclaredDisaster and does not validate or parse the number, so this leaf plays no part in any computation. Digits only as printed after the preprinted DR- prefix. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves the box blank and changes no tax value; a filer whose declaration is an emergency rather than a major disaster answers /casualtyEvents/*/writableFemaEmDeclarationNumber instead.

Fact.Name: FEMA EM- emergency declaration number for this event
Fact.Description: The FEMA EM- (emergency) declaration number the filer enters beside the Section A federally-declared-disaster checkbox on Form 4684 page 1, the alternative to the DR- box printed next to it. A faithful-record intake on the same terms as /casualtyEvents/*/writableFemaDrDeclarationNumber: the deduction gate is the attestation /casualtyEvents/*/federallyDeclaredDisaster, and this leaf is never read by any computation. Digits only as printed after the preprinted EM- prefix. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves the box blank and changes no tax value.

Fact.Name: Casualty property city and state (Form 4684 line 1)
Fact.Description: The city and state of the property lost or damaged in this casualty or theft event, the second column of the Form 4684 line 1 description table. A faithful-record field that plays no part in any computation; the line-1 type column is carried by /casualtyEvents/*/description and this leaf carries the location half of the same printed row. Because the form renders once per event and this dictionary models one property per event, the value prints in the Property A row and rows B-D stay blank. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves the cell blank and changes no tax value.

Fact.Name: Casualty property ZIP code (Form 4684 line 1)
Fact.Description: The ZIP code of the property lost or damaged in this casualty or theft event, the third column of the Form 4684 line 1 description table. The form makes this cell load-bearing for the FEMA box above it - a filer who checked the federally-declared-disaster box enters here the ZIP code for the property most affected - but it is still a faithful-record field that no computation reads; deductibility is gated by /casualtyEvents/*/federallyDeclaredDisaster. Typed String rather than a postal primitive because the graph has no ZIP type. Because the form renders once per event and this dictionary models one property per event, the value prints in the Property A row and rows B-D stay blank. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves the cell blank and changes no tax value.

Fact.Name: This event belongs in the Form 4684 Section B Part II LONG TERM half (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: TRUE when this event is a Section B event whose property was held more than one year, so its row is printed under the line 34 heading "Casualty or Theft of Property Held More Than One Year" rather than under line 29's "Casualty or Theft of Property Held One Year or Less". FALSE otherwise, including on every Section A event. IT IS A SWITCH, NOT AN All, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. ../heldMoreThanOneYear is deliberately allowed to go Incomplete on an event whose holding period the return actually needs, so every Section B sort in this module reads it behind an ../isSectionB short circuit, in the words of the existing facts: a Section A event has no Part II cell, short circuited so the Section B holding period sort never reads the holding period on an event whose Section A requiredness has left it Incomplete. Conjoining the two with All would lose that short circuit and carry the Incomplete out. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT. It exists so a Part II row can be gated as a whole: today only ../longTermSectionBDescription reads it, for the line 34 column (a) cell, whose value is text and therefore cannot carry the sort in a zero the way the six amount columns do.

Fact.Name: This event is not a Section C Ponzi safe harbor theft
Fact.Description: The negation of ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft, needed because Form 4684 Section C line 51 says of a safe harbor loss "Include this amount on line 28 of Section B, Part I. Do not complete lines 19–27 for this loss": the Section C event travels Section B Part II but its Part I measurement boxes stay EMPTY. form4684.xml already writes that exclusion inline, as All(../isSectionB, Not(../isPonziSafeHarborTheft)) on ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement; the supported templates have no inline Not inside an All, so the negation is named here and combined at ../printsSectionBPartIProperty. Read only by that fact.

Fact.Name: The per event floor Form 4684 line 11 prints for this event (100 or 500 dollars)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 11 as printed: $500 when this event keeps the qualified disaster floor (../qualifiedDisasterFiveHundredFloorApplies, the 2025 i4684 Line 11 flip), else $100. The two floors are already the arithmetic of ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor and ../deductibleLossAfterFloor, which subtract them as inline Dollars; nothing named the printed BOX, which is why line 11 had no fact. The selector is the same Boolean those two facts read, so the printed floor and the floor actually subtracted can never disagree. Print only: nothing computed reads it. A Section B event resolves $100 here because the flip Boolean is false for it; the whole of Section A is inapplicable to such an event and its page 1 lines 2 through 9 already print the same way, so this fact inherits that gap rather than adding one, and a part level render gate on page 1 is what fixes both.

Fact.Name: This event's loss after the per event floor (Form 4684 line 12, as printed)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 12 as printed, "Subtract line 11 from line 10. If zero or less, enter -0-", for this event. form4684.xml already computes that subtraction three times, once per destination, and the three gates PARTITION the Section A events with no overlap and no gap: ../deductibleLossAfterFloor takes an eligible event that is not on the 500 dollar path (line 10 less $100), ../qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor takes the 500 dollar path (line 10 less $500), and ../nonDisasterLossAfterFloor takes an event whose ../isEligible is false (line 10 less $100). Exactly one term is nonzero on any Section A event, so their Add is the printed line 12 exactly rather than an approximation. All three are 0 for a Section B event, which is the right print: Section A's floors are personal use rules. Print only: nothing computed reads it.

Fact.Name: This event's line 34 column (a) identification, blank unless the event is long-term Section B (Form 4684 line 34, column (a))
Fact.Description: ../description when ../isLongTermSectionBEvent is true, the empty String otherwise. This is the Form 4684 Section B Part II column (a) cell, "Identify casualty or theft", in the line 34 half. IT IS GATED BECAUSE THE FORM PRINTS TWO HALVES AND AN EVENT BELONGS TO ONE. Line 29 and line 34 are the same four columns under two headings, one year or less and more than one year, and the six AMOUNT cells already carry the sort in themselves: ../shortTermSectionBLossColumnBi and its five siblings each resolve 0 outside their own half. Column (a) is text and cannot say 0, so mapping ../description bare would print the same casualty as both held one year or less and held more than one year on one page. This fact is that missing gate and nothing more; the value it prints is the filer's own description, unchanged. THE SHORT TERM TWIN IS NOT BUILT HERE. Line 29 column (a) is a different printed field, reviewed in another work item of this round; it wants the mirror of this fact, reading a not of the same condition. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, because its condition is.

Fact.Name: Does this event fill the Form 4684 Section B Part I property columns?
Fact.Description: True when the event is a Section B event (../isSectionB, the union of the column (b)(i), column (b)(ii) and Section C arms) AND is not the Section C safe harbor loss whose line 51 says "Do not complete lines 19–27 for this loss". It is the gate ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement (line 26) already applies inline, named once so the lines 19 through 25 print facts read the same test rather than restating it five times. A personal use event resolves false, and every one of those print facts then resolves 0 or empty.

Fact.Name: Section B cost or adjusted basis for this event (Form 4684 line 20, column A)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 20, column A, as printed. /casualtyEvents/*/adjustedBasis restricted to an event that actually completes Section B Part I: /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty, else 0. Section B lines 20, 21, 23, 24 and 25 are Section A lines 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 verbatim, so the measurement is the shared per event fact and only the print gate is new. Print only by design: nothing computed reads it. Section A and Section B of Form 4684 are printed on the same rendered copy today (the register has no part level render gate), so every Section B fact in form4684.xml is gated on /casualtyEvents/*/isSectionB and resolves 0 for a personal use event; this fact keeps that pattern rather than printing a Section A figure under the SECTION B heading.

Fact.Name: Section B decline in fair market value for this event (Form 4684 line 25, column A)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 25, column A, as printed. /casualtyEvents/*/fmvDecrease restricted to an event that actually completes Section B Part I: /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty, else 0. Section B lines 20, 21, 23, 24 and 25 are Section A lines 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 verbatim, so the measurement is the shared per event fact and only the print gate is new. Print only by design: nothing computed reads it. Section A and Section B of Form 4684 are printed on the same rendered copy today (the register has no part level render gate), so every Section B fact in form4684.xml is gated on /casualtyEvents/*/isSectionB and resolves 0 for a personal use event; this fact keeps that pattern rather than printing a Section A figure under the SECTION B heading.

Fact.Name: Section B fair market value after the casualty for this event (Form 4684 line 24, column A)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 24, column A, as printed. /casualtyEvents/*/fmvAfter restricted to an event that actually completes Section B Part I: /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty, else 0. Section B lines 20, 21, 23, 24 and 25 are Section A lines 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 verbatim, so the measurement is the shared per event fact and only the print gate is new. Print only by design: nothing computed reads it. Section A and Section B of Form 4684 are printed on the same rendered copy today (the register has no part level render gate), so every Section B fact in form4684.xml is gated on /casualtyEvents/*/isSectionB and resolves 0 for a personal use event; this fact keeps that pattern rather than printing a Section A figure under the SECTION B heading.

Fact.Name: Section B insurance or other reimbursement for this event (Form 4684 line 21, column A)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 21, column A, as printed. /casualtyEvents/*/reimbursement restricted to an event that actually completes Section B Part I: /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty, else 0. Section B lines 20, 21, 23, 24 and 25 are Section A lines 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 verbatim, so the measurement is the shared per event fact and only the print gate is new. The line prints the reimbursement AS ANSWERED; the later year and declined claim adjustments live in ../reimbursementAmount and are line 22's and line 27's business, exactly as Section A line 3 prints ../reimbursement. Print only by design: nothing computed reads it. Section A and Section B of Form 4684 are printed on the same rendered copy today (the register has no part level render gate), so every Section B fact in form4684.xml is gated on /casualtyEvents/*/isSectionB and resolves 0 for a personal use event; this fact keeps that pattern rather than printing a Section A figure under the SECTION B heading.

Fact.Name: Section B fair market value before the casualty for this event (Form 4684 line 23, column A)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 23, column A, as printed. /casualtyEvents/*/fmvBefore restricted to an event that actually completes Section B Part I: /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty, else 0. Section B lines 20, 21, 23, 24 and 25 are Section A lines 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 verbatim, so the measurement is the shared per event fact and only the print gate is new. Print only by design: nothing computed reads it. Section A and Section B of Form 4684 are printed on the same rendered copy today (the register has no part level render gate), so every Section B fact in form4684.xml is gated on /casualtyEvents/*/isSectionB and resolves 0 for a personal use event; this fact keeps that pattern rather than printing a Section A figure under the SECTION B heading.

Fact.Name: Section B property description for this event (Form 4684 line 19, column A)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 19, column A: "Description of properties (show type, location, and date acquired for each property)", the Section B twin of Section A line 1. It is ../description, the event's own property label, printed only when this event actually completes Section B Part I (../printsSectionBPartIProperty), else the empty String. The gate is the whole point of the fact: ../description alone would print a personal use property's label under the heading "SECTION B—Business and Income-Producing Property" on every return that claims any casualty, which is a false statement on a filed form rather than a harmless zero. Print only by design: nothing computed reads it. Section A and Section B of Form 4684 are printed on the same rendered copy today (the register has no part level render gate), so every Section B fact in form4684.xml is gated on /casualtyEvents/*/isSectionB and resolves 0 for a personal use event; this fact keeps that pattern rather than printing a Section A figure under the SECTION B heading.

Fact.Name: Address of the individual or entity that ran the fraudulent arrangement (Form 4684 Section C, Part II)
Fact.Description: The address the filer writes on the third Form 4684 Section C Part II caption, "Address", for the individual or entity named at ../writablePonziPerpetratorName. Typed String rather than the graph's Address primitive because the caption is one printed rule with no separate city, state or ZIP boxes, and an Address would impose structure the form does not ask for. A FAITHFUL RECORD FIELD - no computation reads its VALUE; the Section C dollar amounts are gated by ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft alone. REQUIRED WHEN ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft IS TRUE, not optional: the printed caption carries no "(if known)" qualifier (contrast ../writablePonziPerpetratorTin, which does), because the safe harbor is granted only to a filer who signs the Part II statements naming who ran the arrangement. THIS FACT ITSELF carries no requiredness logic of its own - the enforcement lives one level up, at /hasPonziIdentityRequiredButMissing (via ../ponziIdentityRequiredButMissing, which reads this writable's completeness, not its value), so a return can never file with the safe harbor attested and this caption blank.

Fact.Name: Name of the individual or entity that ran the fraudulent arrangement (Form 4684 Section C, Part II)
Fact.Description: The name the filer writes on the first Form 4684 Section C Part II caption, "Name of individual or entity", completing the printed declaration "I am claiming a theft loss deduction pursuant to Revenue Procedure 2009-20 from a specified fraudulent arrangement conducted by the following individual or entity." Section C is completed for one Ponzi type theft, which this dictionary models as one /casualtyEvents item, so the intake is per event. A FAITHFUL RECORD FIELD - no computation reads its VALUE. The whole of Section C Part I is already built, from ../writablePonziInitialInvestment through ../ponziDeductibleTheftLoss, and none of those facts identifies WHO ran the arrangement; the DOLLAR amounts stand or fall on ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft, not on this name. REQUIRED WHEN ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft IS TRUE, not optional: the printed caption carries no "(if known)" qualifier (contrast ../writablePonziPerpetratorTin, which does), because the safe harbor is granted only to a filer who signs the Part II statements. THIS FACT ITSELF carries no requiredness logic of its own - the enforcement lives one level up, at /hasPonziIdentityRequiredButMissing (via ../ponziIdentityRequiredButMissing, which reads this writable's completeness, not its value), so a return can never file with the safe harbor attested and this caption blank.

Fact.Name: Taxpayer identification number of the individual or entity that ran the fraudulent arrangement (Form 4684 Section C, Part II)
Fact.Description: The identification number the filer writes on the second Form 4684 Section C Part II caption, "Taxpayer identification number (if known)", for the individual or entity named at ../writablePonziPerpetratorName. TYPED String RATHER THAN TIN OR EIN, and the printed caption is the reason: the declaration covers an arrangement "conducted by the following individual or entity", so the box takes an individual's SSN or ITIN on one return and an entity's EIN on the next, and this graph has no union of the two shapes. A String records either exactly as printed. The parenthetical "if known" is the second reason: a filer who cannot supply the number still signs the statement, and a typed identifier would refuse a blank in a place the form allows one. A FAITHFUL RECORD FIELD that no computation reads. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves the caption blank and changes no tax value.

Fact.Name: This Ponzi safe-harbor event is missing its required perpetrator name or address (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft is true AND either ../writablePonziPerpetratorName or ../writablePonziPerpetratorAddress is unanswered; FALSE otherwise. TIN is deliberately NOT tested here - it alone carries the printed "(if known)" qualifier, so it stays optional. Read only by /hasPonziIdentityRequiredButMissing, the top-level Count that carries the refusal.
COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT: ../isPonziSafeHarborTheft is complete-safe by construction, and Not(IsComplete(...)) on a String writable never itself resolves Incomplete - IsComplete is the one combinator that is always Complete regardless of its operand's state.

Fact.Name: The 500 dollar qualified disaster floor Form 4684 line 11 can print
Fact.Description: A $500 Dollar constant, the second of the two amounts Form 4684 line 11 prints: "Enter $100 ($500 if qualified disaster loss rules apply; see instructions)". The fourteen supported templates select between two values with bool_switch, whose chosen arm must be a fact PATH while only the fallback may be a literal, and no 500 dollar Dollar fact exists in dictionary/manifest/facts-manifest.json. This fact is that path and nothing else: it resolves Complete $500 on every return, depends on nothing, and is read only by /casualtyEvents/*/lineElevenPerEventFloor. The 500 dollar floor itself already lives inside /casualtyEvents/*/qualifiedDisasterLossAfterFloor as an inline Dollar, so this introduces no new tax rule.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 15 as printed, whichever of its two cases the return is in
Fact.Description: The single box Form 4684 line 15 prints carries two different quantities, and form4684.xml holds both: /netPersonalCasualtyGainToScheduleD is the first bullet (line 13 more than line 14: the net personal casualty GAIN, to Schedule D) and /netQualifiedDisasterLoss is the last (line 13 less than line 14 with qualified disaster losses subject to the 500 dollar reduction: the net qualified disaster LOSS, to Schedule A line 16 or the increased standard deduction). They are mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION, not by convention: the first is GreaterOf(line 13 minus line 14, 0) and the second is LesserOf(GreaterOf(line 14 minus line 13, 0), the qualified disaster total), so whichever comparison is false makes that fact 0. Their Add is therefore the printed line 15 in every case, including the equal case both facts print as 0. Print only: nothing computed reads it, and each half keeps its own consumer.

Fact.Name: This event is not in the Form 4684 Section B Part II long term half
Fact.Description: The negation of ../isLongTermSectionBEvent, named because the supported templates have no inline Not inside an All. TRUE on every Section A event as well, which is why it is combined with ../isSectionB at ../isShortTermSectionBEvent rather than read on its own. Read only by that fact.

Fact.Name: This event belongs in the Form 4684 Section B Part II SHORT TERM half (complete safe)
Fact.Description: TRUE when this event is a Section B event that is not in the long term half, so its row is printed under the line 29 heading "Casualty or Theft of Property Held One Year or Less" rather than under line 34's. It is the MIRROR /casualtyEvents/*/isLongTermSectionBEvent asks for in as many words: "THE SHORT TERM TWIN IS NOT BUILT HERE. Line 29 column (a) is a different printed field ... it wants the mirror of this fact, reading a not of the same condition." The ../isSectionB conjunct is what keeps a Section A event out of the Part II table: ../isNotLongTermSectionBEvent alone is true for one. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT, because both conjuncts are.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 46 - the Revenue Procedure 2009-20 safe harbor percentage
Fact.Description: The line 46 multiplier itself: 0.75 when /casualtyEvents/*/ponziHasPotentialThirdPartyRecovery is true, 0.95 otherwise. dictionary/ty2025/form4684.xml folds lines 46 and 47 into /casualtyEvents/*/ponziSafeHarborAmount on purpose, so this fact adds no arithmetic; it names the constant the paper form prints, so the two printed boxes have something to read. The printed value is split across the digit before the decimal point and the digits after it, which the filler takes as the transforms /casualtyEvents/*/ponziSafeHarborRate/~decimalWhole and /casualtyEvents/*/ponziSafeHarborRate/~decimalFraction.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 46 constant - 0.95 with no potential third-party recovery
Fact.Description: The printed 0.95 multiplier of line 46, encoded as a structural Dollar literal (the param ledger treats a rate encoding as structural, not a statutory amount). It is one arm of the line 46 switch and prints nothing by itself.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 46 constant - 0.75 with a potential third-party recovery
Fact.Description: The printed 0.75 multiplier of line 46, encoded as a structural Dollar literal. It is the other arm of the line 46 switch and prints nothing by itself.

Fact.Name: The properties damaged or destroyed in this casualty or theft event
Fact.Description: THE PER PROPERTY COLLECTION that holds Form 4684 property columns A through D. One Form 4684 is one casualty or theft EVENT (the form renders includeForEach /casualtyEvents), and the four property columns inside it are the several properties lost or damaged in THAT event, which dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv declares as "IRS4684 /casualtyEvents/*/properties columns 4". Item [0] is column A and items [1] to [3] are columns B to D; the register prints them there. It carries the INPUT leaves of each column (the description, the basis, the reimbursement and the two fair market values) and the DERIVED per column lines (Section A lines 4 and 7 to 9, Section B lines 22 and 25 to 27), which read the event through relative dependencies (../../../sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear, ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty, ../../../isTotallyDestroyedOrStolen). THE EVENT LEVEL LINES ADD THE COLUMNS when this collection is answered with at least one item (/casualtyEvents/*/propertyColumnsAnswered): line 10 at /casualtyEvents/*/lineTenCasualtyLoss, the line 4 term of line 13 at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionACasualtyGainAmount, line 28 at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyEightMeasure, and the per event gain count /knockoutCasualtyGain reads at /casualtyEvents/*/hasCasualtyGainInAnyColumn. So a casualty that damaged several properties is ONE event with one line 11 floor, as Pub. 547's single event rule requires. When the collection is unanswered or answered empty, the event level leaves (/casualtyEvents/*/adjustedBasis and its siblings) carry the event as a single property, and the register prints nothing in column A. The event level adjustments with no per column intake (the Rev. Proc. 2018-08 and 2010-36 direct entry alternatives, the declined claim and later year reimbursement measures, the section 1033 and section 121 gain adjustments and the Form 4797 Part III recapture) are read only on the event level path. More than four columns print only the first four; the i4684 "additional sheets" for columns E onward are not rendered.

Fact.Name: This property's cost or adjusted basis (Form 4684 line 2 and line 20)
Fact.Description: One property column's cost or other basis, printed on Form 4684 line 2 in Section A and line 20 in Section B. Item [0] of the collection is column A. The event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/adjustedBasis carries the event instead when the collection is unanswered or empty (/casualtyEvents/*/propertyColumnsAnswered false). It prints AS ANSWERED: a writable carries no print gate, and no gated derived twin reading ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty (the shape the derived property cells already use) is built for this leaf, so it prints as answered and is unanswered, therefore blank, on a return that never fills the property columns. The event level lines read it through the column sums, line 10 at /casualtyEvents/*/lineTenCasualtyLoss and line 28 at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyEightMeasure, whenever the collection is answered.

Fact.Name: This property's line 1 and line 19 description (type, location and date acquired)
Fact.Description: One property column's description on Form 4684 line 1 (Section A) and line 19 (Section B): the type of property, its location and the date acquired, as the printed line asks for each property lost or damaged in the same casualty or theft. Item [0] of the collection is column A. The event level /casualtyEvents/*/description, with its Section B gated twin /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPropertyDescription, carries the event instead when the collection is unanswered or empty (/casualtyEvents/*/propertyColumnsAnswered false). It prints AS ANSWERED: a writable carries no print gate, and no gated derived twin reading ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty (the shape the derived property cells already use) is built for this leaf, so it prints as answered and is unanswered, therefore blank, on a return that never fills the property columns.

Fact.Name: This property's fair market value after the casualty or theft (Form 4684 line 6 and line 24)
Fact.Description: One property column's fair market value after the casualty or theft, printed on Form 4684 line 6 in Section A and line 24 in Section B. Item [0] of the collection is column A. The event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/fmvAfter carries the event instead when the collection is unanswered or empty (/casualtyEvents/*/propertyColumnsAnswered false). It prints AS ANSWERED: a writable carries no print gate, and no gated derived twin reading ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty (the shape the derived property cells already use) is built for this leaf, so it prints as answered and is unanswered, therefore blank, on a return that never fills the property columns. The event level lines read it through the column sums, line 10 at /casualtyEvents/*/lineTenCasualtyLoss and line 28 at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyEightMeasure, whenever the collection is answered.

Fact.Name: This property's fair market value before the casualty or theft (Form 4684 line 5 and line 23)
Fact.Description: One property column's fair market value before the casualty or theft, printed on Form 4684 line 5 in Section A and line 23 in Section B. Item [0] of the collection is column A. The event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/fmvBefore carries the event instead when the collection is unanswered or empty (/casualtyEvents/*/propertyColumnsAnswered false). It prints AS ANSWERED: a writable carries no print gate, and no gated derived twin reading ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty (the shape the derived property cells already use) is built for this leaf, so it prints as answered and is unanswered, therefore blank, on a return that never fills the property columns. The event level lines read it through the column sums, line 10 at /casualtyEvents/*/lineTenCasualtyLoss and line 28 at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyEightMeasure, whenever the collection is answered.

Fact.Name: This property's insurance or other reimbursement (Form 4684 line 3 and line 21)
Fact.Description: One property column's insurance or other reimbursement, whether or not a claim was filed, printed on Form 4684 line 3 in Section A and line 21 in Section B. Item [0] of the collection is column A. The event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/reimbursement carries the event instead when the collection is unanswered or empty (/casualtyEvents/*/propertyColumnsAnswered false); the later year and declined claim adjustments stay on the event and are read only on the event level path. It prints AS ANSWERED: a writable carries no print gate, and no gated derived twin reading ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty (the shape the derived property cells already use) is built for this leaf, so it prints as answered and is unanswered, therefore blank, on a return that never fills the property columns. The event level lines read it through the column sums, line 10 at /casualtyEvents/*/lineTenCasualtyLoss and line 28 at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyEightMeasure, whenever the collection is answered.

Fact.Name: This event's line 29 column (a) identification, blank unless the event is short term Section B (Form 4684 line 29, column (a))
Fact.Description: ../description when ../isShortTermSectionBEvent is true, the empty String otherwise. This is the Form 4684 Section B Part II column (a) cell, "Identify casualty or theft", in the line 29 half, and it is the twin /casualtyEvents/*/longTermSectionBDescription names as unbuilt. IT IS GATED FOR THE SAME REASON: line 29 and line 34 are the same four columns under two headings and the six amount cells carry the sort in themselves by resolving 0 outside their own half, but column (a) is text and cannot say 0, so an ungated ../description would print the same casualty as both held one year or less and held more than one year on one page. COMPLETE ON EVERY EVENT.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 1 - date the casualty or theft property was acquired
Fact.Description: The Date Acquired column of the line 1 property table. The graph carries the holding period as the attestation /casualtyEvents/*/writablePropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear, not as a date, so the printed date is its own intake. Typed Day, which the writable template now supports, rather than a String stand-in.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 Section C Part II - tax years and filing dates of the prior returns
Fact.Description: The free text box under the Revenue Procedure 2009-20 declaration: the tax year or years for which the investor filed a return or amended return that does not satisfy the conditions in section 6.02, and the dates on which they were filed. It is a declaration statement, not an amount, and nothing in the graph derives it, so it is an intake typed String rather than Day (the box takes several years and dates at once).

Fact.Name: This property's decline in fair market value (Form 4684 line 7 and line 25 measure)
Fact.Description: The greater of ../fmvDecreaseBeforeFloor and zero: one property column's decline in fair market value, Form 4684 line 7 in Section A and line 25 in Section B. The floor mirrors the event level /casualtyEvents/*/fmvDecrease, which the event level path prints through /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyFiveFmvDecrease; without it a property whose value ROSE would print a negative decline in its column and would feed a negative into the line 26 smaller of rule. This is the measure, not the printed Section B cell: the gated cell is ../sectionBLineTwentyFivePropertyFmvDecrease.

Fact.Name: This property's raw decline in fair market value (Form 4684 line 7 and line 25, before the floor)
Fact.Description: ../writableFmvBefore minus ../writableFmvAfter for ONE property column, the literal subtraction Form 4684 line 7 (Section A) and line 25 (Section B) print. It is the unfloored intermediate only; the printed measure is ../fmvDecrease, which floors it at 0 exactly as the event level /casualtyEvents/*/fmvDecrease does. Nothing prints this fact.

Fact.Name: Is this property column a casualty or theft gain? (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../hasSectionBGain when it is Complete, else FALSE. ../hasSectionBGain is the line 22 test, reimbursement greater than basis for ONE column, and it is also Section A's line 4 test ("If line 3 is more than line 2"), the same comparison on the same two leaves, so one fact serves both sections. This restatement is what the line 9 and line 27 gain arms and the event's ../../../hasCasualtyGainInAnyColumn read, so a column whose basis or reimbursement is still unanswered is not a gain and does not make the event level knockout count Incomplete; that column's own line 9 stays Incomplete until it is answered.

Fact.Name: Is this property column a Form 4684 line 22 gain?
Fact.Description: The line 22 test as the form states it: "If line 21 is more than line 20", that is ../writableReimbursement greater than ../writableAdjustedBasis for ONE property column; it is also Section A line 4's test. Read by ../printsSectionBGain, ../sectionALineFourGain and the complete-safe ../hasGainColumnCompleteSafe.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 9 for one property column (Section A columns A to D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION A line 9 for ONE property column of this casualty or theft event: 0 when the event's /casualtyEvents/*/sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear is true, because the loss belongs to another tax year (it was deducted on an earlier year's return, or the IRC 165(i) election put it on the preceding year's return), otherwise ../lossAfterReimbursementBeforeSuspension. The suppression mirrors the event level /casualtyEvents/*/lossAfterReimbursement, so a suspended event prints a Complete 0 in every column. Line 10 ("Casualty or theft loss. Add the amounts on line 9 in columns A through D") adds this cell over every answered column at /casualtyEvents/*/lineTenCasualtyLoss; item [0] is column A.

Fact.Name: This property's Form 4684 line 9 subtraction, before the zero floor
Fact.Description: ../lossBeforeReimbursement minus the nonnegative ../writableReimbursement for ONE property column: the raw subtraction of Form 4684 SECTION A line 9, "Subtract line 3 from line 8". It may go negative when the reimbursement exceeds the loss, which the floor at ../lossAfterReimbursement removes; a malformed negative reimbursement seed is floored at $0 before this subtraction. Nothing prints this fact.

Fact.Name: This property's Form 4684 line 9 loss, floored at zero
Fact.Description: The greater of ../lossAfterReimbursementBeforeFloor and zero: Form 4684 SECTION A line 9 for ONE property column, "If zero or less, enter 0". A GAIN column (../hasGainColumnCompleteSafe) resolves 0 without reading the fair market values, because line 4 tells the filer to "skip lines 5 through 9 for that column"; the floor gives the same 0 whenever the values are answered, so the arm changes completeness only, which is what lets line 10 add a gain column as nothing. The suspension arm the event level /casualtyEvents/*/lossAfterReimbursement applies sits above it, at ../lossAfterReimbursement.

Fact.Name: This property's loss before reimbursement (Form 4684 line 8, and the line 26 smaller of arm)
Fact.Description: The smaller of ../writableAdjustedBasis and ../fmvDecrease for ONE property column. It is Form 4684 SECTION A line 8, "Enter the smaller of line 2 or line 7", verbatim, and it is also the ordinary arm of SECTION B line 26, "Enter the smaller of line 20 or line 25" - the two sections print the same rule over the same two operands, so one fact serves both and the line 26 Note is applied above it at ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursementMeasure. The event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/lossBeforeReimbursement carries the event when the collection is unanswered or empty.

Fact.Name: Does this property column print a Form 4684 line 22 gain?
Fact.Description: ../hasSectionBGain AND the event's /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty. One conjunct is the line 22 test itself and the other is the Section B Part I print gate, folded together so the printed cell needs a single two arm switch. A personal use event, and a Section C safe harbor theft whose line 51 says not to complete lines 19 through 27, both resolve false here.

Fact.Name: This property's Form 4684 line 27 subtraction, before the zero floor
Fact.Description: ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursementMeasure minus the nonnegative ../writableReimbursement for ONE property column: the raw subtraction of Form 4684 SECTION B line 27, "Subtract line 21 from line 26". It may go negative when the reimbursement exceeds the loss, which the floor at ../sectionBCasualtyLossMeasure removes; a malformed negative reimbursement seed is floored at $0 before this subtraction. Nothing prints this fact.

Fact.Name: This property's Form 4684 line 27 casualty or theft loss, floored at zero
Fact.Description: The greater of ../sectionBCasualtyLossBeforeFloor and zero: Form 4684 SECTION B line 27 for ONE property column, "If zero or less, enter 0". A GAIN column (../hasGainColumnCompleteSafe) resolves 0 without reading the fair market values, because line 22 tells the filer to "skip lines 23 through 27 for that column"; the floor gives the same 0 whenever the values are answered. This is the measure; the printed cell is the gated ../sectionBLineTwentySevenCasualtyLoss. The floor is also what makes the form's "skip lines 23 through 27 for that column" instruction on a GAIN column come out right without a separate arm: when the reimbursement exceeds the basis the subtraction is negative and this resolves 0, exactly as the event level /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBCasualtyLoss does.

Fact.Name: This property column's Form 4684 line 22 difference (line 21 minus line 20)
Fact.Description: ../writableReimbursement minus ../writableAdjustedBasis for ONE property column: "enter the difference" of Form 4684 SECTION B line 22. It is meaningful only when ../hasSectionBGain is true, which is why the printed cell ../sectionBLineTwentyTwoGain selects it through ../printsSectionBGain rather than reading it directly. Nothing prints this fact.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 25 for one property column (columns A to D)
