Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 25, "Subtract line 24 from line 23", for ONE property column of this casualty or theft event: ../fmvDecrease when the event actually completes Section B Part I, else 0. The Section B print gate is the event's /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty, read from inside the nested property item as ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty, so a personal use event and a Section C safe harbor theft both resolve a Complete 0 in every property column instead of printing Section A figures under the SECTION B heading. That is the same gate column A applies at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyFiveFmvDecrease and its siblings. Column A prints the event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyFiveFmvDecrease and is untouched. Print only by design: nothing computed reads it.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 27 for one property column (columns A to D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 27 for ONE property column of this casualty or theft event: ../sectionBCasualtyLossMeasure when the event actually completes Section B Part I, else 0; on a home used for a Schedule C business (/casualtyEvents/*/homeUsedForScheduleCBusiness, one column, the refusal /knockoutCasualtyPropertyColumnsNotCarried fencing more) it is the event's line 27 figure /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBCasualtyLoss, the deductible loss from Form 8829 line 35 that i4684 says to enter on line 27. The Section B print gate is the event's /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty, read from inside the nested property item as ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty, so a personal use event and a Section C safe harbor theft both resolve a Complete 0 in every property column instead of printing Section A figures under the SECTION B heading. That is the same gate column A applies at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyFiveFmvDecrease and its siblings. Item [0] is column A. Line 28 ("Casualty or theft loss. Add the amounts on line 27") adds the ungated measure ../sectionBCasualtyLossMeasure over every answered column at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyEightMeasure, and /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBCasualtyLoss applies the event level overrides above that sum. [A LEADING SUSPENSION CASE SITS ABOVE THE PRINT GATE, resolving 0 when the event's /casualtyEvents/*/sectionALossSuspendedToAnotherYear is true, because the loss belongs to another tax year. It is the Section B twin of /casualtyEvents/*/properties/*/lossAfterReimbursement's own leading Case and it exists for the reason that fact states in terms: without it the columns would print a line 27 loss on the same printed row where the event's line 28 is a Complete 0. Line 26 is deliberately NOT suspended on either side - /casualtyEvents/*/properties/*/sectionBLineTwentySixLossBeforeReimbursement and the event level /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement both still print the measured loss, exactly as Section A's line 8 does, so the suppression appears once on the printed page and at the same line on both sides.]

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 26 for one property column (columns A to D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 26 for ONE property column of this casualty or theft event: ../sectionBLossBeforeReimbursementMeasure when the event actually completes Section B Part I, else 0. The Section B print gate is the event's /casualtyEvents/*/printsSectionBPartIProperty, read from inside the nested property item as ../../../printsSectionBPartIProperty, so a personal use event and a Section C safe harbor theft both resolve a Complete 0 in every property column instead of printing Section A figures under the SECTION B heading. That is the same gate column A applies at /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLineTwentyFiveFmvDecrease and its siblings. Column A prints the event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement and is untouched. Print only by design: nothing computed reads it.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 line 22 for one property column (columns A to D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 22 for ONE property column of this casualty or theft event: the difference ../sectionBGainAmountBeforeGate when ../printsSectionBGain is true, else 0, which is the printed line read literally. It is DELIBERATELY the plain form arithmetic and not a per property copy of /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBCasualtyGainAmount: the recognition adjustments that fact applies (the section 1033 postponement, the section 121 exclusion, the later year and declined claim reimbursement measures and the Part III recapture route) are all EVENT level, have no per property intake, and stay where they are. Item [0] is column A. The event level /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBCasualtyGainAmount is not a sum of these cells; a gain in any column is refused through /casualtyEvents/*/hasCasualtyGainInAnyColumn and /knockoutCasualtyGain.

Fact.Name: This property's Form 4684 line 26 measure, including the line 26 Note
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION B line 26 for ONE property column BEFORE the print gate: ../writableAdjustedBasis outright when the event's /casualtyEvents/*/isTotallyDestroyedOrStolen is true, which is the line 26 Note, "If the property was totally destroyed by casualty or lost from theft, enter on line 26 the amount from line 20"; otherwise ../lossBeforeReimbursement, the ordinary smaller of rule. The Note is the ONE place Section A line 8 and Section B line 26 differ, which is why this fact sits above ../lossBeforeReimbursement rather than replacing it, and it mirrors /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBLossBeforeReimbursement. The Note arm never reads ../fmvDecrease, so a totally destroyed property with no answered fair market value still resolves. APPROXIMATION NAMED: the totally destroyed attestation is an EVENT level intake (/casualtyEvents/*/writableTotallyDestroyedOrStolen), so on a multi property event it applies the Note to every property column alike; a per property attestation would be a module design change, and column A already reads the same event level flag.

Fact.Name: The zero dollar floor and blank cell value of the Form 4684 property columns
Fact.Description: A structural $0 Dollar constant. The property column chain needs a Dollar FACT for three jobs the templates cannot express as an inline literal: the floor of Form 4684 line 9 and line 27 (both printed as "If zero or less, enter 0"), and the value a property column prints when the event does not complete Section B Part I. form4684.xml had no zero dollar literal fact of its own, so this is it. It prints nothing by itself; the precedent is /form5329ZeroFloorAmount and /form4972ZeroDollarFloor.

Fact.Name: Were the Section D valuation intakes answered? (basis, FMV before, FMV after)
Fact.Description: Answered-ness predicate for the Section D elected loss. True only when all three of the valuation intakes the IRC 165(i) election needs are answered: /writableForm4684SectionDAdjustedBasis (the line 2 quantity for the elected event), /writableForm4684SectionDFmvBefore (line 5) and /writableForm4684SectionDFmvAfter (line 6). It is the REAL "was the source answered" predicate that brief rule 3 requires behind a derived fact that replaces a filer-typed attestation, so it reads the raw Writables through IsComplete and never a complete-safe wrapper (an IsComplete on a complete-safe fact is always true and would gate nothing). Reimbursement is deliberately NOT part of it: a blank line 3 means no reimbursement, not an unanswered event, and it enters the chain through /form4684SectionDReimbursementOrZero instead. Complete on every return, false on the ~all that never open Section D.

Fact.Name: Section D reimbursement, or 0 when the line 3 box is blank
Fact.Description: Complete-safe wrapper over /writableForm4684SectionDReimbursement. A blank Form 4684 line 3 for the elected event means no insurance or other reimbursement was received or expected, so this resolves Complete $0 and the elected loss stays Complete on a return that answers the valuation boxes and leaves reimbursement empty. Same shape as the module's other OrZero wrappers.

Fact.Name: Section D fair market value after, floored at zero
Fact.Description: Complete-only nonnegative reading of /writableForm4684SectionDFmvAfter. The writable declares a minimum of zero, but that declaration is not enforced while resolving dependent facts; the printed line-7 subtraction must not let a negative persisted value inflate the fair-market-value decline. Unanswered valuation stays unanswered so the Section D gate retains its existing behavior.

Fact.Name: Decline in fair market value of the elected event (Form 4684 line 7, Section D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 7 for the IRC 165(i) elected event = line 5 minus line 6 (/writableForm4684SectionDFmvBefore minus /form4684SectionDFmvAfterAtLeastZero), floored at 0. Mirrors /casualtyEvents/*/fmvDecrease body for body: Section D carries no dollar box of its own on the printed page, but IRC 165(i)(2) deems the casualty to have occurred in the year the deduction is claimed, so the elected loss is measured by exactly the same lines 5-9 arithmetic this return applies to its own events. Gated on /form4684SectionDValuationAnswered so it resolves Complete $0 on every return that never opens Section D.

Fact.Name: Elected event loss before reimbursement (Form 4684 line 8, Section D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 line 8 for the IRC 165(i) elected event = the smaller of line 2 (/writableForm4684SectionDAdjustedBasis) or line 7 (/form4684SectionDFmvDecrease), the same lesser-of-basis-or-decline the per-event /casualtyEvents/*/lossBeforeReimbursement applies. Gated on /form4684SectionDValuationAnswered so it is Complete $0 when Section D was never opened.

Fact.Name: Loss elected onto this return under section 165(i) (Form 4684 line 9, Section D)
Fact.Description:
THE ONE QUANTITY THE SECTION D ELECTION IS WORTH, computed instead of attested. Form 4684 line 9 for the elected event = line 8 (/form4684SectionDLossBeforeReimbursement) minus line 3 (/form4684SectionDReimbursementOrZero), floored at 0; because one property is modelled for the election it is also its line 10. Before this fact the filer was asked for BOTH the inputs and the answer: /writableForm4684SectionDAdjustedBasis, /writableForm4684SectionDFmvBefore, /writableForm4684SectionDFmvAfter and /writableForm4684SectionDReimbursement had no consumer at all, while /writableForm4684SectionDElectedLossAmount carried the number and could contradict them.
THE ATTESTATION IS KEPT AS THE FALLBACK, not deleted (brief rule 3). The second Switch arm reads /writableForm4684SectionDElectedLossAmount whenever the valuation boxes were NOT answered but the amount was, behind IsComplete on the raw Writable itself - a real "was the source answered" predicate, never IsComplete on a complete-safe fact. So a filer who knows only the elected figure still gets the deduction, and a filer who supplies the valuation boxes gets a figure that cannot disagree with them. The fallback amount is the line 9 quantity, i.e. BEFORE the 100-dollar floor, which /form4684SectionDLossAfterFloor applies.
IRC 165(i)(3) caps the elected amount at "the uncompensated amount determined on the basis of the facts existing at the date the taxpayer claims the loss", which is exactly line 8 minus line 3, so the computed arm is the statutory ceiling as well as the printed arithmetic. Complete $0 on every return that opens neither Section D box.

Fact.Name: Elected section 165(i) loss after the 100-dollar floor (Form 4684 lines 11-12, Section D)
Fact.Description:
Form 4684 line 12 for the IRC 165(i) elected event = /form4684SectionDElectedLoss minus the 100-dollar-per-casualty floor, if zero or less 0. It is the term that routes the election into this return's deduction: it is added to /disasterCasualtyLossAfterFloors (2025 i4684 Worksheet 1-1 line 2, "Add the amounts from line 12 of all Forms 4684 reporting losses attributable to a federally declared disaster"), so it reaches Form 4684 line 14, the line 15 comparison, line 16 and /casualtyLossDeduction on Schedule A line 15 by the ordinary route. The elected loss is attributable to a federally declared disaster by the definition of the election itself, so worksheet line 2 is its row.
THE ORDINARY 100-DOLLAR FLOOR, NOT THE 500-DOLLAR QUALIFIED-DISASTER ONE. The 500-dollar floor and the increased-standard-deduction path require a QUALIFIED disaster loss attestation, which Section D has no intake for; every Section D box is about a federally declared disaster, and "federally declared" is a strictly wider class than "qualified" (/casualtyEvents/*/isQualifiedDisasterLoss is its own separate answer). So the elected loss takes the Schedule A line-15 path, which is also the direction that cannot double-deduct.
NOTHING MOVES ON A RETURN THAT NEVER OPENS SECTION D: /form4684SectionDElectedLoss is Complete $0 there, and GreaterOf(0 minus 100, 0) is 0, so /disasterCasualtyLossAfterFloors keeps the value it had.

Fact.Name: Adjusted basis of the property lost in the following year disaster (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. The cost or other adjusted basis of the property destroyed in the following year disaster, the Form 4684 line 2 quantity for the elected event. Unprinted on Section D and authored for the carry back model the project owner commissioned. Nonnegative, as /casualtyEvents/*/adjustedBasis is.

Fact.Name: Name or description of the federally declared disaster elected into this year (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. Form 4684 line 52, printed "Provide the name or a description of the federally declared disaster". Free text supplied by the filer; nothing in this dictionary holds a following year disaster.

Fact.Name: Amount of the following year disaster loss elected into this return (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. The loss the filer elects onto THIS return under IRC 165(i), the figure the election is worth. It is the one quantity that would change this return's tax. CONSUMED as the FALLBACK rather than the primary: /form4684SectionDElectedLoss computes the same figure from the four valuation intakes (line 5 minus line 6, capped at line 2, less line 3) and reads this attestation only when /form4684SectionDValuationAnswered is false, i.e. when the filer gave the answer without the inputs. From there /form4684SectionDLossAfterFloor applies the 100-dollar floor and the amount joins /disasterCasualtyLossAfterFloors, so it reaches Form 4684 line 14, line 16 and /casualtyLossDeduction on Schedule A line 15 - the route the sentence this replaces recorded as owed ("print only until /casualtyLossDeduction consumes it: IRC 165(i)(2) deems the casualty to have occurred in the year the deduction is claimed, so the amount belongs in this year's Section A chain, and nothing routes it there yet"). THE QUANTITY IS THE LINE 9 FIGURE, before the 100-dollar floor: enter the uncompensated loss, not the deduction. Nonnegative. DISPOSITION keep-fallback: retirement was evaluated and DECLINED, because the computed arm is not total. /form4684SectionDElectedLoss computes the figure only when /form4684SectionDValuationAnswered is true, and a filer who elects a following year disaster loss under IRC 165(i) on the strength of an appraisal or an adjuster's statement, without typing the basis and fair market value boxes, leaves this attestation as the only source of the elected amount and of the whole Section A deduction it feeds.

Fact.Name: FEMA disaster declaration number of the following year disaster elected into this year (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. The FEMA DR or EM declaration number of the disaster named on line 52. It is not a printed Section D box: Form 4684 prints the declaration number on page 1 for THIS year's events (/casualtyEvents/*/writableFemaDrDeclarationNumber), and the carry back model needs the same identifier for the following year's disaster. Authored because the owner's decision names it as part of the carry back intake set; it prints nowhere until the cross year model lands.

Fact.Name: Fair market value after the following year disaster (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. The fair market value of the property after the following year casualty, the Form 4684 line 6 quantity for the elected event. Unprinted on Section D and authored for the carry back model.

Fact.Name: Fair market value before the following year disaster (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. The fair market value of the property before the following year casualty, the Form 4684 line 5 quantity for the elected event. Paired with /writableForm4684SectionDFmvAfter, it gives the decline in value that IRC 165 measures the loss by. Unprinted on Section D and authored for the carry back model.

Fact.Name: Date of the loss attributable to the federally declared disaster elected into this year (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. Form 4684 line 53, printed "Provide the date or dates (mm/dd/yyyy) of the loss or losses attributable to the federally declared disaster". Typed Day rather than String so the date is a date. One date is modelled; the printed line's second entry line is an overflow for a loss spanning several dates and stays unmapped.

Fact.Name: Street address of the damaged or destroyed property, carry back election (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. Form 4684 line 54, first entry line: the street address where the damaged or destroyed property was located at the time of the disaster. The line asks for the whole address across two entry lines, so the street half is here and the city, county, state and ZIP half is /writableForm4684SectionDPropertyCityStateZip, the same split the Section A line 1 intakes already use.

Fact.Name: City or town, county or parish, state and ZIP of the damaged property, carry back election (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. Form 4684 line 54, second entry line: the city or town, county or parish, state and ZIP code the printed line asks for by name, completing the address begun in /writableForm4684SectionDPropertyAddress.

Fact.Name: Insurance or other reimbursement for the following year disaster loss (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Section D is the IRC 165(i) election statement: a loss attributable to a federally declared disaster and sustained in the FOLLOWING taxable year, elected back into this one, so that this return deducts it. It carries no dollar amount of its own on the printed page. The insurance or other reimbursement the filer received or expects for the elected event, the Form 4684 line 3 quantity. Unprinted on Section D and authored for the carry back model. Nonnegative, as /casualtyEvents/*/reimbursement is.

Fact.Name: Name or description of the federally declared disaster whose election is being revoked (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART II, THE REVOCATION. Part II revokes a prior IRC 165(i) election and rides an AMENDED preceding year return, so nothing computes from it on this return; it is a statement the filer supplies. Form 4684 line 55, first entry line: the name or description of the federally declared disaster for which the election now being revoked was claimed.

Fact.Name: Date the prior section 165(i) election being revoked was filed (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART II, THE REVOCATION. Part II revokes a prior IRC 165(i) election and rides an AMENDED preceding year return, so nothing computes from it on this return; it is a statement the filer supplies. Form 4684 line 56, printed "Specify the date (mm/dd/yyyy) you filed the prior election, which you are now revoking". Typed Day rather than String so the date is a date. This dictionary holds no filing date of its own, so the filer supplies it.

Fact.Name: Address of the property for which the revoked election was claimed (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART II, THE REVOCATION. Part II revokes a prior IRC 165(i) election and rides an AMENDED preceding year return, so nothing computes from it on this return; it is a statement the filer supplies. Form 4684 line 55, second entry line: the address of the property that was damaged or destroyed and for which the election was claimed. The printed line asks for the disaster AND the address across two entry lines, so the address half is its own intake.

Fact.Name: Evidence or explanation of the repayment arrangement for the revoked election (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART II, THE REVOCATION. Part II revokes a prior IRC 165(i) election and rides an AMENDED preceding year return, so nothing computes from it on this return; it is a statement the filer supplies. Form 4684 line 57, first entry line: the evidence for, or explanation of, the filer's arrangements to repay any credit or refund received because of the election now being revoked. Free text; the second entry line is an overflow of the same explanation and stays unmapped.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 SECTION A line 4 for one property column (columns A to D)
Fact.Description: Form 4684 SECTION A line 4 for ONE property column of this casualty or theft event: ../sectionBGainAmountBeforeGate when ../hasSectionBGain is true, else zero, which is the printed line read literally. NOTHING IS RE DUPLICATED. The line 4 test the form states, "If line 3 is more than line 2", is the same GreaterThan over the same two property leaves that ../hasSectionBGain already carries for line 22 ("If line 21 is more than line 20"), and the difference is the same Subtract that ../sectionBGainAmountBeforeGate already carries, so this cell REUSES both rather than re authoring them; the event level /casualtyEvents/*/casualtyGainAmount makes the same statement, that Section A line 4 and Section B line 22 are one printed subtraction. IT IS NOT ../sectionBLineTwentyTwoGain: that cell is gated on ../printsSectionBGain, which folds in the Section B Part I print gate, so it resolves zero for a personal use event whose Section A line 4 still has to print. The recognition adjustments the event level fact applies, the section 1033 postponement, the section 121 exclusion, the later year and declined claim reimbursement measures, are all EVENT level, have no per property intake, and stay where they are. Item [0] is column A. Line 13 ("Add the amounts on line 4 of all Forms 4684") takes the sum of this cell over every answered column through /casualtyEvents/*/sectionACasualtyGainAmount, and a gain in any column is refused through /casualtyEvents/*/hasCasualtyGainInAnyColumn and /knockoutCasualtyGain.

Fact.Name: This property's city and state (Form 4684 line 1)
Fact.Description: One property column's city and state on Form 4684 line 1, the second column of the line 1 description table, for property rows A to D. Item [0] of the collection is the Property A row; the event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/writableLine1PropertyCityAndState is the event level path's own entry. A faithful record field that plays no part in any computation; unanswered leaves the cell blank and changes no tax value.

Fact.Name: This property's date acquired (Form 4684 line 1)
Fact.Description: One property column's Date Acquired cell on Form 4684 line 1, for property rows A to D. Item [0] of the collection is the Property A row; the event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/writableLine1PropertyDateAcquired is the event level path's own entry. The graph carries the holding period as the attestation /casualtyEvents/*/writablePropertyHeldMoreThanOneYear, not as a date, so the printed date is its own intake. Typed Day rather than a String stand in.

Fact.Name: This property's ZIP code (Form 4684 line 1)
Fact.Description: One property column's ZIP code on Form 4684 line 1, the third column of the line 1 description table, for property rows A to D. Item [0] of the collection is the Property A row; the event level twin /casualtyEvents/*/writableLine1PropertyZipCode is the event level path's own entry and which the line 1 instruction singles out for the FEMA disaster declaration. Typed String rather than a postal primitive because the graph has no ZIP type. A faithful record field that no computation reads; deductibility is gated by /casualtyEvents/*/federallyDeclaredDisaster.

Fact.Name: Second entry line of the Section D disaster name or description (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Form 4684 line 52 prints TWO entry lines for "Provide the name or a description of the federally declared disaster"; /writableForm4684SectionDDisasterName is the first and this is the second. Free text supplied by the filer, carrying no dollar amount and read by no computation, exactly like its first line twin. The register's own convention on this page is one fact per entry line: line 54's two entry lines are /writableForm4684SectionDPropertyAddress and /writableForm4684SectionDPropertyCityStateZip, and line 55's are /writableForm4684SectionDRevocationDisasterName and /writableForm4684SectionDRevocationPropertyAddress.

Fact.Name: Second entry line of the repayment arrangement for the revoked election (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART II, THE REVOCATION. Part II revokes a prior IRC 165(i) election and rides an AMENDED preceding year return, so nothing computes from it on this return; it is a statement the filer supplies. Form 4684 line 57 prints TWO entry lines for the evidence for, or explanation of, the filer's arrangements to repay any credit or refund received because of the election now being revoked; /writableForm4684SectionDRevocationRepaymentArrangement is the first and this is the second. Free text, like its first line twin.

Fact.Name: Second date of the loss attributable to the federally declared disaster (writable)
Fact.Description: SECTION D, PART I, THE CARRY BACK DIRECTION. Form 4684 line 53 asks for the "date or dates" of the loss or losses and prints two entry lines; /writableForm4684SectionDLossDate is the first date and this is the second, for a disaster whose losses were sustained on more than one day. Typed Day rather than String so the date is a date, matching its first line twin. It carries no dollar amount and no computation reads it; the election itself is /casualtyEvents/*/electsSection165iPrecedingYearDeduction.

Fact.Name: This event's property columns cannot be carried (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: True when (1) the event answers its property columns and takes a direct-entry method: the Rev. Proc. 2018-08 safe harbor (../usedFmvSafeHarborMethod) or the Rev. Proc. 2010-36 corrosive drywall procedure (../usedCorrosiveDrywallProcedure), whose figure the instructions enter for each property and the columns do not ask; (2) the event answers more than four property columns, the four the form prints; or (3) the event is a home used for a Schedule C business (../homeUsedForScheduleCBusiness) and answers more than one property column, so the Form 8829 line 35 figure that line 27 carries has no single column. False otherwise, including every event that answers no property columns. Read by /knockoutCasualtyPropertyColumnsNotCarried.

Fact.Name: Form 4684 property columns the return cannot carry
Fact.Description: A casualty or theft you entered cannot be filed here because of how its properties were entered. One of these applies: you used the Revenue Procedure 2018-08 safe harbor or the Revenue Procedure 2010-36 corrosive drywall procedure for an event whose properties you entered one by one (the safe harbor or repair figure is entered for each property, and this return does not ask for it property by property yet); you entered more than four properties for one event (the form prints four columns); or you entered more than one property for a home used in your Schedule C business (its Form 8829 line 35 loss is entered on line 27 of a single column).

Fact.Name: A Schedule C home casualty not attested as outside a federally declared disaster (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: True when this event is a home used for a Schedule C business (../homeUsedForScheduleCBusiness) and ../federallyDeclaredDisaster is not answered no. Form 8829 line 9 takes the federally declared disaster share of such a loss outside the income limit, which this return does not build. Read by form8829:/knockoutForm8829HomeCasualtyNotCarried.
